subject: CIQA kickoff - perceptual compression labels as a product asset
body:
Team,

Kicking off CIQA formally. The open-source release gives us pairwise forced-choice human ratings over AVA images recompressed at two random JPEG quality factors, and I want to turn that into the canonical training signal for our perceptual compression metric. The product hook: media customers keep asking how far they can push bitrate before users notice, and NIMA-style aesthetic scores don't answer that.

Rough milestones inside our window: label pipeline reproducible by mid-March, second rater wave in May, launch review before June 1. Note the sampling constraint from the original study - only AVA images at JPEG quality factor 99 or above are usable as near-lossless sources, so the pool is a subset of the ~255k AVA images, not the whole thing.

Jelena will follow up on staffing and compute. Please flag conflicts with other commitments this week, not in April.

Thanks,
Lucia

subject: Re: CIQA kickoff - perceptual compression labels as a product asset
body:
Lucia,

Staffing plan, confirmed with everyone individually:

- Milan Zapata 50% through the window, owns the compression/sampling pipeline (ImageMagick sampling of Q>=99 sources, tf.image.adjust_jpeg_quality for recompression).
- Leilani Nakamura 40%, rater-study tooling.
- Saoirse Eriksen 30%, data validation and release packaging.
- Gustavo Moreau is locked in at 60% on CIQA for all of May 2026 to run the second rater wave and the label QA pass. I sized May around him, so please don't let anyone shave that down.

Compute is light - a few hundred A100-hours on titan-a100, best effort is fine. The real budget line is the rater panel: I'm estimating 38k pairwise judgments at roughly $0.14 each, so ~$5.3k. No Vulcan ask.

One dependency: Corpus ingestion for the label tables, but nothing that touches the v2 migration.

Jelena

subject: CIQA status: sampling pipeline done, one distribution risk
body:
Hi both,

Status: the sampling pipeline is reproducible end to end. We filter AVA to sources with JPEG quality factor >= 99 and recompress each at two random quality factors, matching the original study. Good news is the semantic balance holds - the eight classes (animal, architecture, cityscape, floral, food/drink, landscape, portrait, still life) each land at roughly 6.25% after sampling, so no reweighting needed.

The risk: the near-lossless filter is stricter than I expected and our usable pool came out at ~41k images. If Lucia wants per-class metric confidence intervals under +/-2%, the May rater wave needs to cover more pairs per image than we budgeted - I estimate 15-20% more judgments. Options: eat the cost, or drop the two weakest classes from the launch claim.

Also flagging that rater tooling had a two week slip, Leilani has it back on track.

Milan

subject: Re: CIQA status: sampling pipeline done, one distribution risk
body:
Milan, Jelena,

Decision on the coverage question: we eat the cost. I got the rater budget bumped to $6.4k, which covers the extra judgments across all eight semantic classes - dropping classes would undercut the whole "distribution-preserving" story we tell in the launch narrative. The second rater wave is running now and Gustavo reports inter-rater agreement at 0.71 Krippendorff's alpha on the first 9k pairs, which is above our 0.65 bar.

I've asked Nadia to slot us for the Launch Review Board on May 28. Materials owed: dataset card, rater methodology note, and the compression-metric demo. Saoirse owns release packaging; Jelena, please confirm she has what she needs by May 20.

If agreement drops below 0.65 on the full wave we hold the release and re-run the flagged batches - that is the only remaining go/no-go item.

Lucia

subject: COSTAR kickoff: counterfactual forecasting for the platform
body:
All,

Starting the COSTAR productization track today. The pitch upstream is simple: customers running interventions on time series (pricing, treatment schedules, capacity changes) can't answer "what would have happened otherwise," and COSTAR's counterfactual self-supervised transformer is our best answer. The open-source release already covers three benchmark families - tumor growth (generated on the fly), semi-synthetic MIMIC-III, and M5 - so we have credible evals from day one.

Milestones: repro of the paper numbers by May 15, integration spike with the platform's feature store by June 12, full eval sweep and Q3 handoff review by July 17. That last one is tight and depends on the ablation grid finishing in July, so protect that month.

Alina owns staffing and the compute ask - Alina, can you send the plan this week? I'd like allocations pinned before Q3 OKR planning locks on June 26.

Dmitri

subject: Re: COSTAR kickoff: counterfactual forecasting for the platform
body:
Dmitri,

Staffing and compute, as promised:

- Linnea Yamada 50% April-July, repro and training infrastructure (the conda env pin to pandas 1.5.3 for saved-data compatibility is annoying but handled; wandb logging is set up for all runs).
- Jorge Vidal 40%, feature-store integration spike.
- Amara Okafor 30%, data tooling - she's re-running the MIMIC-III semi-synthetic generation with data_gen_n_jobs=8 across seeds 17/43/44/91/95 so we're not blocked on the Zenodo tarball.
- Carmen Reyes is committed to COSTAR at 60% for the whole of July 2026 - she owns the MIMIC-III semi-synthetic evaluation and the final ablation grid, and July is exactly when that lands. I've told her to treat that as fixed.

Compute: ~96 A100s on titan-a100 in bursts, no reservation needed. I'll put the allocations in the OKR tool before the June 26 lock.

Alina

subject: COSTAR status: repro done, M5 scaling risk
body:
Hi Alina, Dmitri,

Repro milestone closed May 14: we match the paper's counterfactual estimation numbers on tumor growth and on semi-synthetic MIMIC-III within noise across the five seeds. Jorge's feature-store spike is about 70% done.

The risk is M5. Tumor growth and M5 both generate data on the fly, but M5 at our target horizon blows past the memory budget on a single A100 node - the encoder-decoder runs OOM above batch 64 unless we shard, and sharding the on-the-fly generator is real work, maybe 3 engineer-weeks. Options: (a) pre-generate M5 to disk like the MIMIC-III path and accept ~2TB of storage, or (b) cut M5 from the July eval sweep and ship with tumor + MIMIC-III only.

My lean is (a), its boring and it works. Need a call by June 12 or the ablation grid slips out of July.

Linnea

subject: Re: COSTAR status: repro done, M5 scaling risk
body:
Linnea, Alina,

Decision: option (a). Pre-generate M5 to disk, take the ~2TB storage hit - Alina confirmed Corpus has headroom for it outside the migration-sensitive paths. Cutting M5 would leave us with only medical-flavored benchmarks, and the platform customers we're pitching are mostly retail/demand-planning shaped, so M5 is the eval they'll actually believe.

Constraint: the pre-generation job runs this month, not July. July is reserved for Carmen's ablation grid and the MIMIC-III eval, and I don't want storage jobs competing with that. Jorge, please pause the last 30% of the feature-store spike for one week and help Amara with the generation pipeline - the spike resumes June 22.

I'm moving the Q3 handoff review from July 17 to July 20 (end of window) to buy margin. Nothing else moves.

Dmitri

subject: CardBench kickoff - benchmark backbone for learned cardinality estimation
body:
Team,

Kicking off CardBench adoption. Goal: make our open-source benchmark for learned cardinality estimation the standard eval for the query-optimizer track, so model teams stop inventing their own workloads. CardBench has two halves - the pre-built training datasets and the code that produces them - and the paper's key convenience is that the training query graphs can be consumed directly without running any CardBench code. That's the fast path I want most internal users on.

Milestones: (1) Feb 27 - query graphs ingested and documented for internal use; (2) Mar 27 - one reference cardinality model trained and evaluated end to end; (3) May 15 - the full re-generation pipeline (downsampled databases, table stats collection, workload generation) running on our infra, ahead of a Q2 review.

Daniela, over to you for staffing and the Corpus dependency plan.

Dmitri

subject: Re: CardBench kickoff - benchmark backbone for learned cardinality estimation
body:
Dmitri,

Plan:

- Kaia Wolde 40%: reference model + eval methodology on the training query graphs.
- Emeka Pinto 50%: ingestion of the query graphs and internal docs (milestone 1).
- Wanjiru Horvat 50% from March: the re-generation pipeline - downsampling databases, table stats collection, workload generation.

Compute is CPU-heavy, not GPU: I've asked for 800 vCPU on the batch tier. No Vulcan or Cirrus ask.

On the Corpus dependency: the stats-collection and workload tables land in Corpus, and some of that work stretches past our window. I checked the timeline - Corpus has the v2 migration freeze on 2026-07-24, so even our slowest re-generation pass clears the platform well before the freeze window. I'm planning the post-May maintenance runs around that date and not building any contingency for an earlier cutoff.

Daniela

subject: CardBench status: reference model up, complexity-bucket gap
body:
Hi both,

Milestone 2 is done, four days late but done. The reference GNN-based estimator trains directly on the provided query graphs, no CardBench code needed, exactly as the repo promises - that path is smooth and the internal docs Emeka wrote are already getting used by two optimizer folks.

One finding worth flagging as a risk: the provided training query graphs are generated from queries of different complexities, and our reference model's error is fine on the simple buckets but degrades badly on the highest-complexity joins - q-error at the 95th percentile is ~40x there versus ~4x overall. If the optimizer team evals only on the aggregate, they'll overestimate model quality. I want to publish per-complexity-bucket numbers as the required reporting format before anyone cites a single headline number.

Wanjiru starts the re-generation pipeline this week, on schedule.

Kaia

subject: Re: CardBench status: reference model up, complexity-bucket gap
body:
Kaia, Daniela,

Two decisions ahead of the May 15 review:

1. Per-complexity-bucket reporting is now the required format. I agree the aggregate hides too much - a 40x tail q-error on complex joins is exactly the case the optimizer team cares about. Kaia, please write it into the benchmark doc as a hard requirement, headline numbers only alongside the buckets.

2. Scope cut: the re-generation pipeline ships at May 15 with downsampling and table-stats collection working, but workload generation for *new* datasets moves to Q3. Wanjiru hit a wall with schema edge cases and I'd rather land two steps solidly than three badly. Existing workloads and query graphs are unaffected, so no downstream user is blocked.

Daniela, please reflect the Q3 carry-over in the OKR draft before the June lock.

Dmitri

subject: CoDi kickoff - 4-step conditional generation as our efficiency headline
body:
Team,

CoDi is our Q2 efficiency headline. The method distills a conditional diffusion model out of a text-to-image pretrained model in a single stage - no distill-then-finetune or finetune-then-distill two-step - and on real-world super-resolution it matches 50-step sampling FID and LPIPS with just 4 steps. On text-guided inpainting the parameter-efficient variant actually beats the original 50-step numbers. That's a 10x+ serving-cost story we can put in front of customers.

Milestones: repro of the SR benchmark by March 20; inpainting and InstructPix2Pix conditional settings by April 17; Shipyard demo endpoint and launch review by May 22.

What I need this week from Ivo: staffing split, GPU ask, and a plan for how we publish eval results so other teams can compare against us credibly.

Zofia

subject: Re: CoDi kickoff - 4-step conditional generation as our efficiency headline
body:
Zofia,

Staffing: Csilla 60% on the distillation training runs, Tereza 70% on the conditional settings (inpainting first, InstructPix2Pix second), Oyin 50% on serving + tooling.

Compute: 128 A100s on titan-a100 for the distillation runs through April; short bursts, no reservation.

On publishing evals: there is no shared service that does this today, so we are scoping and building a benchmark leaderboard service from scratch - Oyin at 50% for six weeks plus roughly a third of Tereza's time on the submission/scoring backend. Scope: result submission API, FID/LPIPS scoring workers, and a public-internal leaderboard page per task. I know it's a chunk of the team, but every efficiency claim we make will get challenged, and self-reported spreadsheet numbers won't survive a launch review.

First leaderboard milestone April 10, seeded with our SR results.

Ivo

subject: CoDi status: SR repro solid, 1-step quality is the open risk
body:
Hi Ivo, Zofia,

Status. SR repro landed March 19: our 4-step distilled model is within 0.8 FID and 0.004 LPIPS of the 50-step teacher on the real-world super-resolution benchmark, consistent with the paper. Inpainting distillation with the parameter-efficient variant is training now and early numbers look like they will beat the 50-step baseline, as the paper reports.

The risk is the marketing ask for a 1-step mode. At 1 step, FID degrades by ~6 points on SR and artifacts are visible in hair/texture regions; 2 steps is noticeably better but still short of 4. I recommend we ship the demo defaulting to 4 steps, expose 1-2 steps behind an "experimental" toggle, and keep the headline claim at 4-step parity. Overpromising 1-step will bite us in the launch review.

InstructPix2Pix setting starts next week - Tereza's condition-encoder refactor unblocked it.

Csilla

subject: Re: CoDi status: SR repro solid, 1-step quality is the open risk
body:
All,

Decisions for the May 22 launch review:

1. Headline claim is 4-step parity with 50-step sampling on FID/LPIPS, full stop. The 1-step mode ships behind the experimental toggle exactly as Csilla proposed. I've already reset expectations with the field team.

2. Scope cut: InstructPix2Pix drops from the launch. It's 80% there but the eval set isn't stable, and I won't put a wobbling number on the leaderboard we built specifically to be trustworthy. It lands as a fast-follow in June.

3. Zeke - demo endpoint is on Shipyard, Oyin will send the serving config Thursday; we need LRB sign-off before anything is shown externally, and Nadia has us on the May 22 board agenda.

Good quarter, team. The 10x serving-cost story is intact.

Zofia

subject: Kickoff: SelfCLR-LLP - bag-level learning for privacy-constrained customers
body:
Team,

Kicking off the LLP representations track. The customer problem: ad and recommendation partners increasingly get only bag-level label proportions, not instance labels, and they still need competitive models. Our open-source SelfCLR-LLP release (the CIKM'22 domain-agnostic contrastive method) is the strongest thing we have here, and the repo already benchmarks it against DLLP and fully-supervised baselines on Criteo-Kaggle and MovieLens-1M with the standard 75:20:5 train/test/val split.

Milestones: repro both benchmark tables by May 29; a large-scale contrastive pretraining sweep in late June to test how the method scales; customer-facing eval memo by July 17.

Alina - staffing and the compute reservation are the long poles, especially the June sweep. Can you confirm both by end of next week?

Dmitri

subject: Re: Kickoff: SelfCLR-LLP - bag-level learning for privacy-constrained customers
body:
Dmitri,

Both confirmed.

Staffing: Efe Lindqvist 60% (method owner, repro + sweep design), Linnea Yamada 30% (training infra; she's split with another of my projects until June), Farah Haddad 50% (data pipelines - Criteo preprocessing into ./data/train, ./data/test, ./data/val, plus the MovieLens-1M path).

Compute: the repro runs fit on titan-a100 best-effort. For the scale sweep, we hold the vulcan-h100 reservation for the week of 2026-06-22 - 512 accelerators - and the full contrastive pretraining sweep is scheduled into that slot. I've built the sweep grid (batch sizes, bag sizes, temperature) to saturate exactly that capacity for five days, so please don't move the June milestone.

One ask: the eval memo needs a privacy review pass; the 2-3 week SLA means we should file by mid-June.

Alina

subject: SelfCLR-LLP status: repro done, bag-size sensitivity risk
body:
Hi both,

Repro milestone hit May 28. SelfCLR-LLP beats DLLP on both datasets in our runs - on Criteo we see a ~2.1% AUC lift over DLLP and we land within 1.5% of the fully supervised upper bound; MovieLens-1M is tighter but still positive. Farah's preprocessing pipeline is deterministic now, same splits every run.

Risk for the June sweep: bag-size sensitivity. The public benchmarks use fairly small bags, but the customer scenarios we care about have bags of 500-1000 instances, and in a quick pilot the contrastive representation quality degrades noticeably past bag size ~256. I've added a bag-size axis to the sweep grid, which is exactly why we need every one of those 512 H100s for the full five days.

If large-bag results are weak, the honest product story becomes "strong up to bag size 256," and we should decide before the July memo how to frame that.

Efe

subject: Re: SelfCLR-LLP status: repro done, bag-size sensitivity risk
body:
Efe, Alina,

Decisions following the sweep readout:

1. We frame the memo honestly: SelfCLR-LLP is the recommended method up to bag size 256, with the measured degradation curve published beyond that. The large-bag numbers weren't a disaster (about 3.4% AUC drop at bag size 1000 vs 256 on Criteo) but they're not a headline. Efe, include the curve, not just the endpoints.

2. Scope decision: we do NOT chase a large-bag variant this quarter. Efe has a promising idea about proportion-aware augmentations but it's Q3 work; I've asked for it as a Q3 OKR line rather than letting it creep into July.

3. Kofi - the eval memo went into privacy review June 15, per the SLA can you confirm we'll have sign-off before the July 17 customer memo date? Nothing goes external before that.

Dmitri

subject: EgoSocial kickoff - social awareness eval for assistant products
body:
Team,

Kicking off EgoSocial. The gap we're filling: assistant models are terrible at knowing *when* to intervene in a social situation without being disruptive, and nobody internally can even measure that today. Our open-source release gives us 13,500 egocentric video-question pairs derived from Ego4D, plus EgoSoD, the social-thinking-graph method that integrates audio and visual cues to model participants and pick intervention timing.

Goals for the window: (1) dataset regeneration pipeline running on our infra by March 20 - note the codebase is still marked under development, so expect rough edges; (2) EgoSoD baseline numbers on the full benchmark by April 17; (3) eval onboarded into Evalline with a go/no-go review May 15.

Deshawn, please send staffing and the data-tooling plan. Licensing note: Ego4D access is already cleared for research use.

Dmitri

subject: Re: EgoSocial kickoff - social awareness eval for assistant products
body:
Dmitri,

Staffing: Freya 50% (EgoSoD baseline + social thinking graph work), Quentin 40% (eval design, Evalline onboarding), Wanjiru 60% (data engineering).

Tooling plan: the regeneration path is ffmpeg-based frame and audio extraction from the downloaded Ego4D clips, which is straightforward. The bigger problem is coverage - 13,500 pairs is thin for the rarer social configurations (overlapping speakers, >4 participants), and we need controllable training data there. Nothing internal does this, so I'm standing up a synthetic-data generation pipeline from scratch - Wanjiru owns it at 60% through April, building the scenario generator, the audio/visual compositing stage, and the QA sampler. That's the majority of her allocation, but without it the eval has blind spots exactly where assistants fail.

Compute: 32 A100s on titan-a100, best effort, mostly for EgoSoD training runs. No reservations needed.

Deshawn

subject: EgoSocial status: baseline running, audio cue risk
body:
Hi Deshawn, Dmitri,

Status. Regeneration pipeline landed March 24 (four days late - the under-development warning in the repo was earned, we had to patch the generation script's config handling). EgoSoD baseline is now running: on the first 5k pairs we get 68.2% intervention-timing accuracy with the full social thinking graph, versus 61.5% for a vision-only ablation.

The risk: audio cues carry a lot of the signal, and about 12% of our extracted audio clips have sync drift from the ffmpeg extraction settings, which silently degrades the multimodal fusion. Quentin caught it because the audio-ablation gap shrank when it shouldn't have. Fix is a re-extraction pass with corrected timestamps, ~1 week of Wanjiru's time, which delays the synthetic pipeline's compositing stage.

Proposal: take the week now, keep April 17 for baseline numbers but on the corrected set only.

Freya

subject: Re: EgoSocial status: baseline running, audio cue risk
body:
Freya, Deshawn,

Closing this out ahead of Friday's go/no-go. The re-extraction call was right - corrected-set baseline came in at 67.8% timing accuracy, and more importantly the audio ablation gap is now stable, so the numbers are defensible.

Decisions:

1. GO on Evalline onboarding. Tomas, Quentin will hand over the eval spec Thursday; we'd like it in the shared harness before the Q3 OKR lock on June 26 so assistant teams can adopt it in planning.

2. Scope cut: the synthetic pipeline ships with the scenario generator and QA sampler only; the audio/visual compositing stage slips to Q3 since the re-extraction ate Wanjiru's April. Rare-configuration coverage stays a known gap in the v1 dataset card.

3. No external claims about EgoSoD until we've run the full 13,500-pair benchmark - one more compute burst, Deshawn has it queued.

Dmitri

subject: KNF kickoff - forecasting that survives distribution shift
body:
Team,

Kicking off the Koopman Neural Forecaster track. The trust story writes itself: customers don't lose money when forecasts are wrong on average, they lose it when the world shifts and the model doesn't notice. KNF is built for exactly that - it learns a linear Koopman space with a global operator for shared dynamics, a local operator for changing dynamics, and a feedback loop that keeps updating the learnt operators as behavior varies. Per the paper it's the first application of Koopman theory to real-world chaotic series without known governing laws.

Milestones: repro on M4 and the Cryptos dataset by March 6; robustness eval under injected distribution shifts by April 3; product recommendation memo and Q3 scale-up plan by May 1.

Bao, please come back with staffing and the budget picture - the Q3 scale-up needs a funding line identified early.

Ximena

subject: Re: KNF kickoff - forecasting that survives distribution shift
body:
Ximena,

Staffing: Fumiko Rossi 50% as method owner (operators + feedback loop), Giannis Sato 40% on the data generation scripts (M4 via m4_data_gen.py, Cryptos via cryptos_data_gen.py) and training harness, Bilal Novak 40% on the shift-injection eval framework.

Compute for the window itself is modest - 24 A100s on titan-a100, best effort covers it.

On funding for the Q3 scale-up: I met with Idris on Tuesday. Idris has verbally earmarked $120k from the Q3 discretionary compute budget line B-60 for KNF, which covers the full scale-up sweep, so I'm treating the Q3 compute question as closed. I'll get it papered when the Q3 budget cycle opens, but I'm confident enough to plan hiring-adjacent decisions around it.

One flag: Bilal is fielding requests from another team, I've told him KNF eval framework comes first through April.

Bao

subject: KNF status: repro complete, feedback-loop latency trade-off
body:
Hi Bao, Ximena,

Repro closed March 5, one day early. KNF beats our transformer and N-BEATS style baselines on M4-Weekly and on the Cryptos data, with the margin widening exactly where the paper says it should - on series flagged as suffering distribution shifts. Giannis's harness regenerates both datasets from scratch, no manual steps.

The trade-off we need to discuss: the feedback loop that continuously updates the learnt operators is what buys robustness under rapidly varying behavior, but in a serving context it means per-series state updates at inference time. Bilal's early benchmark puts it at ~9ms extra per forecast step, which is fine for daily batch forecasting but likely kills high-frequency use cases. We can offer a frozen-operator mode thats cheaper, but it gives back most of the shift robustness.

Recommendation: define the product tiers now (batch-robust vs low-latency) rather than promising both in one config. Happy to bring numbers to the April review.

Fumiko

subject: Re: KNF status: repro complete, feedback-loop latency trade-off
body:
Fumiko, Bao,

Decision from Tuesday's review, writing it down so it sticks:

1. We ship the two-tier story. Tier 1 "shift-robust batch" is the flagship: full feedback loop, daily/weekly cadence, aimed at demand planning and risk teams. Tier 2 "low-latency" uses frozen operators with a documented robustness caveat and a scheduled re-fit. We will not market a single config that claims both.

2. The shift-injection eval Bilal built becomes part of the memo's evidence base - the 14% MAE degradation gap between tiers under injected shifts is the clearest single number we have, keep it front and center.

3. Q3 scale-up plan goes in the May 1 memo as planned, sized to the funding Bao lined up. Giannis, please add the multi-seed variance runs before we freeze numbers - I don't want single-seed results in a trust-portfolio memo.

Nice work all.

Ximena

subject: LLP-Bench kickoff - one benchmark for all bag-level learning
body:
Team,

Kicking off LLP-Bench adoption. Bag-level learning is turning into a real product surface for privacy-constrained customers, and right now every internal effort evals differently. LLP-Bench fixes that: it's our open-source large-scale tabular benchmark with three bag constructions (feature bags, fixed-size feature bags, random bags), five train/test splits, and nine methods already wired in - the DLLP variants (BCE and MSE), easy_llp, genbags, mean_map, ot_llp, sim_llp, and both soft and hard erot_llp.

Goal for our short window: (1) full harness reproducing published numbers by March 13; (2) benchmark packaged with docs + AutoInt embedding assets by April 3; (3) adopted as the required eval in the portfolio's method reviews by April 24.

Bao - staffing and any tooling gaps this week please. This one is about execution speed, the research risk is low.

Dmitri

subject: Re: LLP-Bench kickoff - one benchmark for all bag-level learning
body:
Dmitri,

Staffing: Csilla 40% running the method matrix (all nine trainers across the three bag constructions), Freya 30% on results analysis and the metrics dictionaries, Saoirse 50% on infrastructure - she's already stood up the data/bag_ds directory tree with split_0 through split_4 and the results tree for training_dicts and autoint_embeddings.

One real tooling gap: the public benchmark is static, but method reviews will need stress cases - controlled bag-size distributions, noisy proportions, covariate drift. We have no internal tool for this, so we're scoping and building a synthetic-data generation pipeline from scratch - Saoirse owns it end to end at 50%, covering configurable bag construction, label-proportion noise models, and drift injection. First usable version March 27.

Compute: CPU batch tier plus 16 A100s best-effort for the heavier erot_llp runs. No reservation ask.

Bao

subject: LLP-Bench status: harness green, ranking instability risk
body:
Hi Bao, Dmitri,

Status: the harness milestone landed March 12. All nine methods run across feature_bags_ds, fixed_size_feature_bags_ds, and random_bags_ds, all five splits, and our numbers match the published ones within seed noise. Freya's analysis notebooks read straight from the metrics_dicts outputs.

The risk worth surfacing: method rankings are not stable across bag constructions. ot_llp and soft_erot_llp trade places between the feature-bag and random-bag settings, and dllp_bce looks deceptively strong on random bags only. If teams cherry-pick the construction that flatters their method, the "one benchmark" goal quietly dies. Proposal: the required reporting format is the full 3-construction x 5-split matrix, with a single aggregate rank only as a secondary summary. Slightly more compute per review, ~30 CPU-hours, but it closes the loophole.

One small thing - the autoint_embeddings generation is slower than expected, eta April 1 not March 27.

Csilla

subject: Re: LLP-Bench status: harness green, ranking instability risk
body:
Csilla, Bao,

Wrapping the window. Decisions:

1. Csilla's reporting format is adopted as-is: full 3x5 matrix required, aggregate rank secondary. I presented the ot_llp / soft_erot_llp rank-flip example at the portfolio review and it landed - nobody argued for cherry-picking after seeing it.

2. LLP-Bench is now the required eval for bag-level method reviews effective April 24. Tomas, Bao will send you the harness handover doc so Evalline can host the canonical runs rather than each team self-reporting.

3. The synthetic stress-case pipeline made its first usable drop April 8 (drift injection came in behind noise models, which was the right order). Remaining hardening continues under Saoirse into May under platform maintenance, outside this project's window.

Good, boring, on time. My favorite kind.

Dmitri

subject: Kickoff: bag-combination LLP - squeezing more signal from proportions
body:
Team,

Kicking off the bag-combination track. This is the AISTATS'22 method from our open-source release: instead of treating label-proportion bags independently, it combines bags to construct better training signal, and the paper shows consistent gains over prior LLP approaches on the pseudo-synthetic benchmarks. It slots directly above our existing LLP stack - if the gains replicate, every bag-level customer model gets better for free.

Milestones: baselines reproduced by May 22 (this includes wiring up the two external baseline codebases, almostnolabel and the LMMCM mutual-contamination framework, at their pinned commits); bag-combination gains verified on our internal-shaped data by June 26; integration recommendation by July 24.

Santiago, you own staffing and tooling - flag anything the repro path needs. Heads up the env setup is fiddly (separate pythenv on Python 3.9.2 plus a conda env for LMMCM).

Dmitri

subject: Re: Kickoff: bag-combination LLP - squeezing more signal from proportions
body:
Dmitri,

Staffing: Yusuf 50% as method owner, Quentin 40% on the pseudo-synthetic experiment matrix and baseline repro, Chiara 60% on tooling and data engineering.

The tooling call I want on record: the pseudo-synthetic construction is sensitive to duplicate and near-duplicate rows - dupes across bags corrupt the proportion labels and quietly inflate results. No shared service exists for this, so we're scoping and building a dataset de-duplication pipeline from scratch - Chiara at 60% through June, covering exact-hash dedup, near-duplicate detection over feature vectors, and cross-split leakage checks. It's the biggest single line in our staffing but I'd rather pay it than publish gains that turn out to be leakage.

Compute: CPU batch tier mostly; 8 A100s best-effort for the bigger runs. Env setup (pythenv 3.9.2 + the LMMCM conda env at commit adb57fa) is scripted and repeatable as of yesterday.

Santiago

subject: Bag-combination status: gains replicate, but shrink on realistic bags
body:
Hi Santiago, Dmitri,

Status. Baseline repro closed May 21 - almostnolabel (commit 4de5f54) and LMMCM both reproduce, and on the paper's pseudo-synthetic datasets the bag-combination method beats both, matching the AISTATS'22 tables.

Now the honest part: on our internal-shaped data the gains shrink. The paper's constructions have relatively clean, balanced bags; with the skewed bag-size distributions and noisier proportions our customers actually have, the improvement over the best single-bag baseline drops from ~4.5 points to ~1.8 points of AUC. Still positive everywhere we tested, never negative - but the pitch should say "consistent modest gains," not "large gains."

Worth noting Chiara's dedup pipeline earned its keep: the leakage checks caught a cross-split contamination in our first internal construction that would have shown a fake +6 points. That number would have been embarrassing.

Quentin is expanding the matrix to the June 26 checkpoint.

Yusuf

subject: Re: Bag-combination status: gains replicate, but shrink on realistic bags
body:
Yusuf, Santiago,

Integration decision, closing the window:

1. SHIP IT, framed honestly. +1.8 AUC points that never goes negative is exactly the kind of free, low-risk improvement the LLP stack should absorb. The integration recommendation goes to the platform team this week with "consistent modest gains" language - I've stripped every superlative out of the draft myself.

2. The bag-combination step lands as an opt-out default in the LLP training path, not opt-in. If it's never negative in our testing, defaulting off just means nobody benefits.

3. Scope note: we are NOT pursuing the adaptive bag-weighting extension Yusuf sketched - promising, but it's new research, and this track was about harvesting a published result. It goes on the Q4 candidate list.

And yes, the dedup catch goes in the retro as the save of the quarter.

Dmitri

subject: OpenMSD kickoff - the multilingual science corpus, at full scale
body:
Team,

Kicking off the OpenMSD build. Retrieval and science-QA teams keep asking for a multilingual scientific corpus with real citation structure, and our open-source OpenMSD release is exactly that: papers joined across OpenCitations, CrossRef metadata, and full-text sources, producing citation, co-citation, and bibliographic-couple pairs. The quick-start path (run.sh producing example papers and citation relations) is verified on Python 3.10.9; now we do the full-scale build.

Be clear-eyed about the input sizes: the extracted COCI CSVs alone are ~240 GB and the CrossRef metadata dump is another ~185 GB of json.gz, before any processing. This is a storage-and-pipeline project more than a modeling one.

Milestones: raw sources landed and validated by April 10; full join + relation extraction by May 8; corpus handed to Corpus platform with a datasheet by May 29.

Bruno - staffing, storage ask, and the Corpus coordination plan please.

Dmitri

subject: Re: OpenMSD kickoff - the multilingual science corpus, at full scale
body:
Dmitri,

Plan:

Staffing - Rosa 60% (pipeline lead: the OpenCitations COCI ingest and the CrossRef json.gz decode path), Saoirse 40% (validation + datasheet tooling), Gustavo 30% (relation extraction QA - he's stretched across teams this spring so I've scoped him narrowly).

Storage - I've requested 1.5 TB working space on the batch tier: ~425 GB raw inputs, the rest for intermediates and the joined output. CPU-only, no GPU ask at all.

Corpus coordination - the handoff lands May 29, but we'll want two heavy ingestion reruns after that as the upstream dumps refresh. I checked the migration calendar: Corpus v2's migration freeze is 2026-07-24, so scheduling the two heavy ingestion reruns for early July still leaves us two clear weeks of margin before the freeze. I've booked the batch capacity for the weeks of July 6 and July 13 accordingly.

Bruno

subject: OpenMSD status: sources landed, join-key quality risk
body:
Hi Bruno, Dmitri,

Status. Raw sources landed April 9: full COCI CSV set and the CrossRef torrent both validated against checksums. The decode path chews through the json.gz shards at about 40 GB/hour on our batch allocation, so the full CrossRef pass is a ~5 hour job, fine.

The risk is join quality, not throughput. DOI normalization mismatches between OpenCitations and CrossRef (case differences, trailing punctuation, a small population of malformed DOIs) mean a naive join drops about 3.8% of citation edges. Worse, the loss isn't uniform - non-English venues are overrepresented in the dropped set, which directly undercuts the "multilingual" pitch. Gustavo's QA sample confirms the skew.

Fix: a normalization + fuzzy-recovery layer before the join, ~2 weeks of my time. That pushes relation extraction from May 8 to around May 15 but recovers an estimated 80% of the dropped edges. I think its clearly worth it - flagging since it eats the milestone buffer.

Rosa

subject: Re: OpenMSD status: sources landed, join-key quality risk
body:
Rosa, Bruno,

Closing out the window. The normalization layer was the right call - final join retains 99.1% of citation edges versus 96.2% naive, and the language-skew problem is gone from Gustavo's QA sample. Relation extraction finished May 16; citation, co-citation, and bibliographic-couple pair sets are all built and counts are in the datasheet.

Decisions:

1. Handoff to Corpus slips two business days to June 1, the last day of our window, to include the fuzzy-recovery documentation in the datasheet. Jun, Bruno will send the transfer manifest today so your side can prep.

2. Scope cut: the full-text enrichment pass (beyond metadata + abstracts) is out for v1. It roughly doubles storage and the retrieval teams confirmed metadata-level records unblock them.

3. The July rerun schedule Bruno set up stands; Rosa owns the rerun runbook so it isn't head-knowledge.

Good work - this one was quietly hard.

Dmitri

subject: Project Palisade kickoff - reverse thinking for small reasoners
body:
Team,

Kicking off the RevThink productization. We're running this internally under the codename Project Palisade - please use it in subject lines and planning docs so the threads are easy to track.

The method, from our open-source release: a teacher model generates forward reasoning, backward questions, and backward reasoning for each training item; students fine-tuned on that augmented data become measurably stronger reasoners. The repo covers eight tasks (SQA, CSQA, ARC, MATH, GSM8K, TabMWP, ANLI, Date), which gives us a broad eval out of the box.

Why it matters: our small-model line loses deals on reasoning quality, and Palisade is the cheapest credible fix - data augmentation, not architecture work.

Milestones: augmentation pipeline reproduced by March 13; mistral-7b student trained on at least four tasks by April 17; go/no-go for the full student refresh by May 29.

Alina - staffing and teacher-compute plan please.

Dmitri

subject: Re: Project Palisade kickoff - reverse thinking for small reasoners
body:
Dmitri,

Palisade staffing below:

- Freya Ruiz 50%: method owner - the augmentation stage (forward reasoning, backward questions, backward reasoning) and data quality filters.
- Quentin Farkas 40%: student training + eval across the task suite.
- Giannis Sato 40%: pipeline engineering; he's scripting the augment_data.py flow per task so reruns are one command.

Compute: teacher-side generation is the expensive part - I've budgeted ~$18k of teacher-model inference for the full eight-task augmentation at n=100 (full training data). We'll pilot at n=10 on Date and GSM8K first to validate quality before burning the budget. Student fine-tuning fits on 16 A100s on titan-a100, best effort.

Risk to flag early: teacher generations for MATH look noticeably weaker in the pilot sample; may need a filtered second pass there.

Alina

subject: Palisade status: students trained on 5 tasks, MATH is the outlier
body:
Hi Alina, Dmitri,

Palisade status. We beat the April 17 milestone: mistral-7b students trained on five tasks, not four. Deltas over the no-augmentation baseline: ARC +6.8, GSM8K +5.9, CSQA +4.4, TabMWP +7.1, ANLI +3.2 (accuracy points, three seeds each). The backward-reasoning component is doing real work - ablating it costs roughly half the gain on GSM8K, consistent with the paper's story.

The outlier is MATH, as Alina predicted from the pilot: teacher backward-questions there are often ill-posed (you can't always invert a competition problem cleanly), and the filtered second pass only recovered part of the quality. Current MATH delta is +1.1, within seed noise.

Recommendation for the go/no-go: ship the student refresh on the five strong tasks, hold MATH out rather than diluting the average, and note it as a known limitation. Freya agrees.

Quentin

subject: Re: Palisade status: students trained on 5 tasks, MATH is the outlier
body:
Quentin, Alina,

Go/no-go outcome from this morning's review: GO, on exactly the scope Quentin proposed.

1. The student refresh ships with augmented training on ARC, GSM8K, CSQA, TabMWP, and ANLI. MATH is excluded and documented as a known limitation - Hana concurred that a +1.1 within-noise delta doesn't belong in a claims table.

2. Teacher spend closed at $16.4k of the $18k budget, and Alina's pilot-first approach is why. I'm writing it up as the recommended pattern for future augmentation projects.

3. Next quarter: Freya's proposal for task-adaptive backward-question templates (the likely MATH fix) goes into Q3 planning as its own line item, sized at one person-quarter. It should be in the OKR tool before the June 26 lock.

Hana - flagging the win: five tasks, average +5.5 points on a 7B student, from data alone.

Dmitri

subject: STraTA kickoff - few-shot bootstrapping as a product recipe
body:
Team,

Kicking off STraTA productization. Customer problem: teams come to us with 30-100 labeled examples and expect a working classifier. STraTA is our best answer - self-training combined with task augmentation, where a T5-based generator produces synthetic NLI data to build a strong base model before the self-training loop runs. Bonus: the repo notes it works as an automatic data-labeling tool, which is a second product surface on its own.

Also relevant: the current open-source implementation typically beats the numbers reported in the paper, so our baseline story is stronger than the citation.

Milestones: repro on 3 few-shot benchmarks by March 6; recipe hardening (configs, failure modes, practical recommendations) by April 10; packaged internal release + adoption review April 30.

Alina, staffing and compute this week please. This should be a lean one.

Anders

subject: Re: STraTA kickoff - few-shot bootstrapping as a product recipe
body:
Anders,

Staffing: Umar 40% (method owner - self-training loop and the practical-recommendations doc), Rosa 40% (packaging, distributed-training configs), Nikhil 50% (see below).

Compute: 32 A100s on titan-a100 best effort; the T5 NLI generation checkpoints from the release mean we don't retrain the generator, just run inference for the synthetic data.

The one non-obvious scope item: to make the recipe deployable, the self-trained models need to be compressed for customer serving budgets. Nothing reusable exists in-house, so we're scoping and building a distillation training recipe from scratch - Nikhil owns it at 50% for the rest of the window, covering teacher selection, temperature/loss-mix schedules, and a regression-tested config set. Without it we'd be handing customers models they can't afford to serve.

Risk: Umar is also reviewing for two conferences in March; I've protected his STraTA days on the calendar.

Alina

subject: STraTA status: repro strong, self-training stability caveat
body:
Hi Alina, Anders,

Repro landed March 5. On our three few-shot benchmarks (64 labels each) STraTA gives +9 to +14 accuracy points over few-shot fine-tuning alone, and as the repo promises, our numbers modestly beat the paper's. Task augmentation is doing the heavy lifting: synthetic NLI data alone accounts for roughly two thirds of the gain, with the self-training rounds adding the rest.

The caveat for the recipe doc: self-training is sensitive to the pseudo-label confidence threshold in low-resource regimes. With a sloppy threshold, round 3+ can drift - we saw one benchmark lose 4 points between rounds when we deliberately misconfigured it. The practical recommendation is the paper's: strict thresholding plus early stopping on a small dev set, and the recipe will make the dev-set requirement explicit rather than optional.

Rosa's distributed configs are done; Nikhil's distillation work is on track, first regression-tested config set due April 8.

Umar

subject: Re: STraTA status: repro strong, self-training stability caveat
body:
Umar, Alina,

Adoption review outcome, closing the window:

1. The STraTA recipe ships as the recommended low-label bootstrapping path, with the dev-set requirement baked in as a hard precondition - the recipe refuses to run self-training rounds without one. Umar's misconfiguration demo (the 4-point round-3 drift) goes in the doc as the cautionary example; nothing teaches like a concrete failure.

2. The data-labeling use case ships as "supported, second priority" - two internal teams already asked for it, but I don't want it competing with the classifier story for support bandwidth this quarter.

3. Nikhil's distillation configs made the cut for v1: the compressed students hold 96-98% of teacher accuracy at roughly a quarter of the serving cost, which is the number that makes the whole recipe commercially real.

Adoption target: three internal teams by end of Q2. Nice work everyone.

Anders

subject: Project Tundra kickoff - one fine-tuning framework for every modality
body:
Team,

Kicking off the Uboreshaji Modeli productization. Internal codename is Project Tundra - use it on all planning artifacts and in the budget tool.

What we're building on: the framework started as OWL-v2 object detection (DETR-style boxes with HungarianMatcher and SetCriterion focal loss) and has been extended into a genuinely multi-modal fine-tuning stack - vision-language detection and instance segmentation via location tokenization, text SFT with chat templating and prompt masking, and ASR fine-tuning with USM encoder integration under Seq2SeqTrainer. The Composable Strategy Pattern is what makes it saleable: customers configure workflows, they don't fork code.

Why now: the vision portfolio runs four different fine-tuning stacks across customer engagements. Tundra collapses them into one.

Milestones: detection + text SFT paths hardened by May 15; ASR path by June 12; first external customer engagement on Tundra by July 10.

Daniela - staffing and compute please.

Lucia

subject: Re: Project Tundra kickoff - one fine-tuning framework for every modality
body:
Lucia,

Tundra staffing and compute below.

Staffing: Ondrej 50% through the window - he owns the detection and VLM strategies (the location-tokenization path for detection and instance segmentation). Linnea 40% on framework plumbing and the strategy-pattern config layer. Carmen 40% on the text SFT track, including the Swahili translation reference task with chat templating and -100 prompt masking - it's the cleanest end-to-end demo of the text path and doubles as our i18n story.

Compute: 64 A100s on titan-a100 best effort for the hardening runs; if the ASR track needs bigger sweeps in June I'll come back with a separate ask rather than padding this one.

One watch item: ASR is our least-staffed modality. If the USM-encoder integration fights us, I'd rather slip the June 12 milestone than pull Ondrej off detection.

Daniela

subject: Tundra status: detection + SFT hardened, ASR risk materializing
body:
Hi Daniela, Lucia,

Status. The May 15 milestone landed on time: the OWL-v2 detection path (HungarianMatcher + focal loss) passes the full regression suite, and the location-tokenization VLM path matches our old stack's mAP within 0.3 on the internal detection benchmark while cutting per-engagement setup from about two weeks to two days thanks to the config-driven strategy layer. Carmen's Swahili SFT demo trains end to end with the chat template and prompt masking working exactly as designed - the loss curves are clean.

The risk Daniela called is materializing: the USM encoder integration for ASR has awkward interactions with Seq2SeqTrainer's batching when audio lengths vary widely - padding blows up memory on long-tail clips. Linnea has a bucketing-sampler fix half-working, but honest estimate is June 26 for a hardened ASR path, not June 12.

No ask yet, just early warning so the customer-engagement date doesn't get promised against ASR.

Ondrej

subject: Re: Tundra status: detection + SFT hardened, ASR risk materializing
body:
Ondrej, Daniela,

Decisions for the last stretch of Tundra's window:

1. The July 10 customer engagement proceeds on the detection + text SFT paths only. I've re-scoped the statement of work with the customer to a vision-detection deliverable with a text SFT pilot - no ASR commitment. The two-days-setup number sold itself.

2. ASR: Linnea's bucketing sampler landed June 24 and the path is now hardened, but it ships as "beta" in the v1 release. First ASR engagement targets Q3, entered in OKRs before the June 26 lock (done - it's in as a committed line).

3. Scope cut: instance segmentation polish moves to Q3 as well. Detection is the wedge; segmentation follows once revenue is attached.

Carmen - the Swahili demo goes in the customer deck as the i18n proof point. It reads beautifully.

Lucia

subject: Action-Angle Networks kickoff - physics surrogates that respect structure
body:
Team,

Kicking off the Action-Angle Networks evaluation. Scientific-computing prospects keep telling us generic neural surrogates drift on long rollouts because they ignore the physics. Our open-source JAX implementation attacks this by learning dynamics in action-angle coordinates, where the structure of integrable motion is built in rather than hoped for.

What I like operationally: the whole thing is config-driven via ml_collections config_flags - training runs from main.py with a config like configs/action_angle_flow.py, and hyperparameters (num_train_steps, batch_size) override from the command line. That makes systematic benchmarking cheap.

Plan for the window: repro of the paper's systems by March 27; a long-horizon rollout benchmark versus two baseline surrogate families in May; go/no-go on a customer pilot at the June 1 review.

Deshawn - staffing note and compute ask when you can. This is small-compute, the leverage is in careful evaluation.

Anders

subject: Re: Action-Angle Networks kickoff - physics surrogates that respect structure
body:
Anders,

Staffing:

- Nikhil Abebe 40%: method owner, repro and the comparison methodology.
- Saoirse Eriksen 25%: JAX environment + CI so the config-driven runs are reproducible on our infra.
- Wanjiru Horvat 25% from April: baseline surrogate implementations.
- Bilal Novak is committed at 60% to this project for May 2026 - he owns the long-horizon rollout benchmark and the conservation-error tooling, both of which land that month. May is our crunch month and I've planned it entirely around his availability, so treat that allocation as load-bearing.

Compute: trivial by portfolio standards - 8 A100s on titan-a100 best effort covers every sweep we've sketched. The cost center here is engineer time on careful evals, not GPUs.

One process note: the June 1 go/no-go should include an energy-conservation acceptance threshold agreed in advance, otherwise we'll argue about it after the fact.

Deshawn

subject: Re: Action-Angle Networks kickoff - physics surrogates that respect structure
body:
Hi Deshawn, Anders,

Status ahead of the June 1 review. Repro closed March 25. The May benchmark is now mostly in: on the integrable systems, Action-Angle Networks hold energy conservation error under 0.5% out to 1000-step rollouts where our MLP baseline drifts past 12% by step 400 - Bilal's conservation-error tooling makes this a one-command comparison, and the rollout benchmark covers three horizon regimes.

The honest risk for the go/no-go: the advantage is largest exactly where the action-angle assumption holds. On the driven, weakly-dissipative variant we built to mimic the customer's system, the gap narrows a lot - AAN still wins, but by 1.8x rather than 20x on long-horizon error. So the pilot pitch should be scoped to near-integrable regimes, with the dissipative case labeled experimental.

Proposal for Deshawn's pre-agreed threshold: pilot proceeds if conservation error < 2% at 1000 steps on the customer-shaped system. We're currently at 1.4%.

Nikhil

subject: Activation Clustering kickoff - interpretability for the debugging offering
body:
Team,

Kicking off the Activation Clustering evaluation. Context: our model-debugging engagements keep hitting the same wall - customers can see *that* a model fails, not *why*. The activation clustering method from our open-source release (unsupervised clustering over a trained model's activations, per the "Explaining Deep Neural Networks using Unsupervised Clustering" work) gives us cluster-level concepts and similar-image retrieval from any baseline model, which is exactly the missing artifact in those engagements.

The repo is nicely self-contained: docker build, jupyter server in the container, worked CIFAR-10 examples for training an activation clustering model from a baseline and visualizing similar images and concepts.

Window plan: repro + internal-model spike by March 20; utility assessment on two real debugging cases by April 17; productization decision April 30, with the actual productization sprint (if green) planned for June.

Bao - staffing please, including who carries the June sprint if we go.

Anders

subject: Re: Activation Clustering kickoff - interpretability for the debugging offering
body:
Anders,

Staffing for the window: Rafael Duran 40% leads the repro and the two debugging-case studies; Kaia Wolde 25% on evaluation design (she'll define what "the clusters actually helped" means so we're not grading our own homework); Fumiko Rossi 20% advising on cluster-quality methodology through April.

For the June productization sprint: Fumiko Rossi is committed at 60% to this project for June 2026 for the productization sprint - concept-quality metrics and the customer-facing notebook flow - and I've already booked her time with her and put it in the resourcing sheet. Locking that now was the only way to guarantee the sprint doesn't stall while everyone's Q3 spins up.

Compute: negligible - the docker workflow runs on a single 8-GPU node; I'll use the team's standing titan-a100 slice. No budget ask beyond ~$2k for storage of activation dumps on the larger internal models.

Bao

subject: Re: Activation Clustering kickoff - interpretability for the debugging offering
body:
Hi Bao, Anders,

Status ahead of the April 30 decision. Repro was smooth - the CIFAR-10 notebook flow worked out of the docker container basically first try, and the internal-model spike (our retail-vision classifier) produced clusters by March 18.

Results on the two debugging cases, using Kaia's rubric: case 1 (mislabeled-lookalike failure) was a clear win - the activation clusters isolated the confusing concept group in under an hour, versus roughly a day of manual slicing last time we debugged that model. Case 2 (texture-bias failure) was a partial win: the relevant cluster existed, but you had to already suspect texture to spot it, so Kaia scored it "confirmatory, not discovering."

The risk for productization: cluster granularity is a per-model knob, and bad settings produce plausible-looking but useless concepts. The June sprint needs concept-quality metrics as its first deliverable, before any customer-facing polish - otherwise we're shipping a tool that's convincing when it's wrong.

My vote is a green light with that ordering constraint.

Rafael

subject: ASPEST kickoff - abstain smartly, label smartly
body:
Team,

Kicking off the Active Selective Prediction track. The deployment story we keep failing to tell: when a customer's data shifts, their model should (a) know when to abstain and route to a human, and (b) spend the resulting human-labeling budget on the points that fix it fastest. ASPEST, from our open-source release, does both at once - that's the bridge between active learning and selective prediction, and no one else in our stack has it.

The repo ships six shift benchmarks - mnist->svhn, cifar10->cinic10, fmow, amazon_review, domainnet, and otto - four available via TensorFlow Datasets and the rest downloaded manually, with a build_datasets.sh script to standardize everything.

Milestones: benchmark suite built and repro complete in May; integration design with the human-review routing layer by June 19; pilot-ready eval report by July 24, ahead of an LRB slot in early August.

Alina - staffing and compute please. May is the make-or-break month.

Dmitri

subject: Re: ASPEST kickoff - abstain smartly, label smartly
body:
Dmitri,

Plan for the window:

- Ondrej Bergstrom is committed at 60% to this project for May 2026 - he owns the ASPEST repro across all six benchmark pairs, which is the whole May milestone. I've structured the month so nothing else touches him.
- Halima Toure 50% through July: integration design with the human-review routing layer, then the pilot eval methodology.
- Wanjiru Horvat 40%: dataset engineering - the manual downloads (cinic10, the two wilds sets fmow and amazon_review, otto from the competition dump) plus build_datasets.sh runs on our infra, all landing in a shared $DATA_DIR by May 8.

Compute: 48 A100s on titan-a100 best effort; the active-learning loops are many small jobs rather than big ones, so scheduling matters more than raw capacity.

Flag: the repo pins an old Python 3.7 environment; Wanjiru is containerizing it rather than fighting our base image.

Alina

subject: ASPEST status: repro complete on all six benchmarks, coverage-target risk
body:
Hi Alina, Dmitri,

May milestone closed on time: ASPEST reproduced on all six pairs. Headline confirmation - on mnist->svhn with a 100-label budget, ASPEST beats the best pure selective-prediction and pure active-learning baselines on accuracy-coverage tradeoff in our runs, and cifar10->cinic10 shows the same ordering. fmow and domainnet were the fiddly ones (dataset plumbing, not method issues - Wanjiru's containerization saved us there).

The risk to design around: the accuracy-coverage curve is steep near high coverage. On amazon_review, going from 85% to 95% coverage roughly triples the selective risk. If the pilot customer anchors on "95% automation" as the target, the abstention story falls apart on shifted data. Halima and I want the integration design to expose coverage as an explicit SLA knob with the measured risk curve next to it, so the routing layer's staffing model is driven by our numbers rather than wishful defaults.

On track for the June 19 design review.

Ondrej

subject: Re: ASPEST status: repro complete on all six benchmarks, coverage-target risk
body:
All,

Closing decisions ahead of the LRB slot:

1. The pilot eval report shipped July 23, a day early. The coverage-as-SLA framing survived contact with the pilot customer - they picked 88% coverage off the measured amazon_review-style risk curve rather than demanding 95%, which tells me the design does its job. Halima's routing-layer integration doc is the artifact I'll reuse for every future engagement.

2. Scope cut for v1: we ship with four benchmarks in the standard eval battery (mnist->svhn, cifar10->cinic10, amazon_review, otto). fmow and domainnet stay in the extended suite - their build times are too long for the per-engagement loop.

3. Nadia - requesting the August 6 board. Materials: eval report, coverage-SLA design, and the abstention demo. Nothing customer-facing before sign-off, per process.

Strong quarter, this one turned out exactly like the kickoff pitch said it would, which never happens.

Dmitri

subject: Project Basalt kickoff — AdaRank adaptive-rank LoRA
body:
Hi Bruno, all,

Kicking off our adaptive-rank finetuning effort. Internally we refer to this effort as Project Basalt — please use the codename on decks, calendar invites, and doc titles so tracking stays consistent.

Quick framing: LoRA is almost always applied with one rank across every layer, but the transfer-learning evidence says later layers diverge more from pretrained weights during finetuning. AdaRank predicts a per-module rank from model disagreement, and because it leaves pretraining and adaptation completely intact — no extra objectives or regularizers — it can drop straight into our finetuning service without touching customer workflows.

Milestones inside the window: repro of TREC and yelp_polarity results by Feb 27, adapter-service integration spike through March, internal design review the week of Apr 20. I want us in the platform roadmap conversation before Q2 planning starts.

Thanks,
Dmitri

subject: Re: Project Basalt kickoff — AdaRank adaptive-rank LoRA
body:
Dmitri,

Staffing for Basalt: Wei 80% (lead), Tereza 50% on the rank-prediction probes, Emeka 40% on the training harness, Umar advising at 20%. That mix holds through the design review.

Compute: the disagreement probes need multi-seed runs per module, so we'll burst to ~48 A100s on titan-a100 — best-effort is fine, no Vulcan reservation needed. The 12-module rank vectors themselves (e.g. 1,3,7,9,9,8,8,8,8,10,10,8 on value modules) are cheap to train once predicted; the cost is all in the probe sweeps.

One constraint: Emeka rolls off mid-April for an infra rotation, so any harness work needs to land before then.

Bruno

subject: Basalt status: TREC repro + generalization deltas
body:
Hi Dmitri, Bruno,

Status on the repro. TREC label-coarse (6 classes, seed 538, 500 steps, decay at step 200) matches the open-source release: the predicted rank vector 1,3,7,9,9,8,8,8,8,10,10,8 on value modules beats uniform rank-8 by +1.7 accuracy on unseen test data, consistent with the claim that AdaRank generalizes notably better than uniform ranks. yelp_polarity is running now at batch size 256; first numbers Friday.

Risk worth flagging: the disagreement probes add roughly 30% wall-clock ahead of adaptation. For service integration that's the number the platform team will push back on. Tereza is prototyping probe-output caching, which should cut most of it for repeated tasks.

Wei

subject: Re: Basalt status: TREC repro + generalization deltas
body:
Wei, thanks — good numbers.

Decisions from yesterday's sync so we're all on one page:

1. v1 scope is text-classification adapters with value-module replacement only; multimodal adapters move to a Q3 conversation.
2. Probe-output caching is in scope for v1 — the 30% overhead is not sellable to the platform team without it.
3. Design review is Apr 29; Bruno owns the deck, I'll cover the roadmap slide.

No Launch Review Board pass needed since this stays internal for now. Nice work getting the repro locked before the yelp numbers even landed.

Dmitri

subject: Kickoff: after-kernel invariance diagnostics
body:
Hi Santiago, team,

Kicking off the after-kernel study. The one-liner: the after kernel is like the neural tangent kernel, but computed after training — and comparing the two tells us which invariances a trained network actually acquired versus inherited. The experiment suite measures invariance to translations, zooms, quadrant swaps of the input image, and rotations.

Why product cares: if this holds up, it becomes a model-diagnostics report we can attach to every finetuned model — a trust signal customers keep asking for.

Milestones: MNIST 3-vs-8 binary study complete by end of March, invariance report template mid-April, readout to Hana's staff the week of May 11.

Priya

subject: Re: Kickoff: after-kernel invariance diagnostics
body:
Priya,

Resourcing picture. Freya leads at 60%; Umar advises at 15% on the kernel-alignment methodology. Nothing on the shelf covers kernel-level invariance metrics, so we are scoping and staffing an internal evaluation harness built from scratch — Jorge at 50% and Saoirse at 40% own it, first cut end of March.

Compute is modest by our standards — the kernel computations batch well, so 8 A100s on titan-a100 best-effort covers the sweeps; no reservation request needed.

One dependency: the invariance sweeps (num_translations=1000 per model, plus the zoom and swap grids) multiply quickly across seeds, so the harness needs to land before the full grid or Freya ends up serializing runs by hand.

Santiago

subject: After-kernel status: MNIST 3-vs-8 invariance results
body:
Hi both,

Status. On MNIST 3-vs-8 after 10 epochs of training, the after kernel is measurably more translation-invariant than the kernel at initialization — evaluated over num_translations=1000 test examples — and the gap widens if we train down to the training_loss_target instead of stopping at max_num_epochs. Quadrant-swap invariance shows the same direction with a weaker effect.

Risk: the rotation sweep is the expensive corner. num_rotations at the sample sizes we'd need roughly doubles the grid, and the stopping criteria differ across seeds (loss target vs epoch cap), which makes those comparisons noisy. Recommend we decide next week whether rotations make report v1.

Freya

subject: Re: After-kernel status: MNIST 3-vs-8 invariance results
body:
Freya, Santiago,

Decision on scope, following Monday's sync: rotation invariance is out of report v1. We keep translation, zoom, and quadrant-swap — those three already tell the diagnostics story, and the rotation grid would push the readout past the window. Rotations go on the backlog together with the seed stopping-criterion fix.

The harness stays in scope; it's the piece that makes this repeatable for every future finetune, and it's most of the reason this becomes a product surface rather than a one-off repro.

Readout confirmed for May 14, Hana's staff. Freya, send me the three headline plots by May 11 and I'll build the deck around them.

Priya

subject: Kickoff: Agile Deliberation — concept deliberation for subjective visual classification
body:
Hi Bao, team,

Kickoff for Agile Deliberation. This is the human-in-the-loop framework for classifying subjective, evolving visual concepts: structured concept scoping up front, then the system iteratively surfaces borderline examples so raters can sharpen their own ambiguous mental models. The released notebook walks the whole deliberation flow end to end.

Product framing: our rater-tooling group struggles most on exactly these subjective concepts, so the pilot is a concept-deliberation add-on for their queue.

Milestones: FAISS nearest-neighbor index over the Laion400M training slice by mid-April, an eight-rater internal pilot in early May, readout before the window closes May 25.

Dmitri

subject: Re: Kickoff: Agile Deliberation — concept deliberation for subjective visual classification
body:
Dmitri,

Staffing: Yusuf leads at 70%, Nikhil 50% on the deliberation loop, Quentin 30% on rater UX. The Laion400M slice is full of near-duplicates, which poisons the borderline-example queue, so we are scoping and staffing a dataset de-duplication pipeline built from scratch — Giannis owns the build at 50% through April.

Compute: faiss-gpu on 4 A100s for index build and retrieval; the faiss-cpu fallback is fine for notebook demos. Storage ask into Corpus for the index shards is ~3TB — quota request is filed.

Sequencing note: dedup has to finish before the pilot, otherwise raters see the same borderline image four times and the agreement numbers are garbage.

Bao

subject: Agile Deliberation status: index built, early pilot signal
body:
Hi Dmitri, Bao,

Status. Index is built — setup.sh reproduces the file layout and the FAISS index over the training slice, and Demo.ipynb runs end to end on the internal mirror. Early pilot signal is genuinely encouraging: surfacing borderline examples for reflection moved inter-rater agreement +0.11 kappa on the two subjective concepts we tested, which is exactly the mechanism the deliberation framework is meant to exercise.

Risk: at full 400M scale the faiss-gpu index doesn't fit a single card; we're testing a sharded index across the 4 A100s. If that stalls, fallback is faiss-cpu with ~6x slower retrieval, which the rater UI can absorb but won't enjoy.

Yusuf

subject: Re: Agile Deliberation status: index built, early pilot signal
body:
Yusuf, thanks.

Decisions from the pilot review:

1. Pilot extends to three concepts and twelve raters through end of May; the agreement delta stays the headline metric.
2. We defer the full 400M index — the sharded build keeps eating your time, and the pilot runs fine on the 40M subsample. Revisit in Q3 planning.
3. Quentin writes up the deliberation-flow findings for the rater-tooling leads by May 22; I take the readout on May 25.

Good project — the kappa movement is the strongest tooling result this quarter in the portfolio.

Dmitri

subject: Kickoff: Agile Modeling — concept to classifier in minutes
body:
Hi Alina, team,

Kicking off Agile Modeling. The promise: a user with no ML experience goes from a concept in their head to a working image classifier in minutes. The open-source release includes the end-to-end notebook flow plus all user-labeled data for the 14 concepts from the experiments, which gives us a ready-made regression eval.

Product goal: a self-serve classifier builder for internal ops teams, alpha in early August.

Milestones: unlabeled-pool prep from LAION-400M in June, embedding precompute in July, internal alpha the week of Aug 3. Note Q3 OKR planning locks 2026-06-26 — I want the alpha on that list.

Dmitri

subject: Re: Kickoff: Agile Modeling — concept to classifier in minutes
body:
Dmitri,

Resourcing. Maren 60% on the pool pipeline, Vera 50% on the labeling loop, Linnea 50% on model training. We're pinning TensorFlow 2.13.0 to match the release; the Python version drift is the usual pain but manageable.

Compute: For the LAION-400M embedding precompute we hold the cirrus-tpu reservation for the week of 2026-07-06 — 128 accelerators — so the pool is ready well before the alpha. Titan covers everything else best-effort.

Ask: the LAION download and preprocessing (per the Demo.ipynb instructions) needs ~8TB of staging on Corpus — filing the quota this week. If quota slips, pool prep slips a week and the whole back half compresses.

Alina

subject: Agile Modeling status: end-to-end flow live, alpha metric needed
body:
Hi Dmitri, Alina,

Status. The end-to-end flow works on the internal mirror: concept in, a few labeling rounds, working classifier out — about 20 minutes wall-clock for our test users, which matches the concept-to-classifier-in-minutes pitch. The 14-concept user-labeled data is mirrored and is now our regression eval; we track mean AP across concepts.

Risk for the OKR lock on 2026-06-26: we need to commit to an alpha metric now. I propose mean AP >= 0.75 across the 14 concepts plus time-to-first-classifier under 30 minutes. If we don't lock a number this week we'll get one assigned to us.

Vera

subject: Re: Agile Modeling status: end-to-end flow live, alpha metric needed
body:
Vera, Alina,

Post-precompute decisions. The embedding run over the unlabeled pool finished on Cirrus during our reserved week, so the pool is live — nice execution.

Scope call for the alpha: we go with six concepts, not fourteen. The other eight stay in the regression eval, but the alpha UX only ships the six with mean AP above 0.78. Time-to-first-classifier target stays under 30 minutes.

Linnea owns the alpha build, Maren keeps the pool refresh weekly. Alpha demo for Hana's staff the week of Aug 3, which keeps us inside the window with margin.

Dmitri

subject: Kickoff: active learning for free-energy prediction
body:
Hi Santiago, team,

Kicking off the active-learning-for-FEP work. The nice property of this codebase is that the whole active learning cycle is defined by a single ConfigDict configuration file — model_config, features, targets, selection_config — and you can override any parameter from the command line. That means the loop is a config artifact, not a codebase fork, which is exactly what our screening partners need.

Product framing: a configurable screening loop where a partner points at a CSV of SMILES and gets an acquisition-ranked list back.

Milestones: baseline cycles reproduced by mid-May, greedy vs. alternative selection comparison in June, internal readout the week of July 6.

Anders

subject: Re: Kickoff: active learning for free-energy prediction
body:
Anders,

Staffing and budget. Ondrej leads at 60%, Paloma 40% on the config/feature plumbing, Maren 25% on the data pipeline for the SMILES ingest.

On budget: Idris walked me through it and verbally earmarked the full $120k from Q3 discretionary compute budget line B-19 for this project, so the retraining cycles are funded. We'll spend most of it on the retraining sweeps — each cycle retrains the model from scratch on the accumulated pool, and with the sklearn-side tuning_hyperparameters search space that adds up faster than people expect.

Compute is CPU-heavy rather than GPU-heavy: Morgan fingerprint featurization (fingerprint_size/fingerprint_radius sweeps) and ElasticNet fits parallelize on the general pool. Small GPU ask only for the neural baselines.

Santiago

subject: AL-for-FEP status: baseline cycles + selection strategy risk
body:
Hi Anders, Santiago,

Status. Baseline cycles reproduce. With Morgan fingerprints at radius 2 / 2048 bits and ElasticNet (l1_ratio tuned via the tuning_hyperparameters block), greedy selection reaches the target correlation in 6 cycles versus 11 for random acquisition — a solid 45% reduction in simulated assay spend.

Risk: greedy selection_type collapses diversity. By cycle 4 it's picking near-identical scaffolds, and the held-out error on novel chemotypes actually degrades. Paloma is adding a batch-diversity term through the selection hyperparameters, which the config format supports without touching the cycle code.

We should decide by late June whether greedy alone is the shipped default.

Ondrej

subject: Re: AL-for-FEP status: baseline cycles + selection strategy risk
body:
Ondrej, Santiago,

Decisions ahead of the readout:

1. Shipped default becomes greedy-with-diversity, not plain greedy. The novel-chemotype degradation is the exact failure a screening partner would notice first.
2. Neural model baselines are cut from the July readout — the ElasticNet + fingerprint story is complete and the neural runs aren't ready. They move to the Q3 backlog.
3. Paloma publishes the reference ConfigDict for both selection modes so partners can diff them.

Readout July 13 as planned. Ondrej, the 6-vs-11 cycle number is the slide; everything else is supporting.

Anders

subject: Kickoff: ALOE — discrete energy-based models via local exploration
body:
Hi Ivo, team,

Kicking off our ALOE effort — learning discrete energy-based models via auxiliary-variable local exploration. We're calling this Project Sirocco internally — the codename is already on the fuzzing workstream docs and the compute request, so let's keep it consistent everywhere.

Two tracks. The synthetic track (run_varlen.sh) gives us training, sampling, heat-map visualization, and MMD checks on held-out sets with either linear or hamming kernels — that's our correctness harness. The applied track is fuzzing: take raw seed inputs from an OSS-Fuzz-style corpus and learn a generative model over structured inputs. That second one is where a product lives, as a smarter seed generator for our own fuzzing infra.

Milestones: synthetic repro plus MMD parity by end of May, fuzzing seed model in June, readout the week of July 20.

Dmitri

subject: Re: Kickoff: ALOE — discrete energy-based models via local exploration
body:
Dmitri,

Staffing for Sirocco: Hyun leads at 70%, Kaia 50% on the energy model and sampler, Bilal 40% on the fuzzing harness and seed ingest, Yusuf 20% advisory on evaluation.

Compute: 32 A100s on titan-a100 best-effort. The synthetic runs are small (500 epochs on the varlen configs finishes overnight), but the fuzzing track needs a Docker-capable pool to build the LibFuzzer binaries and collect seed inputs — that's an infra ask, not a GPU ask, and I've opened it with Ines.

Flagging: pretrained model dumps and data have to be mirrored internally before Bilal can start. Kaia is doing that this week.

Ivo

subject: Sirocco status: synthetic MMD parity, fuzzing track slower
body:
Hi Dmitri, Ivo,

Status. Synthetic track is done: after 500 epochs on the varlen configs, held-out MMD under the hamming kernel matches the published numbers within noise, and the learned heat maps look right under plot phase. Linear-kernel MMD is slightly better than reported, likely a seed effect.

Risk on the fuzzing track. Getting usable raw seed inputs out of the LibFuzzer setup is taking Bilal much longer than scoped — the docker build and seed extraction are two weeks in with partial coverage on three targets. Sampling itself is fine; it's the corpus plumbing. If this doesn't converge by early July, I'd rather cut the fuzzing demo than have a half-evaluated claim in the readout.

Hyun

subject: Re: Sirocco status: synthetic MMD parity, fuzzing track slower
body:
Hyun, Ivo,

Taking your recommendation. Scope cut for Sirocco:

1. The July 20 readout covers the synthetic track only — MMD parity on held-out sets, the heat maps, the sampler. That's a clean, defensible result.
2. Fuzzing becomes an appendix slide: three targets, seed generation working, no comparative claim against the existing fuzzer.
3. Bilal drops to 20% on corpus plumbing after the readout and picks it back up if Q3 planning funds it.

I'd rather ship one complete result than two partial ones. Thanks for calling it early instead of at the deadline.

Dmitri

subject: Kickoff: ALX — large-scale matrix factorization on TPUs
body:
Hi Bruno, team,

Kicking off ALX. It's a JAX library for distributed matrix factorization with Alternating Least Squares, designed around the TPU architecture — it scales to problems with billions of rows/columns by scaling the number of TPU cores.

Why we care: our internal recommendation surfaces still run a factorization job that takes eleven hours and can't grow. If ALX gives us the same Recall@20 in a fraction of the time, that's a straight infrastructure win we can bank this half.

Milestones: single-pod training loop with checkpoint/restore by mid-April, scaling study across core counts in May, Recall@20 and Recall@50 comparison against the incumbent by end of May, decision June 1.

Priya

subject: Re: Kickoff: ALX — large-scale matrix factorization on TPUs
body:
Priya,

Staffing. Maren 50% on the data pipeline (build_datasets and the eval splits), Linnea 50% on the training loop and checkpointing, Wanjiru 40% on the scaling harness, Ondrej 20% advisory.

Rafael Duran is committed at 60% to ALX for May 2026 — he owns the sharded ALS solver work and that allocation is what the May milestone is built on. Without him at that level the scaling study slides into June and we miss the June 1 decision date.

Compute: Cirrus TPU allocation from the language portfolio quarterly pool. We start at 32 cores for the training loop and step up through the scaling study; peak ask is 256 cores for two days in mid-May.

Bruno

subject: ALX status: scaling looks right, checkpoint restore is the risk
body:
Hi Priya, Bruno,
