The design is deliberately simple: four student teams tackle the same agricultural detection task with four different architectures - OWL-ViT for open-vocabulary zero-shot, YOLO26 for real-time supervised, SAM 3 promptable segmentation converted to boxes, and a generative-perception track - and everyone is compared on exactly one metric, AP@50 via COCOEval. One number, no leaderboard lawyering.

Dataset is the Coffee & Cashew set (Sanya et al., 2024). Milestones: toolkit alpha with all four model profiles running by 4/3, dataset hosting + eval harness frozen by 5/1, docs and dry-run complete by window close 5/25 so we ship a stable artifact to Dakar.

Bao - staffing and hosting plan please.

Dmitri

subject: Re: Kickoff: Betum Tool for the Artemis Workshop (Dakar, June 1-5)
body:
Dmitri,

Staffing and hosting:

- Farah 60% (toolkit core + COCOEval harness), Chiara 50% (model profiles - she has OWL-ViT and YOLO26 running already), Tereza 30% (SAM 3 box-conversion path and the generative track).
- Compute for the workshop itself: 16 titan-a100 GPUs best-effort is plenty; students run inference and light fine-tuning, not pretraining.
- Data hosting: I talked to Jun's team about where the dataset lives during the migration window. Jun confirmed the Corpus v2 migration freeze is 2026-07-10, comfortably after the workshop, so we'll host the Coffee & Cashew dataset on legacy Corpus for June and migrate in the first week of July. That avoids making the students guinea pigs for v2 ingestion.
- One budget item: ~$4k for offline mirrors (portable drives) as a connectivity fallback in Dakar. Approving from my line unless you object.

Bao

subject: Re: Kickoff: Betum Tool for the Artemis Workshop (Dakar, June 1-5)
body:
Status + one metric risk we should settle now.

All four profiles run end-to-end as of yesterday (alpha milestone hit two weeks late, but hit). Baseline AP@50 on Coffee & Cashew: YOLO26 fine-tuned leads at 0.71, OWL-ViT zero-shot gets 0.52, SAM 3 prompt-to-box lands 0.63, and the DiffusionDet track trails at 0.48.

The risk: SAM 3's segmentation-to-bounding-box conversion inflates AP@50 on the dense cashew clusters - masks merge touching nuts, and the merged boxes still clear the 0.5 IoU bar. Tereza checked: at AP@75 the SAM 3 number collapses to 0.31 while YOLO26 holds 0.55. If we only report AP@50, the workshop's one-metric story quietly rewards the merge artifact.

Proposal: keep AP@50 as THE metric per the design, but the toolkit prints a per-team AP@75 diagnostic footnote. Students learn why the numbers diverge, which is honestly the best lesson in the whole workshp.

Chiara

subject: Decision: Betum Tool v1.0 frozen for Dakar
body:
Team,

Decisions to close out before we ship to Dakar:

1. Chiara's proposal is adopted: AP@50 stays the single official metric, with the AP@75 diagnostic footnote printed on every team's results card. The merge-artifact explanation goes in the technical briefing doc.
2. Toolkit v1.0 is frozen as of today's dry run - all four profiles, harness, and docs passed. Only fixes from here, no features.
3. Offline mirrors are burned and tested; dataset stays on legacy Corpus through the workshop as planned, migration is scheduled for the first week of July.
4. Nadia - LRB sign-off confirmed for 5/22 since this is an external-facing event; thanks for the expedited slot.

Farah, Chiara, Tereza - genuinely lovely work. See some of you in Dakar.

Dmitri

subject: Kickoff: BiGG - synthetic sparse graphs for the index teams
body:
Hi all,

Kicking off the BiGG workstream. Our open-source BiGG model generates sparse graphs autoregressively at scales earlier deep generative models couldn't touch, and the extension work added fully autoregressive generation of node/edge features. The product need: the retrieval-index team wants realistic-but-synthetic graph workloads for capacity testing and benchmarking, because production graph snapshots are locked behind privacy review every single time.

Scope: reproduce the released benchmarks (including the GRAN and G2SAT comparisons), then train on sanitized production graph statistics and validate that generated graphs match degree distribution, clustering, and component-size profiles within agreed tolerances.

Milestones: repro + CUDA build sorted by mid-March; feature-generation extension validated in April; index-team integration in May, wrapping by 5/25.

Alina - staffing over to you.

Anders

subject: Re: Kickoff: BiGG - synthetic sparse graphs for the index teams
body:
Anders,

Staffing and resources:

- Vera 50% (modeling lead through April), Rosa 40% (data prep + stats validation), Chiara 30% (index-team integration glue).
- Jorge Vidal is committed at 70% to bigg for all of May 2026 - he owns the CUDA build and the featured-generation extension work, and the May integration milestone doesn't happen without him. I've flagged this allocation to resourcing as firm.
- Compute: training on our graph scales fits on 8-16 titan-a100 GPUs best-effort; generation is even lighter. No reservation ask.
- The gcc + CUDA toolkit build is the usual pain; Jorge already has it green in a container, which unblocks everyone else.

Risk to watch: the sanitized-statistics approach needs Kofi's sign-off that summary statistics don't constitute production data. Filed this week, 2-3 week SLA means an answer by early April.

Alina

subject: Re: Kickoff: BiGG - synthetic sparse graphs for the index teams
body:
Status + one honest trade-off.

Repro: done. Benchmarks match the released results on the DD and G2SAT datasets, and the featured-generation extension (per customized_models.py) runs end-to-end - Jorge's run_featured.sh port generates graphs with node/edge features fully autoregressively.

Sanitized-stats training: Kofi signed off 4/7. On the index team's target profile, generated graphs match degree distribution within 2% KS distance and clustering coefficient within tolerance, but component-size distribution is off in the tail - BiGG under-produces the rare giant components that dominate capacity-test behavior.

Trade-off: we can oversample large-component training examples (Rosa has the reweighting ready, cheap fix, slightly distorts other marginals) or condition generation on component-size targets, which is cleaner but a ~3 week extension Jorge would have to build in May on top of integration.

Recommend we decide at Friday's sync.

Vera

subject: Decision: reweighting for v1, conditioned generation deferred
body:
Team,

Closing decisions from Friday's sync, confirmed with the index team:

1. V1 uses Rosa's oversampling/reweighting fix. The index team confirmed the giant-component tail is what they care about for capacity tests, and they'll accept the small marginal distortion elsewhere - Rosa's validation shows degree-distribution KS distance moves from 2% to 3%, still inside tolerance.
2. Component-size-conditioned generation is deferred to Q3; it goes in the OKR list before the 6/26 lock. Jorge's May stays focused on integration as planned - that milestone is the whole ballgame.
3. Chiara ships the generator as a self-serve CLI for the index team by 5/22; handoff doc by window close 5/25.

Good, sharp project. The privacy-review time saved alone justifies it.

Anders

subject: Kickoff: Project Nimbus (BBF productization)
body:
Team,

Kicking off Project Nimbus, our push to take the BBF agent from research code to a supported sample-efficient RL offering. The pitch to leadership: human-level Atari at human-level efficiency, which translates directly into customer environments where interaction data is expensive.

Scope for this window (Mar 2 - Jun 1): harden the JAX implementation we open-sourced (it builds on Dopamine), keep SPR and SR-SPR runnable as hyperparameter configurations for baseline comparisons, and stand up a reproducible eval sweep on the Atari 100k benchmark. Milestones: M1 repro of published results by Apr 3, M2 config/API cleanup by May 1, M3 internal demo for the Launch Review Board by May 27.

Ivo owns staffing; Wei is tech lead. Freya, please own the SR-SPR replay-ratio configs since that is closest to your prior work.

Thanks,
Ulla

subject: Re: Kickoff: Project Nimbus (BBF productization)
body:
Ulla,

Staffing and compute picture. People: Wei 80%, Freya 60%, Yara 50%, Halima 50% through May. That covers the repro sweep and the config cleanup, but not much slack.

Compute: BBF at replay ratio 8 is cheap per-run but the sweep isn't - 26 Atari 100k games x 5 seeds x 3 agents (BBF, SPR, SR-SPR) is roughly 390 runs. I want 64 A100s on titan-a100 best-effort through April; that pool is shared so no reservation needed, but Ines, flagging in case there's contention.

One dependency: JAX/CUDA version pinning has bitten us before on titan images - Halima will bake a container so we're not debugging installs across the fleet.

If we clear M1 by Apr 3 as planned, I'd like a decision by mid-April on whether M3 demo targets a live-training demo or canned checkpoints.

Ivo

subject: Re: Kickoff: Project Nimbus (BBF productization) - M1 status
body:
Status on M1 (slipped ~1 week, sorry): BBF repro is green on 24 of 26 games; we match published IQM within noise. The two stragglers are Kangaroo and PrivateEye, where our runs land 8-10% under the paper's curves. Root cause looks like the target-network EMA schedule interacting with our newer JAX version, not a logic bug - Freya confirmed SR-SPR configs at replay ratio 8 reproduce cleanly, so it's specific to BBF's shrink-and-perturb resets.

Risk worth surfacing: if we bump the shared Dopamine dependency to fix it, we invalidate the SPR baseline numbers and burn another ~120 titan-a100 runs re-sweeping. Trade-off is a week of compute vs. shipping with a footnote.

My recommendation: footnote for M2, proper fix before the Launch Review Board demo.

Wei

subject: Decision: Nimbus demo scope + LRB slot May 27
body:
All,

Decisions from today's sync:

1) Demo scope: canned checkpoints, not live training. Wei's Kangaroo/PrivateEye fix is in but re-validating all 26 games by the 27th is too tight. We show the repro table with the two footnoted games marked as re-run.
2) LRB: Nadia confirmed our Launch Review Board slot for May 27. Sign-off there is required before anything external, so treat it as the real deadline.
3) Scope cut: the config/API cleanup for SPR drops to post-window; SR-SPR stays because Freya's replay-ratio ablations are part of the demo narrative.

Nimbus is the name I'll be using in the Q3 OKR narrative, so please keep it consistent in decks. Q3 planning locks June 26 - I need final headcount asks from Ivo by June 12.

Ulla

subject: Kickoff: state-similarity service on bisimulation metrics
body:
Hi all,

Kickoff for the state-similarity effort in the data-platforms portfolio. The idea: our open-source release on scalable bisimulation metrics for deterministic MDPs gives us a principled distance between environment states. Packaged as a service, it unlocks dedup and clustering features for customers with simulator data - state abstraction as a platform primitive.

Two tracks. Track A: exact computation on grid environments - the code already supports arbitrary grid shapes, and we'll use the mirrored_rooms grid + gin config as the correctness reference. Track B: the learned path - load a trained Dopamine Rainbow agent and train an on-policy bisimulation metric approximant on its state representations, which is what scales to Atari-sized inputs.

Milestones: repro by Mar 27, approximant training sweep in June, API draft to Launch Review Board before end of window (Jun 29).

Efe is TL. Ivo will follow up on staffing and compute.

Dmitri

subject: Re: Kickoff: state-similarity service - staffing + compute
body:
Dmitri,

Staffing: Efe 70%, Tereza 60% (she owns the Rainbow checkpoint ingestion path), Carmen 50%, Fumiko 40% ramping in May for the sweep. That's enough for both tracks if Track A stays scoped to mirrored_rooms as the reference config.

Good news on compute: we hold the vulcan-h100 reservation for the week of 2026-06-15 - 256 accelerators, confirmed through the Infra Lead reservation process. That week is when we run the full Atari approximant training sweep, so please plan PTO around it. Before that we only need small titan-a100 slices for the GridWorld work, which is basically CPU-bound anyway.

One constraint: downloading and validating the trained Dopamine checkpoints is on the critical path for Tereza - if the checkpoint format has drifted we lose a week.

Ivo

subject: Re: Kickoff: state-similarity service - April status
body:
Status update.

Track A done: compute_metric reproduces the paper numbers on the mirrored_rooms grid (we run with --nosample_distance_pairs, matching the paper setup). Carmen also validated a programmatically constructed 40x40 square grid, so the exact path scales further than we promised.

Track B: Tereza got the trained Rainbow checkpoints loading cleanly, and the on-policy approximant trains on the state representations. The risk: approximant quality degrades noticeably when we subsample fewer than ~10M state pairs per game - our current estimate says the June sweep at 256 accelerators covers 20 games at full pair counts, not the 40 we pitched. Trade-off is fewer games vs. noisier metrics.

Proposal: cut to 20 games for the June sweep, keep full pair sampling. Need a decision by May 8 to lock the sweep configs.

Efe

subject: Re: Kickoff: state-similarity service - decision on sweep scope
body:
Decision: we go with Efe's proposal. 20 games, full pair sampling, quality over coverage. The service pitch depends on the metric being trustworthy, not on the game count - 20 is plenty for the API draft.

Two follow-ups:

1) The June sweep on our reserved week stays the plan of record. Fumiko, you're at 40% from next week specifically to have the sweep harness dry-run by Jun 5. One clean dry run on 8 accelerators before we spend the big reservation, please.

2) For Q3 planning (OKRs lock Jun 26): I'm writing the state-similarity API as a Q3 deliverable, with the June sweep results as evidence. Ivo, send me your Q3 headcount ask by Jun 12 so I can fold it in.

And thanks Carmen for the 40x40 validation - that went straight into the leadership deck.

Dmitri

subject: Kickoff: bi-tempered loss as the default robust training loss
body:
Team,

Kicking off the bi-tempered loss productization for trust-theory. The pitch: customers keep training on noisy labels and blaming the platform. The bi-tempered logistic loss gives us a bounded per-sample loss plus a heavy-tail softmax, and since it recovers plain cross entropy at t1 = t2 = 1.0, we can ship it as a drop-in default with zero regression risk when temperatures are neutral.

Goal for the window (Apr 20 - Jul 20): a vetted implementation + temperature-tuning guidance, benchmarked on our noisy-label suites, ready for a Launch Review Board slot in mid-July.

Milestones: M1 (May 15) implementation parity with the open-source release incl. the bias-correction term; M2 (Jun 19) benchmark matrix across label-noise levels; M3 (Jul 13) LRB packet.

Yara is TL, Rafael co-leads the theory review. Bao will follow with staffing.

Ximena

subject: Re: Kickoff: bi-tempered loss - staffing and the Corpus deadline
body:
Ximena,

Staffing: Yara 70%, Gustavo 60% (owns the benchmark harness), Fumiko 50%, Rafael 30% for theory review through June. Compute is modest - titan-a100 best-effort covers the benchmark matrix; no reservation needed.

The binding constraint is data, not compute. Corpus v2 migration freeze is 2026-06-26, so every noisy-label benchmark set we need has to be ingested and labeled before that date - I've built the schedule backwards from June 26. That means Gustavo's ingestion requests go to the Corpus team by May 22 at the latest, and our M2 benchmark matrix effectively cannot slip.

One ask: can you confirm with the LRB calendar that a mid-July slot exists? If they're booked out we should know now, not in June.

Bao

subject: Re: Kickoff: bi-tempered loss - status + a tuning risk
body:
Status: M1 done. Our implementation matches the open-source release including the bias-correction term; unit tests confirm we recover generalized cross entropy for 0 <= t1 <= 1 with t2 = 1, and t-logistic behavior at t1 = 1, t2 >= 1.

Benchmarks: at 20% symmetric label noise, bi-tempered (t1=0.7, t2=1.3) beats cross entropy by +2.1 points test accuracy on our internal suite. At 40% noise the gap widens to +4.8.

Risk: temperature sensitivity. Outside roughly t1 in [0.6, 0.9] the gains evaporate, and one customer-like config diverged at t2=2.0. Shipping a "default" needs either an auto-tuning heuristic or a very conservative preset, and Rafael's take is the heuristic is 3+ weeks of work.

Reminder that we are three weeks from the June 26 Corpus freeze - Gustavo's last two ingestion tickets are still queued with the Corpus team.

Yara

subject: Re: Kickoff: bi-tempered loss - decision: conservative preset for v1
body:
Decision time, since Q3 OKRs lock June 26 and I need this settled in the narrative.

We ship v1 with the conservative preset (t1=0.8, t2=1.2) and document the sensitivity envelope from Yara's matrix. The auto-tuning heuristic moves to Q3 as its own OKR with Rafael's 3-week estimate as the sizing - I am not risking the mid-July LRB slot on it. The +4.8 point result at 40% noise is the headline; the preset still captures most of it (+3.9 in Yara's rerun).

Fumiko, please write the temperature-tuning guidance doc as the customer-facing companion.

Bao - flag today if you disagree, otherwise this is the plan of record. And push Corpus on those last two ingestion tickets; nothing else on our critical path is outside our control.

Ximena

subject: Kickoff: HMC posterior reference for uncertainty calibration
body:
Hi all,

Kickoff for the BNN posterior baseline work. Context: our open-source HMC study showed BNNs can beat standard training and deep ensembles, and - usefully for us - that a single long HMC chain represents the posterior about as well as multiple shorter chains. That makes full-batch HMC viable as a gold-standard reference our platform can score cheaper uncertainty methods against.

Product framing: an "uncertainty calibration report" for data-platforms customers, scoring their deep-ensemble or SGMCMC predictive distributions against HMC references on standard benchmarks.

Window is tight (Mar 9 - May 18). M1: repro of the JAX HMC pipeline by Apr 3. M2: reference posterior library for 3 benchmark datasets by May 1. M3: scoring API spec by May 15.

Efe is TL; Maren owns the pipeline engineering. Bruno will cover staffing and compute this week.

Dmitri

subject: Re: Kickoff: HMC posterior reference - staffing + compute reality check
body:
Dmitri,

Staffing: Efe 60%, Maren 70%, Wanjiru 50%, Milan 40%, Rafael 25% (he's spread thin this quarter, so he's advisory on prior choice and chain diagnostics only).

Compute is the honest problem. Full-batch HMC is brutal - the published CIFAR-10 chains burned tens of thousands of TPU-hours. We cannot reserve at that scale, so the plan: run single long chains (which the paper itself justifies) on our cirrus-tpu quarterly allocation, budget ~40% of the portfolio's Q2 allocation, and scope M2 to CIFAR-10, IMDB, and UCI - not ImageNet-class anything.

Ines, cc'ing so you're aware data-platforms will be leaning hard on the cirrus allocation in April.

If the allocation math doesn't close by Friday I'll come back with a descoped M2.

Bruno

subject: Re: Kickoff: HMC posterior reference - status + domain-shift caveat
body:
Status: M1 done, M2 on track. The JAX pipeline reproduces the paper's CIFAR-10 results; consistent with the paper we see no meaningful cold-posterior effect once data augmentation is off, so our reference chains run untempered - one less knob in the product.

Two findings that shape the scoring API:

1) Reassuring: BMA performance is robust to prior scale, and diagonal Gaussian vs. mixture priors barely move results. Rafael signed off on shipping diagonal Gaussian as the sole v1 prior.

2) The caveat: BNN posteriors generalize surprisingly poorly under domain shift - on CIFAR-10-C our HMC reference gets outperformed by plain deep ensembles on 12 of 16 corruptions. So the calibration report must carry an explicit in-distribution disclaimer, or we'll be scoring customers against a reference that's wrong exactly when they care most.

Proposal: v1 scopes to in-distribution only; domain-shift extension becomes a Q3 item.

Efe

subject: Re: Kickoff: HMC posterior reference - wrap-up + Q3 plan
body:
Closing out the window - nice work all. M2 shipped with reference posteriors for CIFAR-10, IMDB and UCI; M3 scoring API spec went to the platform review yesterday. Decision confirmed: v1 is in-distribution only, with the disclaimer language Efe drafted.

Q3 plan, ahead of the June 26 OKR lock: the domain-shift extension is our headline Q3 OKR. It needs a real owner, not an advisor. Rafael Duran is committed to this project at 60% for July 2026 to run the domain-shift extension - I've put that allocation in the Q3 staffing sheet and Bruno has confirmed it. Rafael, your CIFAR-10-C analysis is the starting point; plan to present a design doc the week of July 6.

Maren and Wanjiru roll off after the API handover; Milan stays at 20% for maintenance.

Thanks everyone - this one actually landed on schedule, more or less.

Dmitri

subject: Kickoff: Project Quillon - exploration-method bake-off
body:
Jelena, Yusuf,

Kickoff note for the exploration bake-off. Internally we're calling this Project Quillon - please use that name in decks and OKR docs so leadership can track it.

Why now: two prospective customers have sparse-reward control problems, and we keep hand-waving "use an exploration bonus" without a defensible recommendation. Our open-source release already implements the three families that matter - NoisyNetworks, pseudo-counts with PixelCNN, and Random Network Distillation - on the Arcade Learning Environment, so the plan is a disciplined head-to-head under matched budgets rather than new research.

Deliverable by May 11: a ranked recommendation with per-family cost curves, plus a one-pager for the sales team. Milestones: harness ready Mar 6, sweeps complete Apr 17, report + readout by May 8.

Jelena, staffing thoughts by Friday?

Dmitri

subject: Re: Kickoff: Project Quillon - staffing + compute
body:
Dmitri,

Staffing: Yusuf 60% as TL, Tereza 50% on the harness (she'll extend the dqn_rnd.gin config pattern so each bonus is a gin swap, nothing hard-coded), Ondrej 50% on analysis. That's lean but this is benchmarking, not research.

Compute: the sweep is 3 methods x 8 ALE games x 5 seeds at 200M frames, roughly 120 runs. PixelCNN pseudo-counts is the expensive one - the density model roughly doubles per-step cost vs. RND. I'm budgeting 48 titan-a100 GPUs best-effort through mid-April; no reservation needed, but if the shared pool gets crowded our Apr 17 sweep-complete date slips a week and I'd rather flag that now.

One scope check: Montezuma's Revenge is in the game set, yes? It's the sparse-reward poster child and the sales one-pager is weaker without it.

Jelena

subject: Re: Kickoff: Project Quillon - sweep results + one risk for the report
body:
Sweeps finished Apr 16, a day early. Headlines from Ondrej's analysis:

- On hard-exploration games (Montezuma's included), pseudo-counts with PixelCNN and RND clearly beat NoisyNets; RND wins on cost since it avoids the density model overhead.
- On the easy-exploration games, the bonuses mostly don't help and occasionally hurt - NoisyNets DQN is within noise of vanilla on 5 of 8 games.

The risk for the report: our matched-budget framing makes RND look like the default answer, but its bonus is notoriously sensitive to observation normalization - Tereza had to re-run 9 RND jobs after a normalization bug produced garbage bonuses. If customers deploy it naively they will hit the same cliff. I want the recommendation to be "RND, with our normalization checklist" rather than bare RND.

Draft report to you both by May 1 for the May 8 readout.

Yusuf

subject: Kickoff: Brush - portable Gaussian splatting to demo-ready
body:
Hi both,

Kicking off the Brush maturation effort for the vision portfolio. Brush is our 3D reconstruction engine using Gaussian splatting, and its differentiator is portability: it renders AND trains on macOS/Windows/Linux, in a browser, and on Android, via the Burn framework and custom WGSL kernels. Nobody else in the space demos on-device training - that's the wedge.

The README says it plainly: today it's a proof of concept, basic training only, none of the newer extensions. Goal for Apr 13 - Aug 3 is demo-ready, not feature-complete.

Milestones: M1 (May 15) stable ingestion of both zip formats - synthetic-NeRF-style with transform_train.json, and COLMAP with images + sparse folders. M2 (Jun 26) quality bar vs. reference implementation on standard scenes. M3 (Jul 24) browser + Android demo for the Launch Review Board.

Hyun is TL. Bao, staffing and the eval question are yours.

Lucia

subject: Re: Kickoff: Brush - staffing + eval harness scoping
body:
Lucia,

Staffing: Hyun 70% (TL, owns the WGSL kernel work and the Burn upgrade), Bilal 50%, Rafael 30% on splat-quality methodology through June.

On the eval question: to hit M2 we need systematic quality tracking, not eyeballing renders in the desktop app. There is no shared tooling for this, so we're scoping and building an internal evaluation harness from scratch - Bilal will own it at 50% for roughly six weeks, covering dataset loading, metric computation (PSNR/SSIM), and regression tracking across commits. Rerun integration stays for interactive debugging (training stats visualize there already), but the harness is what gates merges.

Compute: modest - single-GPU training runs; a dozen titan-a100 slots best-effort suffices. The Android CI devices are the scarcer resource; I've asked for 4 test phones.

Risk to flag early: Burn is a fast-moving dependency and the custom WGSL kernels break on upgrades. Hyun wants to pin versions until after LRB.

Bao

subject: Re: Kickoff: Brush - June status: quality gap on outdoor scenes
body:
Status ahead of the M2 checkpoint.

Done: both ingestion paths are solid (synthetic-NeRF zips and COLMAP zips), and Bilal's harness now runs nightly - PSNR/SSIM on 8 standard scenes with per-commit regression tracking. The .ply viewer path also got a nice speedup from a kernel fix.

The gap: on indoor scenes we're within 0.4 dB PSNR of the reference 3DGS implementation, but on the two outdoor scenes we trail by 1.8-2.3 dB. Root cause is that we only do basic 'standard' Gaussian splatting - the reference results people compare against lean on post-release extensions (exposure handling, anti-aliasing) that Brush deliberately doesn't implement yet.

Trade-off for M2: implement exposure compensation (~3 weeks, Rafael thinks it closes most of the outdoor gap) or declare indoor-only scope for the LRB demo. Android build is fine btw, trains a small scene in 11 min on the test phones.

Need a call by Jun 19.

Hyun

subject: Re: Kickoff: Brush - decision: indoor-first demo, exposure work continues
body:
Decision, so we stop burning cycles on this:

The Jul 24 LRB demo is scoped to indoor scenes plus the on-device Android training story - 11 minutes to train a scene on a phone is the demo, honestly; nobody in the room will ask about outdoor PSNR. Nadia, adding us to the LRB agenda for Jul 24 on that basis.

BUT we don't drop the outdoor gap: Rafael and Hyun start the exposure-compensation work now, targeting end of window (Aug 3). If it lands early and the harness shows we've closed to within ~0.8 dB on outdoor, we add one outdoor scene to the demo as an upside surprise. Bilal, please add the two outdoor scenes to the nightly harness dashboard so we can watch the gap close.

Also locking this into the Q3 OKR narrative before the Jun 26 lock: "portable splatting demo through LRB" is the committed item; outdoor parity is stretch.

Lucia

subject: Kickoff: Project Vantage - metric-aware inventory forecasting
body:
Team,

Kickoff for the inventory forecasting effort. We're branding this internally as Project Vantage - use that name on all decks, OKR entries and the demo booking.

The product story writes itself: customers optimize MAPE and then wonder why stockouts and holding costs don't improve. Our research showed optimizing conventional forecasting metrics does not necessarily improve downstream business performance, and it gives us an efficient procedure to optimize common inventory metrics end-to-end differentiably even though they aren't differentiable in general. That's the differentiator versus every off-the-shelf forecaster.

Window is short (Feb 2 - Apr 13), so scope is a customer-shaped pilot: M1 (Feb 27) repro on the favorita multivariate dataset using the existing embedding code; M2 (Mar 20) cost trade-off study - the method adapts to different cost regimes and we need those curves for sales; M3 (Apr 10) pilot readout deck.

Nikhil is TL. Daniela owns staffing.

Dmitri

subject: Re: Kickoff: Project Vantage - staffing + data plumbing
body:
Dmitri,

Staffing for the window: Nikhil 70% (TL, owns the differentiable inventory-metric objectives), Amara 60% on data_formatting - the favorita preprocessing and embedding path is the fiddliest part of the repo, so that's a real job, not a chore. Jorge 40% on training infra, Leilani 40% on the readout tooling and dashboard.

Compute is a non-issue: LSTM Encoder-Decoder models train on single GPUs; 8 titan-a100 slots best-effort covers the full sweep including the Naive Seasonal Scaler baselines.

Two constraints:
1) Favorita licensing check with Legal before any customer-facing artifact uses those numbers - I've pinged Kofi's queue, 2-3 week SLA, so it needs to be in flight now to clear before M3.
2) Amara is out the week of Mar 2, so M1 has zero slack after Feb 27. If the favorita embedding repro drags, M1 slips a full week.

Daniela

subject: Re: Kickoff: Project Vantage - M2 status: good curves, one honest caveat
body:
Status: M1 landed Feb 26 (Amara beat her own deadline). M2 cost trade-off study is nearly done.

The good: end-to-end optimization of the inventory objectives beats the business-agnostic baselines in most cost regimes we tested. Where holding cost dominates, e2e training cuts total inventory cost 9-14% vs. the MSE-trained LSTM baseline; the model visibly learns to under-forecast slow movers, which is exactly the behavior the paper promised - the method adapting to the cost trade-off.

The caveat for the deck: in the balanced-cost regime the gap narrows to 2-3%, occasionally within noise. So the honest pitch is "metric-aware training pays off most when your cost structure is asymmetric" - which most real inventory customers are, but we should not claim universal wins. Leilani's dashboard shows the crossover point nicely; I'd put that chart front and center at the readout.

On track for the Apr 10 M3 readout.

Nikhil

subject: Re: Kickoff: Project Vantage - readout decision + what's next
body:
Wrap-up ahead of tomorrow's readout.

Decision on positioning: we go with Nikhil's honest framing - "metric-aware training pays off most when your cost structure is asymmetric", with the 9-14% holding-cost-regime result as the headline and the crossover chart as the second slide. I'd rather under-promise at the readout than walk back claims in a pilot.

One scope cut to log: the real-time reforecasting demo Jorge prototyped is out - it's cool but the pilot customer runs weekly batch, and Legal's favorita clearance came through for static charts only, pending one wording change from Kofi. Jorge, park the prototype in the repo with a README.

Next step: if the readout lands, Vantage graduates to a Q2/Q3 pilot with the customer's own data, which means a fresh scoping round for ingestion. Daniela, hold Amara's and Nikhil's allocations until that decision - I'll know within two weeks.

Good sprint, everyone. Short window, real result.

Dmitri

subject: Kickoff: BUSTLE formula suggestion for data-platforms
body:
Hi all,

Kickoff for the BUSTLE effort. The research: a learned model guides a bottom-up program synthesis search to efficiently synthesize spreadsheet programs from input-output examples. The product: "write two example rows, get the formula" inside our data-platform tables - a genuinely sticky feature for the analyst persona.

Scope for Apr 6 - Jul 27:
- M1 (May 8): repro of the released system. Note the codebase is mostly Java (compile.sh pulls the jars) with Python/TensorFlow for model training - plan around that split.
- M2 (Jun 12): retrain the guidance model on an internal task distribution; benchmark on the SyGuS tasks (download script is in the repo) plus 200 tasks mined from our own users' formula history.
- M3 (Jul 20): latency-bounded prototype behind an internal flag - synthesis under 2s p95 for the demo set.

Saoirse is TL. Bao, over to you on staffing + the Q3 budget question we discussed.

Dmitri

subject: Re: Kickoff: BUSTLE - staffing + budget confirmation
body:
Dmitri,

Staffing: Saoirse 70% (TL), Giannis 60% on the Java synthesis core and the SyGuS benchmark rig, Oyin 50% on the TF training pipeline and task mining. That covers M1/M2; M3 latency work may need a short loan from the serving team, which I'll raise with Zeke when we get there.

Budget: Idris has verbally earmarked $120k from the Q3 discretionary compute budget line B-77 for this project, which covers the model retraining sweeps and the synthesis benchmark farm through September. I'm treating that as committed and building the Q3 plan on it. Idris - cc'd - just reply with the paperwork when the Q3 books open.

Near-term compute is small: guidance-model training is single-GPU TensorFlow; the search itself is CPU-heavy, so I'm requesting a 96-vCPU batch pool instead of GPU slots.

Bao

subject: Re: Kickoff: BUSTLE - M2 status: retrained model wins, latency tail is the risk
body:
M2 status, two days ahead of the checkpoint.

Results: the retrained guidance model solves 61% of our 200 mined internal tasks within the search budget, vs. 44% for the released model - the internal task distribution (lots of date munging and string normalization) really is different from the published benchmarks. On SyGuS we're at parity with the released model, so no regression. Giannis's rig runs the whole benchmark suite in 40 min, which has been great for iteration.

The risk for M3: latency. Median synthesis is 380ms, but p95 is 4.1s on tasks where the learned model ranks the right string primitives poorly and the bottom-up search blows up the candidate pool. Options: (a) hard timeout at 2s and return best partial - solves ~54% within budget, (b) prune the value pool harder, which Oyin estimates costs 3-4 points of solve rate but tames the tail.

Recommend (a) for the flag-gated prototype and revisit after real usage data. Need a call by Jun 19.

Saoirse

subject: Re: Kickoff: BUSTLE - decision: 2s timeout, ship the prototype
body:
Decision: option (a). Hard 2s timeout, return the best partial program with a "couldn't finish" affordance in the UI. 54% solve rate inside the budget is enough for a flag-gated prototype, and honestly the 61%-vs-44% retraining story is the number I'm taking into Q3 planning - OKRs lock Jun 26 and "formula suggestion GA decision by end of Q3" goes in as our committed item, funded from the B-77 earmark Bao lined up.

One scope cut with it: the 200-task mined benchmark stays internal-only for now. Kofi hasn't finished the privacy review of using customer formula history, even anonymized, and the 2-3 week SLA means we don't block M3 on it - the SyGuS numbers carry the external story until then.

Saoirse, July 20 M3 stands. Nice work team, the p95 analysis was exactly the right level of detail.

Dmitri

subject: Kickoff: C-Learning for goal-conditioned robotics sim
body:
Hi Jelena, Halima,

Kickoff for the C-Learning effort in agents-rl. The research reframes goal-conditioned RL as predicting and controlling the future state distribution of the agent, trained indirectly via a classifier that predicts whether an observation comes from the future. Two properties make this a product play for the robotics-sim offering:

1) The off-policy variant predicts the future state distribution of a NEW policy without collecting new experience - that's offline policy evaluation for customer robots, a straight cost saver.
2) The theory tells us how to choose the goal-sampling ratio, replacing the hand-tuned relabeling folklore our solutions team currently ships.

Milestones for Apr 27 - Jul 27: M1 (May 29) repro on the MuJoCo manipulation suite; M2 (early July) goal-sampling-ratio ablation + off-policy evaluation study; M3 (Jul 24) integration spec for the sim platform.

Halima is TL. Jelena owns staffing/compute - note MuJoCo licensing is handled at the org level already.

Ulla

subject: Re: Kickoff: C-Learning - staffing + compute reservation
body:
Ulla,

Staffing: Halima 70% (TL), Gustavo 60% on the classifier training loop and ablations, Oyin 40% on the sim-platform integration path. That holds through the window.

Compute: we hold the cirrus-tpu reservation for the week of 2026-06-22 - 512 accelerators from the agents-rl quarterly allocation. The full goal-sampling-ratio ablation runs that week, so the sweep configs must be frozen by Jun 17. Before then, M1 repro runs fine on titan-a100 best-effort; the MuJoCo environments are the bottleneck, not the networks.

One infra note: the mujoco200 install with the libGL symlink dance is fragile on our base images. Oyin is baking a container this week so the whole team stops fighting it - budget half a day each to migrate.

Also: if the ablation slips past June, we run into Q3 allocation negotiations and I can't promise the same accelerator count. Jun 17 freeze is the real deadline here.

Jelena

subject: Re: Kickoff: C-Learning - status before sweep freeze
body:
Status two days before config freeze.

M1 done (landed Jun 2, few days late - the mujoco container saved us, thanks Oyin). C-Learning matches published performance on 5 of 6 MuJoCo manipulation tasks and beats our internal HER-style relabeling baseline on 4, consistent with the paper's claim that it outperforms prior goal-relabeling methods.

For the ablation week: Gustavo's sweep is 6 tasks x 7 goal-sampling ratios x 4 seeds, plus the off-policy track where we evaluate 3 held-out policies against ground-truth Monte Carlo rollouts. Configs freeze Wednesday as planned.

One risk to flag for the integration spec: the off-policy variant's future-state predictions degrade when the new policy is far from the data-collection policy - on our farthest held-out policy the predicted goal-reach probabilities are off by up to 18 points. We'll quantify the "trust radius" during the sweep, but M3 should probably ship with a policy-divergence guardrail rather than unconditional claims.

Halima

subject: Re: Kickoff: C-Learning - decision: guardrail in, unconditional OPE claims out
body:
All,

Sweep results reviewed with Jelena this morning. Decisions:

1) The ablation confirms the theory-driven goal-sampling ratio: the predicted optimum was within one grid step of the empirical best on all 6 tasks. That's the headline for the M3 spec and it's a clean story - "principled, not folklore".

2) On off-policy evaluation: Halima's trust-radius data settles it. The integration spec ships WITH the policy-divergence guardrail - OPE results outside the trusted region get flagged, not reported. I'm cutting the "evaluate any policy, zero new data" phrasing from the customer-facing material; it becomes "evaluate nearby policies without new data collection", which the 18-point miss makes non-negotiable.

3) Scope cut: the image-observation variant moves out of this window entirely. State-based observations only for M3 on Jul 24.

Oyin, please have the spec skeleton to Halima by Friday.

Thanks all - the reserved week paid for itself.

Ulla

subject: Kickoff: Project Meltwater - learned cache replacement
body:
Hi Ivo, Milan,

Kickoff for the learned cache-replacement effort. We're running this under the codename Project Meltwater - use it in decks, OKR entries and standups so the graphs-retrieval reviews can track us.

Why: our retrieval serving spends real money on cache misses. Our ICML work showed an imitation learning approach to cache replacement beats heuristic policies, and the released code gives us the full training loop over LLC access traces.

Plan for Mar 2 - May 25: since we can't use the original paper's traces (never released), we follow the README's recommended path - the 2nd Cache Replacement Championship (CRC2) traces, collected by patching ChampSim. M1 (Mar 27): trace pipeline + repro of published-quality policies on CRC2. M2 (Apr 24): traces captured from our own retrieval-serving cache and a first learned policy trained on them. M3 (May 22): offline eval report vs. our production LRU variant, go/no-go for a serving experiment.

Milan is TL. Ivo has staffing.

Anders

subject: Re: Kickoff: Project Meltwater - staffing + trace-capture dependency
body:
Anders,

Staffing: Milan 70% (TL), Quentin 60% on model training and the imitation targets, Jorge 50% on the ChampSim patch + trace tooling. Compute is light - these are small models; 16 titan-a100 slots best-effort covers all training.

The real dependency is M2 trace capture from production. Zeke (cc'd): we need read access to the retrieval-serving cache layer plus a sampling hook to log ~200M LLC-equivalent accesses. Your team's SLA on new taps has been 3+ weeks lately, and M2 lands Apr 24 - can we get the request in this week? Without it, M2 slides and the whole go/no-go compresses.

Also setting expectations on Python versions: the repo pins Python 3.7-era deps and the baselines package installs from a git commit; Jorge will containerize before anyone burns a day on env drift.

Ivo

subject: Re: Kickoff: Project Meltwater - M2 status + a distribution-shift risk
body:
Status: M1 landed on time - Jorge's ChampSim patch produces clean CRC2-style LLC traces and Quentin's policies reproduce the expected gains over LRU/heuristics on the championship workloads.

M2 is a week late (trace tap went live Apr 20, thanks Zeke's team) but data is flowing: 240M accesses captured from retrieval serving so far. First learned policy on our traces shows an 11.4% miss-rate reduction vs. production LRU in offline replay.

The risk: our production access patterns shift hard around index rebuilds - the every-6-hours rebuild causes a burst pattern CRC2 never sees, and during those windows the learned policy's advantage drops to ~2% and briefly goes negative on one shard. Quentin wants to add rebuild-window traces to the training mix; that's a ~2 week add and would push M3 from May 22 to Jun 5, outside our window.

Options for the go/no-go: (a) report as-is with the rebuild caveat, (b) extend. Preference from us is (a) - the caveat is honest and the serving experiment would surface it anyway.

Milan

subject: Re: Kickoff: Project Meltwater - decision: report as-is, guarded rollout ask
body:
Decision: option (a). The M3 report ships Friday with the 11.4% offline miss-rate reduction as the headline and the index-rebuild windows called out as a known weakness, quantified per shard. We stay inside the window and keep credibility.

Go/no-go outcome I'm proposing to the review: GO for a serving experiment in Q3, but guarded - the experiment config falls back to production LRU during rebuild windows until Quentin's rebuild-aware training lands. Zeke, that fallback switch is the one thing I need your team to commit to before I take this to the review; can you confirm feasibility by Wednesday?

Q3 planning note (OKRs lock Jun 26): Meltwater's committed item is the serving experiment with a miss-rate target; rebuild-aware training is the stretch. Ivo, keep Quentin at 60% in your Q3 sheet.

Good work all - a real dollars-and-cents result.

Anders

subject: Kickoff: debiased calibration reporting (caltrain)
body:
Hi Santiago, Kaia,

Kickoff for the calibration-reporting module. Context: every model card we publish quotes ECE, and our own research showed those estimates carry systematic bias - binning choices can make a model look better- or worse-calibrated than it is. Our open-source release has the debiased estimators plus the reliability-diagram tooling; agents-rl wants this productized because calibration is the first question customers ask about agent confidence scores.

Scope for Feb 16 - Apr 27: M1 (Mar 13) reproduce the paper's figures from the released scripts - including the reliability diagrams and the curves controlling true calibration error - as our correctness reference. M2 (Apr 3) wrap the debiased estimators in a clean API with bootstrap confidence intervals. M3 (Apr 24) integrate into the Evalline harness so every eval run reports debiased calibration by default.

Kaia is TL. Santiago, staffing and the Evalline coordination are yours.

Ulla

subject: Re: Kickoff: debiased calibration reporting - staffing + dependencies
body:
Ulla,

Staffing: Kaia 60% (TL), Katya 60% on the estimator API and bootstrap CIs, Yusuf 30% - he's splitting with the exploration bake-off, so he takes the repro track only (the plotting scripts are self-contained; mostly a matter of the cached data_dir setup and the MPLBACKEND env var).

Dependencies:
1) Evalline: Tomas (cc'd), M3 needs a review slot from your team in mid-April. The change is additive - a new calibration section per eval run - but it touches the default report template, so I want your sign-off early, not on Apr 20.
2) Figure 3 requires the external logit data the README points to; Katya is mirroring it internally this week.

On data: the Corpus v2 migration freeze is 2026-08-07, so we have comfortable runway - our benchmark logit sets can be ingested any time before early August, well after this window closes. No need to rush Corpus tickets for this project.

Compute: negligible. All CPU plotting and bootstrap work.

Santiago

subject: Re: Kickoff: debiased calibration reporting - status + an uncomfortable finding
body:
Status: M1 done (Yusuf reproduced the intro reliability diagram, the ECE-distribution figure, and the TCE-controlled curves; pixel-level match after sorting out the cached data_dir). M2 is mid-flight - Katya has the debiased estimator API working with bootstrap CIs.

The uncomfortable finding: we ran the debiased estimator over 14 of our own recent model cards. For 9 of them, the debiased calibration error is 1.3-2.1x the ECE number we published - the bias the paper warns about was flattering us, especially on small eval sets where binning bias is worst. Two agent-confidence models move from "well-calibrated" to "borderline".

That makes M3 slightly political: when Evalline flips to debiased-by-default, historical comparisons will look like regressions. Recommend we ship with both numbers side by side for two quarters plus a one-pager explaining the estimator change, rather than silently replacing the metric.

Risk to M3 date: none currently - Tomas's review slot is booked for Apr 14.

Kaia

subject: Re: Kickoff: debiased calibration reporting - decision: dual reporting for two quarters
body:
All,

Decision, agreed with Tomas at Tuesday's review: Evalline ships debiased-by-default on Apr 24 as planned, with Kaia's dual-reporting proposal adopted - both the legacy ECE and the debiased number appear side by side through Q3, then legacy drops. Kaia's one-pager goes out with the release notes; I've asked her to include the 14-model-card comparison as the motivating example, because nothing sells "the old metric was biased" like our own numbers moving.

One escalation to be transparent about: the two borderline agent-confidence models belong to teams with launches in flight, and their PMs will see the new numbers before their launch reviews. I'm giving those PMs a heads-up this week rather than letting the dashboard surprise them - Tomas agreed. If either pushes back on the Apr 24 flip, it comes to me, not the team.

Nice, clean project. This is what a research-to-platform handoff should look like.

Ulla

subject: Kickoff: CamP Zip-NeRF quality reference pipeline
body:
Hi Deshawn, Milan,

Kickoff for the neural-rendering reference pipeline. Our open-source release bundles two methods in one JAX codebase: Zip-NeRF for the rendering quality and CamP for camera-pose preconditioning, which is what makes casually-captured scenes viable - poses from phone capture are never clean.

Product thesis for data-platforms: a scene-capture ingestion track where customers upload capture sessions and get a navigable scene. This window is about the quality reference, not serving.

Milestones (Feb 16 - Apr 27): M1 (Mar 13) environment + unit tests green (the repo ships run_all_unit_tests.sh - use it), repro of Zip-NeRF numbers on the NeRF Blender set. M2 (Apr 3) Mip-NeRF 360 dataset repro, plus CamP ablation on perturbed poses. M3 (Apr 24) capture-robustness report and a decision on the product track.

Milan is TL. Deshawn: staffing, compute, and the eval-data question.

Dmitri

subject: Re: Kickoff: CamP Zip-NeRF - staffing, compute, and the synthetic-data pipeline
body:
Dmitri,

Staffing: Milan 60% (TL, owns the JAX pipeline incl. the pycolmap quirk - the README is explicit that pip's pycolmap is the wrong one, so that goes in the setup doc in bold). Yusuf 40% on the CamP perturbed-pose ablations. Katya 60% - see below.

Compute: Zip-NeRF training is heavy; the release's own scripts warn the full reproduction takes a long time. Estimate: ~110 A100-days for both dataset repros plus the CamP ablation grid. titan-a100 best-effort should absorb that spread over six weeks; if contention bites in March I'll ask Ines for a short vulcan slice.

On eval data: the public benchmarks won't answer the capture-robustness question - we need scenes where we control pose error and scene content exactly. Nothing exists in-house for this, so we're scoping and staffing a synthetic-data generation pipeline built from scratch - Katya owns it at 60%: procedurally generated scenes, randomized camera trajectories, and rendered ground truth we control end to end. First usable scenes by Mar 20 to feed the M2 ablations.

Deshawn

subject: Re: Kickoff: CamP Zip-NeRF - M2 status: 360 repro green, CamP earns its keep
body:
Status.

M1 recap: unit tests green, Blender repro matched published PSNR within 0.1 dB. M2: the Mip-NeRF 360 repro finished Sunday - we're within noise on 6 of 7 scenes, one (bicycle) is 0.3 dB under and Yusuf suspects a train-schedule difference; rerunning with the release's exact config.

CamP ablation on Katya's synthetic scenes is the interesting bit: with clean poses, CamP preconditioning changes nothing (expected). At synthetic pose noise matching what we measured from phone-capture COLMAP runs, Zip-NeRF alone drops 4-6 dB PSNR; with CamP the drop is 0.8-1.4 dB. That's the product story in one chart - casual capture is unusable without pose refinement and fine with it.

Risks for M3: training cost. ~14 A100-hours per scene at our settings is fine for a quality reference, not for an ingestion product. The report will say that plainly: the product track needs a distillation/acceleration phase before any customer-facing latency promise. Also titan contention did bite twice; thanks Deshawn for the vulcan bridge.

Milan

subject: Re: Kickoff: CamP Zip-NeRF - M3 decision: quality reference adopted, product track gated
body:
Closing the window. Decisions from the M3 review (Hana attended, cc'ing for the record):

1) The CamP+Zip-NeRF stack is adopted as our scene-quality reference - the capture-robustness chart (4-6 dB loss without pose preconditioning vs. under 1.4 dB with CamP) was the deciding evidence.

2) The customer-facing ingestion product is GATED, not green-lit. Milan's 14 A100-hours/scene number makes the unit economics unworkable; the product track only opens once an acceleration phase gets us under ~1 A100-hour/scene. That goes to Q3 planning as a proposal, not a commitment.

3) Katya's synthetic-scene pipeline is explicitly called out in the report as reusable infrastructure - it stays maintained at 20% of her time next quarter.

Bicycle-scene rerun matched after the config fix, for the record, so the repro is fully clean.

Thanks all. Exactly what a reference-quality window should produce.

Dmitri

subject: Kickoff: CANN visual localization core
body:
Hi Daniela, Nikhil,

Kickoff for the CANN effort in vision. Our ICCV work on Constrained Approximate Nearest Neighbors is a genuinely strong wedge for indoor visual positioning - malls, airports, warehouses - where GPS dies. Two properties matter commercially: the retrieval scheme is independent of the local feature type (any d-dimensional vectors, so customers aren't locked to our extractor), and the reference results on Baidu-Mall are already competitive.

Window Apr 13 - Jul 6. M1 (May 8): repro of the released end-to-end run.sh index/query flow on the sample data (FIRE features), then the Baidu-Mall benchmark. M2 (Jun 5): scale test - index a 10x larger internal capture set, measure recall/latency curves. M3 (Jun 29): integration proposal for the vision serving stack + go/no-go on a pilot with the logistics customer.

Nikhil is TL (25%, he's still wrapping Vantage follow-ups; Linnea carries the build). Daniela owns staffing.

Lucia

subject: Re: Kickoff: CANN - staffing + data timing
body:
Lucia,

Staffing confirmed: Linnea 70% carrying the implementation, Quentin 50% on the recall/latency methodology, Chiara 50% on data plumbing (feature extraction jobs and the Eigen binary matrix format the index expects - one matrix per image, rows as d-dim vectors), Nikhil 25% TL as you said.

Compute: CPU-heavy indexing, not GPU. I've requested a 64-vCPU pool; the only GPU use is FIRE feature extraction for the internal set, maybe 10 titan-a100 days total.

Heads-up on data timing: the Corpus v2 migration freeze is 2026-07-24, so our indoor capture set needs to be ingested by mid-July at the latest. That's after our window closes, so ingestion can trail the M3 report without risk - I've sequenced Chiara's tickets accordingly.

One flag: the sample data download comes from an external Drive link; Chiara is mirroring it internally today so CI doesn't depend on it.

Daniela

subject: Re: Kickoff: CANN - M2 status: scale test in, memory is the story
body:
M2 status, couple days early since the numbers are stable.

M1 recap: run.sh end-to-end flow reproduced on the sample data (the Mapillary sanity set caught a real path bug, worth keeping in CI), Baidu-Mall results match the paper.

Scale test on the 10x internal capture set: recall@1 holds up well - we lose 2.3 points vs. the small-index regime, which Quentin says is in line with ANN scaling folklore. Query latency is fine: p50 41ms, p95 87ms on the 64-vCPU pool.

The story is memory: the index at 10x is 118GB resident, and the growth looks close to linear in total feature count. For the logistics pilot (their site survey is ~4x our test set again) that's approaching half-a-TB per site, which changes the serving hardware conversation entirely. Options we'll cost out for M3: feature subsampling per image (cheap, recall cost unknown), PQ-style compression on the vectors (CANN is feature-agnostic so nothing structural blocks it), or sharding per mall wing.

No schedule risk to M3 yet.

Linnea

subject: Re: Kickoff: CANN - decision: pilot yes, compression first
body:
Decisions ahead of the M3 writeup, and locking these into Q3 OKRs today given the planning deadline:

1) Pilot: GO with the logistics customer, but scoped to two site wings, not the full survey - that keeps us inside one serving node at current index sizes while the memory work lands.

2) Of Linnea's three options, compression first. Quentin's quick experiment (PQ at 8x on the vectors) cost only 0.9 recall@1 points on Baidu-Mall, and since the framework is feature-type-agnostic it slots in cleanly. Subsampling stays as the fallback; sharding-per-wing is the deployment pattern regardless.

3) M3 report includes the half-TB-per-site math prominently. I want the serving-hardware conversation to happen with real numbers, not vibes, when we bring Zeke's team in next quarter.

Q3 committed OKR: pilot live at two wings with recall@1 within 3 points of the uncompressed reference. Stretch: full-site index under 150GB.

Great window so far, team.

Lucia

subject: Kickoff: EMCAPSNet viability study for pose-sensitive matching
body:
Hi Bruno, Yara,

Kickoff for the EMCAPSNet study. Motivation: graphs-retrieval keeps hitting viewpoint sensitivity in visual matching - the same object from a new angle tanks retrieval quality. Capsules with EM routing are explicitly built for viewpoint robustness, and our open-source release ships the model with smallNORB training and eval.

This is a viability study, not a committed product: I want a clear yes/no by early July on whether capsule routing earns a place in the matching stack.

Milestones for Mar 9 - Jul 6: M1 (Apr 10) repro the released checkpoints - the README's eval flow should give 1.8 test error on smallNORB, and 1.3 with patching enabled. M2 (May 22) viewpoint-robustness comparison vs. our CNN baseline under held-out azimuth/elevation splits. M3 (late June) scale stress-test: does EM routing's cost stay sane beyond smallNORB-sized inputs? Then the yes/no memo.

Yara is TL. Bruno: staffing + the June compute ask.

Anders

subject: Re: Kickoff: EMCAPSNet - staffing + June compute locked
body:
Anders,

Staffing: Yara 60% (TL, owns the robustness methodology), Gustavo 50% on training runs and the docker path - the repo ships run_local_gpu.sh with NVIDIA docker support, which Giannis has already adapted to our images. Giannis 40% on eval tooling and the checkpoint plumbing (norb_em_checkpoints + smallNORB tfrecords are mirrored internally as of yesterday).

Compute: near-term needs are small - the README's smallNORB training config wants 8 GPUs, fine on titan-a100 best-effort. For M3, compute is sorted: we hold the vulcan-h100 reservation for the week of 2026-06-22 - 512 accelerators for the scale stress-test sweep, with jobs queued to start as soon as the scheduled maintenance wraps on the 24th. It's a short effective window, so Gustavo will have the sweep fully rehearsed on titan beforehand.

One caveat: the release is marked preliminary/under construction, so expect some code archaeology in M1.

Bruno

subject: Re: Kickoff: EMCAPSNet - M2 status: robustness real, cost curve ugly
body:
M2 status.

M1 recap: repro clean. Eval on the released checkpoint gives 1.8 test error on smallNORB with patching off and 1.3 with --patching=True, exactly matching the README (paper says 1.4, we and the README get 1.3 - noted in the log).

M2 results: on held-out azimuth splits, EMCAPSNet degrades 3.1 points vs. 8.7 for our CNN baseline at matched params - the viewpoint-robustness claim is real, at least on smallNORB-class data. Novel-elevation is similar (2.8 vs. 7.9).

The concern going into M3: EM routing cost. Per-step time grows much faster than input resolution - our 96x96 prototype is ~9x slower per step than 32x32, and memory scales worse. Gustavo's projection says anything ImageNet-sized is off the table without serious kernel work. So the June stress-test is genuinely decisive: if the cost curve doesn't bend with the optimizations Gustavo is testing, my memo will be "no for the general stack, maybe for small pose-critical verticals".

Sweep rehearsal on titan is scheduled for Jun 12.

Yara

subject: Re: Kickoff: EMCAPSNet - decision memo: no for the general stack
body:
All,

Closing the study. The stress-test sweep ran (compressed week, but Gustavo's rehearsal discipline meant we used the reservation efficiently) and the answer is clear, so the memo I'm sending to Eleni says:

DECISION: No for the general matching stack. The cost curve did not bend - even with Gustavo's routing-iteration cap and fused-op experiments, EM routing at retrieval-relevant resolutions costs 6-11x our CNN baseline per training step, and inference latency lands outside the serving budget by a wide margin.

BUT: the viewpoint-robustness numbers (3.1 vs. 8.7 azimuth degradation) are too good to shelve entirely. Recommendation: a narrow follow-up for the warehouse-inventory vertical, where images are small, poses vary wildly, and latency budgets are loose. That's a Q3 proposal for Eleni's review, sized at ~1.5 FTE.

Yara, Gustavo, Giannis - a clean negative with a documented boundary is a good outcome. The memo credits the study design.

Anders

subject: Kickoff: CATE video embeddings for the platform
body:
Hi Bruno, Yusuf,

Kickoff for the CATE video-embedding effort. Our ICCV work on Composable Augmentation Encoding gives us self-supervised video representations with no labeling cost, and the released assets are unusually product-ready: a Kinetics-400-pretrained model with a working inference colab, nearest-neighbor classification demo on UCF-101, and Something-Something v1/v2 checkpoints in the same storage layout for transfer studies.

Product shape: a video-embedding endpoint for data-platforms customers - similarity search and dedup over video libraries without asking anyone to label anything.

Milestones for Apr 20 - Jul 6: M1 (May 15) repro of the UCF-101 nearest-neighbor demo from the released checkpoint, embeddings behind an internal batch API. M2 (Jun 12) cost + quality study for serving - this is where the model-size question bites. M3 (Jun 30) go/no-go on a customer-facing endpoint.
