The real engineering item surfaced in Bilal's audit of the raw pairs: Wikipedia mirrors, redirects and near-identical revisions create pairs that are effectively the same document twice. If those leak into the benchmark, similarity scores inflate and the eval loses credibility. So: we are scoping and staffing a dataset de-duplication pipeline, built from scratch - Bilal owns the design (shingling + MinHash over document text, plus URL-normalization rules), Oyin the batch infrastructure, working version by 6/19. I am carrying it as a first-class deliverable, since every dataset this portfolio hosts after GWikiMatch will need the same pass.

That pushes the hosted-dataset milestone from 5/29 to 6/26. Baselines and the 8/5 adoption review still hold.

Bao

subject: Status: dedup numbers, protocol draft, rater-agreement caveat
body:
Hi both,

Status. Bilal's de-dup pipeline is in dry-run and the numbers justify the schedule slip: 3.1% of candidate pairs are mirror/redirect duplicates, and they are heavily concentrated in the label-2 (most similar) bucket - exactly where inflation would have hurt most. Production run lands 6/19 as planned.

Eval protocol draft is circulating: we report accuracy and AUC on the majority-vote labels, with the 0/1/2 scale collapsed to binary at two operating points so teams cannot cherry-pick a threshold.

Caveat I want on record: rater agreement is solid on 0-vs-2 but noticeably weaker between adjacent labels (0-vs-1, 1-vs-2). Where the 3 raters split three ways there is no majority at all - about 2% of pairs - and we drop those, documented. Teams should treat small deltas on the middle band as noise, and the protocol doc says so.

Baselines on track for 7/3; dual-encoder one is already running.

Quentin

subject: Re: Status: dedup numbers, protocol draft, rater-agreement caveat
body:
Team,

Decisions ahead of the 8/5 adoption review:

1. The de-duplicated dataset (production run of 6/19) is the only version we host. The pre-dedup snapshot is archived, access-restricted, and the dataset card cites the 3.1% duplicate rate so external comparisons are honest about the difference.
2. Both baselines shipped 7/3 - the dual-encoder and the hierarchical attention model - and the leaderboard-style results table goes in the review pack with the two fixed operating points, no custom thresholds.
3. Quentin's middle-band noise caveat gets promoted from the protocol appendix to the front page. If teams are going to quote GWikiMatch numbers in launch reviews, the noise floor needs to be unmissable.
4. Adoption: two retrieval teams confirmed, a third interested. That clears our bar.

Bilal, Oyin - the dedup pipeline is getting reuse requests already. Write the runbook before vacation season, please.

Anders

subject: Kickoff: health equity toolbox for LLM evaluation
body:
Hi Alina,

Kicking off the health equity toolbox workstream. Health-side teams evaluating LLM outputs currently have no standard way to surface equity harms and biases; our open-source analytic toolbox gives us one, and I want it running as a platform capability rather than a one-off paper artifact.

Scope: reproduce the primary published analyses - the rate and confidence-interval estimates behind Figures 2, 3 and 4 - over the EquityMedQA rating data, supporting both input paths the code allows (the xlsx workbook and the three Figshare csv extracts: ratings_independent, ratings_pairwise, ratings_counterfactual). Then wrap it so any internal eval run can produce the same figures over its own ratings.

Milestones: repro validated against published outputs by 3/20, wrapped pipeline on one internal model eval by 4/24, review 5/13.

Kaia leads analysis, Farah the pipeline, Saoirse integration, Giannis data handling. Staffing from you this week?

Dmitri

subject: Re: Kickoff: health equity toolbox for LLM evaluation
body:
Dmitri,

Staffing: Kaia 50%, Farah 60%, Saoirse 30%, Giannis 40%. Compute is negligible - this is statistical analysis over rating tables, not model training; everything runs on standard CPU quota.

The real work is data logistics. Giannis has both input paths working (equitymedqa_ratings.xlsx and the three csv extracts), but for the platform version the ratings need to live in Corpus as governed tables, not as files someone downloads. His plan: land ratings_independent, ratings_pairwise and ratings_counterfactual as versioned Corpus tables in July, after the window, once the internal-eval pilot tells us what schema tweaks we need. The Corpus v2 migration freeze is 2026-08-07, so landing the ratings tables in Corpus during July leaves us clear of it by several weeks.

Also flagging: rating data is human-subjects-adjacent, so I asked Kofi whether the internal pilot needs a privacy review. Awaiting answer, will build the 2-3 week SLA into the plan if yes.

Alina

subject: Status: repro validated, pilot running, scope caveat for the review
body:
Hi both,

Status. The repro is validated: our pipeline regenerates the rate and confidence-interval estimates behind Figures 2, 3 and 4 from both input paths, and Kaia diffed our outputs against the published values - everything matches to the reported precision. The xlsx and csv paths now share one normalization layer, so future ratings only need to hit that schema.

The internal pilot (wrapping one model eval's ratings through the toolbox) started 4/13 and the counterfactual analysis is already surfacing a rater-disagreement pattern the eval team had not noticed. Good sign for usefulness.

Caveat to state at the 5/13 review: the open-source code implements the primary analyses only - the Extended Data and Supplementary figures are explicitly not implemented. If health-side teams expect the full paper's analysis surface, that is a Q3 build, not a config flag. Kaia sized it at roughly 6 engineer-weeks.

Kofi's answer on privacy came back: pilot is fine under the existing eval program approval; the Corpus tables in July will need a lightweight review.

Farah

subject: Kickoff: Hierarchical Visual Foresight for long-horizon planning
body:
Hi Bruno,

Kicking off the HVF workstream in vision. The capability: self-supervised long-horizon task learning via visual subgoal generation - instead of planning pixel-by-pixel to a distant goal, HVF generates intermediate visual subgoals and plans between them. For the robotics-simulation customers this is the difference between demos that reach across a table and demos that tidy a room.

The stack per the release: an SV2P video prediction model trained via tensor2tensor, a conditional VAE for subgoal generation, plus the temporal distance cost function (TDM) and the time-agnostic prediction (TAP) baseline. Evaluation runs through the meta_cem planner on maze environments at horizon 50.

Milestones: full pipeline repro (generate_data through meta_cem) by 3/13, our simulation-env port by 4/17, review 5/6.

Carmen leads research, Hyun the video model, Bilal training infra, Saoirse env integration. Staffing and compute from you by Friday?

Lucia

subject: Re: Kickoff: Hierarchical Visual Foresight for long-horizon planning
body:
Lucia,

Resourcing.

Staffing: Carmen 70%, Hyun 40%, Bilal 60%, Saoirse 50%.

Compute: SV2P training is the heavy piece - video prediction models are hungry, and we will train once for the maze repro and again for our simulation env. I am asking for 64 A100s on titan best-effort through March, and I want to avoid a Vulcan reservation unless the second training run stalls. The VAE, TDM and TAP components are cheap by comparison.

Data plan: generate_data output for the repro stays local, but the trajectory datasets for our simulation env should live in Corpus so the robotics-sim teams can reuse them. Re-ingestion is a Q3 task after the window closes. The Corpus v2 migration freeze is 2026-07-24, so scheduling the trajectory-dataset re-ingestion for the first half of July keeps us safely inside it.

One env annoyance: the reference setup wants python3.6 and the tensor2tensor dependency is legacy; Bilal is building the container now so it doesn't bite us mid-March.

Bruno

subject: Status: maze repro done, subgoals earn their keep, SV2P is the bottleneck
body:
Hi both,

Repro status: the full chain runs - generate_data, SV2P training through tensor2tensor, then train_vae, train_tdm and train_tap, finishing with meta_cem on the medium-difficulty maze at horizon 50. Results match the release qualitatively: with one generated subgoal (numsg=1) planning success on medium mazes roughly doubles versus flat CEM with pixel cost, and TDM cost outperforms pixel cost on the harder layouts. That's the headline for the 5/6 review.

Bottleneck: SV2P. Training it for our own simulation env is 5x the maze data volume, and on best-effort titan we keep getting preempted - Bilal estimates the run loses a third of its throughput to restarts. Either we accept an April 24 -> May 1 slip on the env port, or Bruno escalates for a short reserved slice.

Also, teh conditional VAE occasionally generates subgoals behind walls; filtering candidates through the TDM cost before planning fixes it cheaply. Writing that up as a recommended default.

Carmen

subject: Re: Status: maze repro done, subgoals earn their keep, SV2P is the bottleneck
body:
Team,

Decisions for the home stretch:

1. Bruno escalated and Ines granted a one-week reserved slice of 32 H100s on Vulcan (thanks Ines) - that recovers most of the preemption losses, and the env port now lands 4/28. It did, in fact, land yesterday. Review stays 5/6.
2. The review scope is locked: maze repro numbers (subgoal doubling of planning success at horizon 50, TDM-over-pixel cost on hard layouts) plus the env-port demo. The multi-subgoal (numsg=2) ablation is cut from this window - Carmen's early data says the second subgoal buys little on our layouts and the sweep would eat the reserved slice.
3. Carmen's TDM-filtering trick ships as the default candidate filter, documented in the runbook.
4. Post-review: trajectory datasets to Corpus per Bruno's Q3 schedule, and we pitch continuation funding at the vision portfolio review in June.

Nice recovery on the schedule, everyone.

Lucia

subject: HIPI kickoff - inverse-RL relabeling as our multi-task data flywheel
body:
Team,

Kicking off HIPI for the agents-rl portfolio. The pitch: our open-source release showed that inverse RL is a principled way to relabel past experience - asking 'for what task was this trajectory optimal?' - and that it beats prior goal-relabeling methods on goal-reaching tasks while extending to reward families where those methods don't apply at all (discrete reward sets, linear rewards). Productized, this is a sample-efficiency multiplier for every agent we train: one experience buffer, many tasks.

Rough milestones inside our window: goal-reaching repro by mid-March, discrete and linear reward-family experiments through April, and an internal demo plus write-up before 2026-05-18. Bruno owns staffing and compute; Maren leads the relabeling infra, Tereza and Nikhil the experiment matrix.

I want one crisp metric for the demo: relabeled vs. non-relabeled sample efficiency at fixed steps. Bruno, resourcing note by end of month?

Thanks,
Ulla

subject: Re: HIPI kickoff - inverse-RL relabeling as our multi-task data flywheel
body:
Ulla,

Resourcing picture as promised. Staffing: Maren at 80%, Tereza at 50%, Nikhil at 40% through the window. Compute: we can live on titan-a100 best-effort for the repro phase - I've asked for 64 GPUs steady-state, bursting to 128 for the April experiment matrix. No Vulcan reservation needed for this one.

Platform dependency worth flagging: our experience buffers and relabeled-trajectory shards live on Corpus. One date to plan around: the Corpus v2 migration freeze is 2026-06-26, so relabeled-experience buffers need to be reading from v2 paths before then. That lands after our demo window, but Maren's relabeling infra should write v2-compatible shards from day one so we're not doing a rushed migration in June.

Only staffing risk is Tereza splitting time with another review in March; I'll keep it above 50%.

Bruno

subject: HIPI status: goal-reaching repro done, linear-reward inference is the risk
body:
Ulla, Bruno,

Status through week 7. Goal-reaching repro is done: inverse-RL relabeling hits 71% success at 1M steps vs. 58% for the goal-relabeling baseline on our hardest reaching task, matching the published direction. Discrete-reward-set domains are running now; Tereza has 6 of 9 configs finished and the acceleration effect is visible in 5.

The risk is the linear reward family. Inferring the hindsight task there means normalizing over the reward-parameter space, and our current estimator needs roughly 3x the samples we budgeted to stay stable. Nikhil is testing a cheaper approximation; if it's not converged by April 10 we should consider demoing discrete rewards only and keeping linear as a stretch.

Compute is fine - titan-a100 best-effort has been giving us ~70 GPUs.

Maren

subject: Re: HIPI status: decision - demo scopes to goal-reaching + discrete rewards
body:
All,

Decision, so we stop re-litigating this in standups: the May 14 internal demo covers goal-reaching and discrete-reward-set results only. Linear reward families move to a stretch appendix - Nikhil's cheaper estimator got the sample cost down to ~1.8x budget, which is progress but not demo-grade.

What we show: the 71% vs 58% goal-reaching result, plus discrete-reward acceleration on 7 of 9 configs. Framing for leadership is the data-flywheel story from kickoff - relabeling with inverse RL lets one buffer serve many tasks.

For Q3 OKR planning I'll propose 'HIPI relabeling available as a library for two partner agent teams' as the follow-on. Bruno, please sanity-check the staffing implication before I submit.

Nice work getting here inside the window.

Ulla

subject: HITNet kickoff - real-time stereo depth as a platform capability
body:
Team,

Kicking off the HITNet track. Goal: turn our open-source HITNet release (hierarchical iterative tile refinement for real-time stereo matching) into a supported depth-estimation capability other portfolios can call, instead of everyone hand-rolling stereo.

Scope for this window: stand up evaluation on the three dataset families we ship models for - FlyingThings (max disparity 320, cleanpass and finalpass), Middlebury at half resolution (160/288/400 disparity variants), and ETH3D (128). Milestones: eval harness reproducing PSM EPE by mid-April, latency characterization in May, go/no-go on a real-time serving demo at the June Launch Review Board.

One heads-up from the repo: datasets have to be downloaded manually and scripts pointed at the right locations, so Rosa - can you own a one-time ingest so the rest of the team isn't fighting paths?

Deshawn will follow up on staffing and compute.

Dmitri

subject: Re: HITNet kickoff - staffing + compute plan
body:
Dmitri,

Staffing and compute for the window:

- Wei 50% (eval + metrics), Umar 30% (Middlebury/ETH3D analysis), Rosa 40% (data ingest, then serving glue), Bilal 40% (infra).
- Farah Haddad is committed at 60% to HITNet for June 2026 - she leads the custom CUDA op work that the latency milestone depends on, and I've blocked her calendar accordingly.
- Compute is light: 16 titan-a100 GPUs best-effort covers eval and latency runs. No Vulcan ask.

Rationale on Farah: the released models use default tensorflow ops and run 3x slower than the custom-op variants, so the June real-time demo lives or dies on that port. She's our only person who's shipped custom CUDA kernels recently.

Budget-wise this fits inside the existing data-platforms envelope; no incremental headcount ask.

Deshawn

subject: HITNet status: EPE repro green, latency is the open risk
body:
Dmitri, Deshawn,

Status. Eval harness reproduces published-direction numbers on both FlyingThings passes - finalpass EPE within 2% of the reference, cleanpass within 1% - and the three Middlebury half-resolution models (160/288/400 max disparity) all evaluate cleanly. ETH3D done too.

The risk is exactly what Deshawn called out: with default TF ops we're measuring ~92 ms/frame on our target GPU, which is roughly 3x too slow for the real-time story. Farah's custom CUDA op port has the tile-hypothesis propagation kernel working; warp/refinement kernels are in review. Realistic ETA for an end-to-end custom-op model is first week of June, which leaves one week of margin before the LRB slot.

One more trade-off to flag: the released models are fixed disparity range. If LRB asks about arbitrary-range scenes we should say 'later release', not promise it.

Wei

subject: Re: HITNet status: decision for LRB on June 11
body:
All,

Decisions for the June 11 Launch Review Board:

1. We demo the custom-CUDA-op model. Farah landed the full kernel set on June 2 and we're at 31 ms/frame - inside the real-time budget. Great work.
2. Variable disparity range is explicitly out of scope; the LRB one-pager says 'fixed-range models (128-400), variable range in a later release'. No verbal promises beyond that please.
3. Middlebury half-resolution models are what we show for high-detail scenes; we do not upsample and imply full-res quality.

Remaining ask before the 11th: Wei to freeze the eval table (EPE + latency, all three datasets), Umar to write the two-paragraph limitations section. Deshawn keeps Farah's June allocation as planned through demo hardening.

If LRB signs off, Q3 goal becomes onboarding two internal consumers.

Dmitri

subject: HMC Swindles kickoff - cheaper posterior inference for the platform
body:
Team,

Kicking off the HMC Swindles workstream. Our open-source release showed you can substantially cut the variance of Hamiltonian Monte Carlo estimates with a couple of well-chosen 'swindles', and it ships a clean four-step pipeline: train the NeuTra preconditioner, tune the sampler, benchmark, evaluate. The product angle for data-platforms: a hardened posterior-inference service that internal teams can use for calibrated uncertainty on pipeline metrics without hand-tuning samplers.

Milestones across our (long) window: pipeline repro on the shipped tune_outputs hyperparameters by end of March, our own tuning loop by mid-May, then a full benchmark sweep in late June and a decision memo by 2026-07-13.

Wei owns methodology, Paloma the pipeline hardening, Leilani and Oyin infra and the benchmark harness hookup. Deshawn - resourcing note when you can; the June sweep is the only big compute item.

Dmitri

subject: Re: HMC Swindles kickoff - resourcing + the June benchmark week
body:
Dmitri,

Resourcing:

- Staffing: Wei 40%, Paloma 60%, Leilani 30%, Oyin 40%. Steady through the window, no changes planned.
- Day-to-day compute: preconditioner training and tuning fit comfortably on 8-16 titan-a100 GPUs best-effort.
- The big item: for the full benchmark sweep we hold the vulcan-h100 reservation - 384 accelerators for the week of 2026-06-29. Confirmed through the Infra Lead reservation process; that week is deliberately after the Vulcan maintenance window (June 22-24), so we shouldn't be exposed to it.

Env note from setup: the pipeline pulls in r-base plus a fresh tensorflow/probability clone, so Paloma is baking a container image this month - saves everyone the 'works on my venv' round trips.

No budget or headcount asks beyond the above.

Deshawn

subject: HMC Swindles status: tuning loop live, one stability risk before June
body:
Dmitri, Deshawn,

Status. Repro on the shipped tune_outputs hyperparameters is done and matched expectations. Our own tuning loop is live - we drive the 'objective' mode externally, starting from step_size 0.1 and a single leapfrog step, then let the optimizer walk from there. On the two easiest targets we're seeing effective-sample-size-per-flop gains of roughly 2.3x over vanilla HMC with the swindle estimators on, which is the headline we hoped for.

Risk: NeuTra preconditioner training occasionally diverges on our heaviest-tailed target - about 1 run in 6 - and a diverged preconditioner poisons everything downstream in the benchmark. Paloma has a checkpoint-and-retry wrapper in review; we want it merged at least two weeks before the June sweep so the 384-GPU week isn't spent babysitting restarts.

On track otherwise for the late-June benchmark and the July decision memo.

Wei

subject: Re: HMC Swindles status: decision memo direction after the benchmark week
body:
All,

Closing the loop after the benchmark week. Headline numbers held up: 2.1x median ESS-per-flop improvement across the full target suite, and the checkpoint-and-retry wrapper meant zero human intervention over the whole sweep - exactly what we wanted before recommending this as a platform service.

Decision for the July 13 memo: we recommend productizing the preconditioned-HMC-plus-swindles pipeline as an internal inference service, phase 1 limited to the target families we benchmarked. The heavy-tailed divergence issue is mitigated, not solved, so those targets ship behind a 'best effort' flag with the retry wrapper mandatory.

One process note: Q3 OKRs locked on June 26, and this is in there as a data-platforms commitment, so the memo mostly formalizes what leadership already expects.

Thanks all - long window, well run.

Dmitri

subject: HSPACE kickoff - synthetic humans at scale for 3D sensing
body:
Team,

Kicking off HSPACE. The thesis: 3D human sensing is bottlenecked on datasets with real 3D ground truth - multiple people, motion, occlusion, moving cameras - and we can manufacture that data synthetically. Our pipeline fits the GHUM body model to single scans, then re-targets and places animated, dressed humans into complex indoor and outdoor scenes. With a hundred base individuals plus parametric shape variation we get 1,600 distinct humans and an initial dataset north of one million frames, all compatible with real-time rendering and game engines.

Product framing: this becomes the training-data backbone for every 3D human pose/shape effort in the vision portfolio, plus an external evaluation server down the line.

Milestones: retargeting pipeline hardened by end of March, scene-placement QA pass through April, full render campaign in May, dataset v1 frozen by 2026-06-08.

Alina owns staffing/compute; Freya methodology; Farah and Milan the pipeline.

Lucia

subject: Re: HSPACE kickoff - staffing and render compute
body:
Lucia,

Staffing plan for the window:

- Freya 50% throughout (GHUM fitting quality, motion retargeting evaluation).
- Milan 70% (scene placement, engine export).
- Farah Haddad is committed at 60%+ to HSPACE for June 2026 - she owns the render-farm orchestration for the May campaign and then drives dataset packaging and the v1 freeze through early June. I have her calendar blocked for it.

Compute: the render campaign is CPU/GPU-mixed; we've sized it at ~40 titan-a100 GPUs best-effort for four weeks in May. No Vulcan reservation - renders tolerate preemption fine. Storage is the bigger ask: ~180 TB for the million-frame v1, which I've filed with the platform team.

One dependency: the parametric shape-variation sweep (the piece that takes us from 100 scans to 1,600 humans) needs Freya's fitting QA done first, so that's the critical path item for March.

Alina

subject: HSPACE status: retargeting solid, multi-person placement needs a QA gate
body:
Lucia, Alina,

Status ahead of the May render campaign. GHUM fitting QA is done on all 100 base scans; the parametric variation sweep produced the full 1,600-human set and dressed-human retargeting holds up well - under 3% of motion clips show visible skinning artifacts, and Milan's engine export runs clean.

The risk is jointly consistent multi-person scene placement. In our current outdoor scenes about 11% of sampled multi-person configurations have interpenetration or implausible contact when two moving people cross paths. That's high enough to contaminate training signal for occlusion-heavy benchmarks - which is exactly the regime this dataset is supposed to be strongest in. Proposal: add an automated collision/contact QA gate before a frame enters v1, at an estimated cost of ~8% render throughput.

If we accept the throughput hit we still make the June 8 freeze, but with maybe 0.9M frames instead of 1.1M. Want a decision this week so Farah can bake the gate into the orchestration.

Freya

subject: Re: HSPACE status: decision - QA gate in, outdoor scenes trimmed for v1
body:
All,

Decisions, confirming what we agreed in Tuesday's review:

1. The collision/contact QA gate ships in v1. Quality over raw frame count - 0.9M clean frames beats 1.1M with an 11% contamination rate in exactly our headline regime.
2. We trim the worst 4 outdoor scenes (the ones driving most interpenetration failures) rather than fixing them under deadline. They come back in v1.1.
3. Freeze date holds: 2026-06-08. Farah's orchestration keeps the render farm hot through then; Milan finalizes engine-export manifests the same week.

For the evaluation-server piece, that's a Q3 item and goes through Launch Review Board before anything is externally visible - I'll take the LRB paperwork.

Great catch on the placement issue, Freya. This is the difference between a dataset people cite and one they quietly drop.

Lucia

subject: Hyperbolic Agent kickoff - multi-horizon value learning
body:
Team,

Kicking off the Hyperbolic Agent effort for agents-rl. Basis is our open-source release on hyperbolic discounting and learning over multiple horizons: instead of one exponential discount, the agent maintains value heads across many gammas and combines them hyperbolically. The interesting product question isn't the discounting itself - it's the repeated finding that the multi-horizon auxiliary task makes the base agent stronger, especially on exploration-heavy games.

Scope: reproduce Hyperbolic/Multi-Rainbow from the shipped gin configs, then sweep the head count and exponent to find the cheapest configuration that keeps the gains. Milestones: repro by early April, sweep through May, recommendation memo by 2026-06-15 feeding the Q3 agent-training-stack decisions.

Halima leads experiments, Leilani infra, Gustavo analysis. Bao - staffing and compute note please, the Atari sweeps are the cost center here.

Ulla

subject: Re: Hyperbolic Agent kickoff - staffing, compute, Corpus timing
body:
Ulla,

Resourcing:

- Staffing: Halima 60%, Leilani 40%, Gustavo 50% through mid-June. No hiring ask.
- Compute: Atari sweeps sized at 48 titan-a100 GPUs best-effort. Multi-Rainbow with number_of_gammas=10 costs us roughly 1.4x a vanilla Rainbow run, so the May sweep is ~220 GPU-weeks total. Fits best-effort if we queue smartly; no Vulcan reservation.
- Platform: replay logs and eval episodes sit on Corpus v1 paths today. The Corpus v2 freeze is 2026-08-07, so we have headroom to keep replay logs on v1 through July and do the v2 migration as a post-project cleanup rather than burning sweep time on it now. Leilani will schedule that migration for early August.

One practical note: gin-binding sprawl bit us in week one (two runs silently used gamma_max=0.99 with different exponents), so Leilani is adding config hashing to the run metadata.

Bao

subject: Hyperbolic Agent status: repro done, sweep half through, one trade-off
body:
Ulla, Bao,

Status. Repro is done: hyperbolic_rainbow from the shipped gin config (number_of_gammas=10, hyp_exponent=0.01, gamma_max=0.99, acting policy largest_gamma) matches the released numbers within noise on our 12-game subset, and we see the expected outsized gain on MontezumaRevenge - +14% average return over the Rainbow baseline at 50M frames.

Sweep is half through. Early read: dropping to 5 gammas keeps ~90% of the auxiliary-task benefit at ~1.15x baseline cost, which would be the sweet spot for the training stack.

Trade-off to flag: acting with largest_gamma is best on exploration games but slightly hurts on dense-reward ones (-3% median). If we want one default config for the stack we either accept that, or ship per-game acting policies, which complicates the story. Gustavo is quantifying both options for the memo.

On track for the June 15 recommendation.

Halima

subject: Re: Hyperbolic Agent status: decision for the June 15 memo
body:
All,

Decision for the memo: we recommend the 5-gamma configuration as the default multi-horizon auxiliary task for the agent training stack - ~90% of the benefit at 1.15x cost is the right trade, and it's the version other teams will actually adopt. The 10-gamma largest_gamma config gets documented as the 'exploration mode' for sparse-reward domains like Montezuma, not as the default.

On the dense-reward regression: we accept the -3% median with the default acting policy rather than shipping per-game policies. One config, one story. Gustavo, please make sure the memo shows the regression honestly next to the exploration gains.

Bao - the memo went into the Q3 OKR discussion ahead of the June 26 lock, so numbers need to be final by June 15, no slips.

Thanks all, clean execution on this one.

Ulla

subject: HyperTransformer kickoff - few-shot personalization for small models
body:
Team,

Kicking off HyperTransformer. Core idea from our open-source release: a high-capacity transformer generates the weights of a small CNN directly from the support samples of a task, so the complexity of the task space lives in the transformer, not the tiny deployed model. That's a natural fit for on-device personalization: ship a small CNN, generate its weights per user/task in one shot, no on-device fine-tuning loop.

Scope this window: reproduce the supervised few-shot results on omniglot, miniImageNet and tieredImageNet; then evaluate the semi-supervised regime (unlabeled support samples) since real personalization data is mostly unlabeled; and produce a feasibility read on target-CNN sizes where the method actually wins.

Milestones: repro by mid-May, semi-supervised evaluation by late June, feasibility memo at the July 13 close. Deshawn owns staffing/compute; Carmen methodology; Vera experiments; Saoirse data tooling.

Lucia

subject: Re: HyperTransformer kickoff - staffing, compute, dataset caches
body:
Lucia,

Resourcing:

- Staffing: Vera 60%, Saoirse 40%, Carmen 50%. Stable through July 13.
- Compute: transformer training runs fit on 32 titan-a100 best-effort; the semi-supervised sweeps in June push us to ~64 for three weeks. I don't think we need a Vulcan reservation; will revisit if best-effort queues get ugly.
- Data: the trainer consumes datasets as saved NumPy caches (omniglot, miniImageNet, tieredImageNet). Saoirse is rebuilding those caches on Corpus rather than using ad-hoc copies. Timing matters: per Jun Varga, the Corpus v2 migration freeze is 2026-07-10, so all three dataset caches must be regenerated on v2 paths before that date - I've put the cache work at the front of Saoirse's queue, target end of May, so we're not touching migration anywhere near our July close.

No budget asks. One risk: miniImageNet raw pickles come from an external mirror; Saoirse is archiving them internally this week.

Deshawn

subject: HyperTransformer status: repro green, semi-supervised gains real but size-dependent
body:
Lucia, Deshawn,

Status. Supervised repro is green on all three benchmarks - omniglot essentially saturated, miniImageNet and tieredImageNet 5-way results within 0.4 pts of the released numbers, off the rebuilt Corpus caches.

Semi-supervised: adding unlabeled support samples gives us +2.3 pts on miniImageNet 5-way 1-shot with our smallest target CNN. That's the regime the release predicted - the win concentrates where the target CNN is too small for a fixed universal embedding to do the work, and the transformer modulating all generated weights actually matters.

The catch, and it's the key feasibility finding so far: at our largest target size the semi-supervised gain shrinks to +0.5 pts and supervised parity with a plain fine-tuning baseline gets close. So the product story is specifically small-model personalization, not a general few-shot win. Carmen is mapping the crossover curve (accuracy delta vs target-CNN params) for the memo - that plot will carry the July recommendation.

Vera

subject: Re: HyperTransformer status: decision for the feasibility memo
body:
All,

Decision for the July 13 memo: we position HyperTransformer as the weight-generation engine for small-model on-device personalization only. Carmen's crossover curve is unambiguous - below ~200K target-CNN parameters we win clearly (with the semi-supervised +2.3 pt result as the headline), above it we don't beat fine-tuning enough to justify the serving complexity. The memo recommends a Q3 prototype with one partner team on the small end, and explicitly recommends against pitching this as a general few-shot platform.

Saoirse - please snapshot the eval configs and Corpus cache manifests with the memo so the Q3 team starts from a reproducible state. Deshawn - nothing in this plan needs Vulcan, which will make Ines's quarter easier.

Good, honest feasibility work. This is exactly what the portfolio needed to know.

Lucia

subject: iALS kickoff - an honest recommendation baseline for the platform
body:
Team,

Kicking off the iALS baseline track. Context: our open-source work ('Revisiting the Performance of iALS on Item Recommendation Benchmarks' and 'iALS++: Speeding up Matrix Factorization with Subspace Optimization') showed that a well-tuned implicit ALS is embarrassingly competitive with neural recommenders at a fraction of the cost. For data-platforms, the goal is a trustworthy internal baseline: any team proposing a fancy recommender should have to beat tuned iALS first.

Scope: reproduce the NCF-protocol results on MovieLens 1M and Pinterest, package the tuning recipe (holdout generation included), and hand Evalline a runnable baseline config. Milestones: environment and data by mid-Feb, repro by late March, packaged baseline + write-up by 2026-04-27.

Bilal leads repro, Linnea tuning methodology, Rosa packaging, Oyin infra. Deshawn - resourcing note please. This one is cheap on compute and heavy on rigor.

Dmitri

subject: Re: iALS kickoff - resourcing + Corpus migration timing
body:
Dmitri,

Resourcing, short version because this really is a small footprint:

- Staffing: Bilal 50%, Linnea 40%, Rosa 30%, Oyin 20%.
- Compute: CPU-dominant; a handful of titan-a100 GPUs best-effort for the sweep weeks. Nothing to reserve.
- Data: the NCF benchmark datasets (MovieLens 1M, Pinterest) are getting registered on Corpus so Evalline can consume the baseline reproducibly. Planning note: the Corpus v2 migration freeze is 2026-06-26, so Rosa will register everything as v2-native from the start - our project closes in April, but I don't want the packaged baseline to be one of those things that breaks in late June because it pointed at v1 paths.

One genuine annoyance: the upstream NCF evaluation code needs a Python 2.7 runtime. Oyin is isolating it in a container; if security pushes back on py2.7 we may need Bilal to port the eval loop instead, which would cost ~2 weeks.

Deshawn

subject: iALS status: Table 5 reproduced, one methodology risk on repetitions
body:
Dmitri, Deshawn,

Status. MovieLens 1M reproduces cleanly with the published settings (embedding_dim 192, 12 epochs, regularization 0.007, unobserved_weight 0.3) - HR@10 and NDCG@10 land within 0.003 of the Table 5 numbers. Pinterest matches too with its own config (16 epochs, regularization 0.02, unobserved_weight 0.007). The py2.7 container worked, so no porting detour needed - good call Oyin.

The methodology risk: published numbers are means over 10 repetitions, and run-to-run variance on Pinterest is big enough that a single lucky run can look +0.004 over the mean. If Evalline consumes a single-seed baseline, teams will 'beat' it with noise. Linnea's proposal, which I support: the packaged baseline ships as a 10-seed protocol with mean and standard deviation, and Evalline gates on the mean minus one sigma.

Remaining: holdout-generation tooling for hyperparameter tuning, then packaging. On track for April 27.

Bilal

subject: Re: iALS status: decision - 10-seed protocol adopted, closing April 27
body:
All,

Decision: the 10-seed protocol is adopted as proposed - the baseline ships with mean and standard deviation over 10 repetitions, and the Evalline gate is mean minus one sigma. I'd rather have teams grumble about a strict gate than have the platform bless noise as progress.

Close-out plan for April 27: Rosa finishes packaging (both dataset configs plus the holdout-generation script), Linnea writes the two-page tuning recipe, Bilal freezes the final numbers table. Handoff meeting with Tomas Fofana's Evalline team is booked for the last week of April.

One caveat for the write-up: the py2.7 container is a reproduction artifact, not a supported dependency - the packaged baseline itself is py3-only. Please make that unmissable so nobody cargo-cults a 2.7 runtime into production.

Good, unglamorous work - this is what platform credibility is made of.

Dmitri

subject: ICETEA kickoff - causal benchmarks where images are the confounder
body:
Team,

Kicking off ICETEA. The gap our release identified: benchmarking causal-inference methods is genuinely hard, and existing benchmarks rarely have both a plausible causal story and a real need for ML models. Our answer is a semi-synthetic benchmark where retinal fundus images act as covariates - there's decent evidence they correlate with general vascular condition, so adjusting on them for confounding is scientifically defensible, and you can't do that adjustment without an image model.

For data-platforms the deliverable is a benchmark suite: IHDP and ACIC as the standard baselines, plus our fundus-image semi-synthetic benchmark with the beam pipeline to regenerate it at scale.

Milestones: IHDP/ACIC estimators reproduced by mid-March, image benchmark generation pipeline running by mid-April, benchmark v1 plus docs by 2026-05-11.

Halima leads estimators, Tereza the image pipeline, Nikhil experiments, Linnea data engineering. Alina - staffing/compute note please.

Dmitri

subject: Re: ICETEA kickoff - staffing + the de-duplication build
body:
Dmitri,

Resourcing:

- Staffing: Halima 50%, Tereza 60%, Nikhil 40%, Linnea 50%.
- Compute: image-model training for the confounder adjustment fits on 24 titan-a100 best-effort; the beam pipeline is CPU-heavy but bursty.

One scope addition I want to be explicit about, since it's real engineering: the fundus corpus has a serious near-duplicate problem (same eye, multiple visits, slightly different framing), and duplicates across the train/eval split would quietly corrupt the causal benchmark. There's nothing on the shelf that handles image near-duplicates at our scale, so we're scoping and staffing a dataset de-duplication pipeline built from scratch - embedding-based near-duplicate detection with a clustering pass, wired into the beam job. Linnea takes it at 50% for roughly six weeks, with Tereza consulting on the embedding choice.

That's the only thing on this project I'd call a genuine build rather than assembly, and it's on the critical path for the mid-April pipeline milestone. Flag now if the six weeks worries you.

Alina

subject: ICETEA status: estimators reproduced, UKB preprocessing is the long pole
body:
Dmitri, Alina,

Status. The estimator suite reproduces on IHDP and ACIC - all estimators in estimators.py land within published tolerances, and Nikhil's experiment configs (via config.py) sweep cleanly.

Image side: Linnea's de-duplication pipeline is working end-to-end on a 10% sample - it's flagging about 7% of images as near-duplicates, which confirms the split-leakage worry was justified. The long pole is the UK Biobank-style preprocessing in ukb.py: the beam pipeline hits throughput limits on the resize/quality-filter stage, currently ~14 hours per full pass where we budgeted 6. Tereza has a fix (fusing the filter stages) in review.

Risk to the May 11 date: if the fused pipeline doesn't hold, benchmark v1 ships with the 60% subset that's already clean rather than the full corpus. Statistically fine for v1 - the semi-synthetic treatment assignment is ours anyway - but we should agree on that fallback now rather than at the deadline.

Halima

subject: Re: ICETEA status: decision - v1 ships on the clean subset
body:
All,

Decision for the May 11 close: benchmark v1 ships on the clean 72% subset (the fused pipeline helped but didn't fully close the throughput gap - thanks Tereza, 14h down to 9h). Full-corpus regeneration becomes the first v1.1 item.

Rationale: the causal story doesn't depend on corpus size, it depends on split hygiene - and the de-dup pipeline is exactly what makes the benchmark trustworthy. Linnea, please write the de-dup methodology up as its own section in the docs; the 7% near-duplicate rate is a headline finding for anyone using medical imaging in evaluation, and I want it visible.

Also for the docs: an explicit caution that IHDP/ACIC numbers and fundus-benchmark numbers are not comparable across estimator families - Halima has the details.

Handoff review Friday May 8, then we freeze. Privacy note: the fundus corpus stays internal-only pending Kofi Weber's review; docs should say so.

Dmitri

subject: IEG kickoff - training that survives noisy labels
body:
Team,

Kicking off the IEG workstream. Our labeling platform produces labels of, let's be honest, mixed quality - and every consumer team pays for it in silent accuracy loss. Our open-source work on meta sample re-weighting gives us two tools: IEG (distilling effective supervision from severe label noise) and FSR (fast sample re-weighting without reward data). The claim worth productizing: with the right re-weighting, training stays usable even at extreme noise ratios.

Scope this window: reproduce IEG on CIFAR100 at 20/40/80% uniform noise with wrn28-10, evaluate FSR as the cheaper alternative, and produce a recommendation for a 'noise-robust training' option on the platform.

Milestones: IEG repro by end of May, FSR comparison by end of June, recommendation memo by 2026-07-13.

Tereza leads methodology, Bilal experiments, Chiara and Emeka infra. Bruno - resourcing note when ready.

Dmitri

subject: Re: IEG kickoff - staffing + we need our own eval harness
body:
Dmitri,

Resourcing:

- Staffing: Tereza 50%, Bilal 50%, Chiara 70%, Emeka 50%.
- Compute: the noise-ratio sweeps parallelize per-ratio on single GPUs, so 32 titan-a100 best-effort is plenty. No reservation ask.

The bigger call: we're going to build an internal evaluation harness from scratch for the noisy-label work - controlled noise injection (uniform and asymmetric), per-noise-ratio eval matrices, seed management, and re-weighting diagnostics like weight-distribution tracking. I looked at what exists and nothing supports injecting calibrated label corruption into the eval loop, which is the whole experiment here. Chiara owns it at 70% with Emeka at 50%; roughly seven weeks, harness stable by mid-June so the FSR comparison runs on it.

It's a real cost, but every future noise-robustness claim on the platform needs exactly this machinery, so I'd rather build it properly once.

Bruno

subject: IEG status: 80% noise result reproduced, meta-step cost is the trade-off
body:
Dmitri, Bruno,

Status. IEG repro is done on CIFAR100 with wrn28-10 across 20/40/80% uniform noise - at 80% noise we hold within 1.2 pts of the released accuracy, which is the number that makes people sit up. Also confirmed the augmentation note from the release: switching AutoAugment to RandAugment is on par, within noise, so we'll standardize on RandAugment for the platform since it's simpler to serve. Asymmetric-noise CIFAR10 configs are queued on Chiara's harness this week - the noise-injection module made spinning those up trivial.

The trade-off for the memo: IEG's meta-step roughly doubles training cost versus standard training. Early FSR runs recover most of the benefit at low noise for a fraction of the overhead, but degrade faster at 80%. So the likely recommendation shape is tiered: FSR as the default noise-robust option, IEG reserved for known-bad label sources. Bilal is filling in the cost/accuracy frontier now.

On track for July 13.

Tereza

subject: Re: IEG status: decision - tiered recommendation adopted
body:
All,

Decision for the July 13 memo: we adopt the tiered recommendation as Tereza framed it. FSR becomes the default noise-robust training option on the platform (most of the benefit, modest overhead), and IEG is the heavy-duty mode for label sources we know are severely noisy - the 80% uniform-noise CIFAR100 result is the evidence that it holds up where FSR fades. RandAugment is the standard augmentation in both modes.

Bilal's cost/accuracy frontier chart goes in as the decision graphic; the 2x meta-step cost for IEG needs to be stated plainly so nobody turns it on by default.

Bruno - the harness Chiara and Emeka built deserves its own paragraph in the memo. Controlled noise injection with seed management is what made these claims defensible, and I want leadership to see where the seven weeks went.

Q3 follow-on is a pilot with one real labeling-pipeline consumer; I'll bring it to the OKR check-in.

Dmitri

subject: IGT optimizer kickoff - do transported gradients pay off at ResNet scale?
body:
Team,

Kicking off the IGT evaluation for trust-theory. Our open-source release implements Implicit Gradient Transport with Anytime Average - reducing variance in online optimization by extrapolating gradients rather than computing them at the current parameter values. The question this project answers for the org: does that variance reduction translate into more predictable, more trustworthy training curves at ResNet scale, or does it stay a theory result?

Scope: run the released resnet_main.py framework, compare IGT against our standard optimizers on convergence variance across seeds, and sweep tail_fraction for the anytime-average window. Deliverable is a recommendation on whether IGT enters the blessed optimizer list.

Milestones inside our short window: framework running by mid-Feb, main comparison done by mid-March, memo by 2026-04-13.

Efe owns methodology, Halima experiments, Emeka and Bilal infra. Bao - resourcing note please.

Ximena

subject: Re: IGT optimizer kickoff - staffing + evaluation harness build
body:
Ximena,

Resourcing:

- Staffing: Efe 50%, Halima 40%, Emeka 60%, Bilal 40% through April 13.
- Compute: multi-seed ResNet runs are the cost - 5 seeds x 4 optimizer configs. We'll use 32 titan-a100 best-effort; the released framework is a fork of TPU-era resnet code, and Emeka has it running fine on GPU.

One build item to be upfront about: we're standing up an internal evaluation harness from scratch for optimizer comparisons - multi-seed orchestration, variance-across-seeds metrics, and curve alignment that correctly handles IGT's true-vs-shifted parameter distinction (eval_igt mode evaluates at the true parameters stored in slots, and naive comparisons silently plot the shifted ones - we nearly got burned by that in week one). Nothing we have does seed-variance reporting properly, so Emeka owns the build at 60% with Bilal at 40%, about five weeks.

That harness is most of Emeka's allocation, but it's also the reusable artifact this project leaves behind.

Bao

subject: IGT status: variance reduction is real, wall-clock story is mixed
body:
Ximena, Bao,

Status. Main comparison is done on the harness. Headline: IGT with anytime averaging cuts across-seed variance of validation accuracy by ~40% at matched step counts versus our default momentum config, and the tail_fraction sweep shows the effect is robust between 0.3 and 0.7. The eval_igt mode (true parameters from the slots, not the shifted variables) was essential - measured on shifted parameters the 'benefit' looks 2x larger than it really is, which is exactly the kind of overstatement the trust-theory portfolio exists to catch.

The mixed news: per-step overhead from maintaining the transport is ~8%, so at matched wall-clock the variance win shrinks to ~30%. Still real, but the memo has to quote wall-clock numbers or we're kidding ourselves.

Risk to the date: one lr_decay_step_fraction interaction produces occasional late-training spikes on 2 of 20 runs; Halima is isolating it this week. If it's config-specific we exclude that cell with a note; if it's inherent, the recommendation gets a caveat.

Efe

subject: Re: IGT status: decision - conditional listing, wall-clock numbers only
body:
All,

Decision for the April 13 memo: IGT enters the blessed optimizer list as a conditional entry - recommended where training-curve predictability matters more than raw throughput (canary training, reproducibility-sensitive evals), not as a general default. All quoted numbers are wall-clock-matched; the ~30% variance reduction at 8% overhead is the honest headline, and the step-matched 40% goes in a footnote with the methodology.

On the late-training spikes: Halima traced them to an lr_decay_step_fraction cell interacting badly with the transport - config-specific, so that cell is excluded with an explicit note and a recommended safe range.

Bao, please register the optimizer-comparison harness with an owner going forward; the true-vs-shifted parameter lesson alone justifies keeping it alive.

Clean, skeptical work - exactly what this portfolio is for.

Ximena

subject: IME kickoff - forecasts you can explain to an auditor
body:
Team,

Kicking off IME. Our open-source Interpretable Mixture of Experts work gives us a forecasting architecture where the experts themselves are interpretable models and an assignment module (interpretable linear, or black-box LSTM) routes each sample - crucially, to a single expert at inference time, so every prediction comes with a readable explanation of which regime produced it.

Product motivation: internal forecasting consumers (capacity planning, spend forecasting) keep asking for explanations their reviewers will accept. IME is the credible middle ground between 'linear model everywhere' and 'trust the LSTM'.

Scope: reproduce the released results on the Electricity (ECL) and Rossmann datasets with both IME_WW and IME_BW variants at num_experts=20, then evaluate on one internal forecasting workload. Milestones: repro by mid-June, internal-workload eval by mid-July, recommendation by 2026-07-27.

Kaia leads modeling, Amara infra, Efe evaluation methodology. Jelena - resourcing note please.

Dmitri

subject: Re: IME kickoff - staffing + synthetic-data pipeline build
body:
Dmitri,

Resourcing:

- Staffing: Kaia 60%, Amara 60%, Efe 30% through the window.
- Compute: trivial by portfolio standards - these train on single GPUs, so a small titan-a100 best-effort slice covers everything including sweeps over utilization_hp and smoothness_hp.

The substantial build: for the internal-workload eval we can't move the real forecasting data across privacy boundaries on our timeline (Kofi's review SLA is 2-3 weeks and the data owner wants scoping first). So we're scoping and staffing a synthetic-data generation pipeline from scratch - regime-switching time series with configurable seasonality, trend breaks, and covariate structure that mimics the internal workload's statistics without containing any real records. Amara owns the build at 60% for about six weeks, with Kaia specifying the regime structure. It doubles as the stress-test bed: we can dial regime overlap and see exactly where single-expert assignment breaks.

Nothing else exotic. Budget-neutral.

Jelena

subject: IME status: repro done, interpretability tax quantified
body:
Dmitri, Jelena,

Status. Repro complete on both datasets with num_experts=20: IME_BW (LSTM assignment) matches the released numbers on Rossmann and ECL; IME_WW (linear assignment) lands where expected, slightly behind BW. Amara's synthetic pipeline is generating regime-switching series that match the internal workload's autocorrelation and seasonality profile well - the data owner's team eyeballed the marginals and signed off on fidelity.

The finding that will shape the recommendation: single-expert assignment at inference costs about 4% RMSE versus soft mixing on the synthetic bed when regimes overlap heavily, but under 1% when regimes are cleanly separated. Our internal workload looks like the clean case, fortunately. Also, smoothness_hp at 0.01 matters more than we expected - dropping it produces expert-flapping, where consecutive timesteps flip experts and the 'explanation' becomes noise. Efe wants flap-rate reported as a first-class metric alongside RMSE, which I support.

On track for mid-July internal eval.

Kaia

subject: Re: IME status: decision - IME_WW recommended for the pilot
body:
All,

Decision for the July 27 close: we recommend IME_WW - the fully interpretable variant with linear assignment - for the internal forecasting pilot. On the internal-workload eval it finished within 1.5% RMSE of IME_BW (the clean-regime story held), and a linear assignment module means the whole prediction path is explainable, which is the actual product requirement. IME_BW goes in the memo as the fallback if pilot accuracy disappoints.

Flap-rate ships as a first-class metric next to RMSE, with the smoothness_hp=0.01 guidance baked into the default config. Efe was right to push on this - an explanation that changes every timestep is worse than none.

Jelena - please make sure Amara's synthetic-generation pipeline gets documented and kept; dialing regime overlap to find the failure boundary is a trick the whole portfolio should steal.

Pilot kickoff with the capacity-planning team targeted for August.

Dmitri

subject: imGHUM kickoff - implicit human models for scan completion
body:
Team,

Kicking off imGHUM. Our release gives us implicit generative models of 3D human shape, facial expression, and articulated pose that share the GHUM latent space - with gender-neutral and gender-specific models for full body, head, and both hands. Two properties make it a product candidate: fast differentiable signed-distance queries at arbitrary spatial points, and topology-freedom, which lets imGHUM sit as the inner layer under personalized, clothed, animatable humans.

The concrete bet for this window: point-cloud reconstruction and completion for our scan-processing pipeline. Partial scans are today's biggest source of manual cleanup, and imGHUM's SDF queries plus semantics should automate a big slice of it.

Milestones: models integrated and SDF-query benchmarks by mid-May, scan-completion evaluation on our internal capture set by mid-June, go/no-go memo by 2026-06-29.

Yara leads research, Efe evaluation, Farah and Gustavo the pipeline integration. Daniela - resourcing note please.

Lucia

subject: Re: imGHUM kickoff - staffing, compute, Corpus migration deadline
body:
Lucia,

Resourcing:

- Staffing: Yara 50%, Efe 40%, Gustavo 60%; Farah 30% through May for the pipeline integration scaffolding (her calendar is heavily contested for June, so I've front-loaded her portion deliberately).
- Compute: SDF query benchmarks and fitting runs sit fine on 24 titan-a100 best-effort. No reservation ask.
- Data/platform: the internal capture set (raw scans plus registered point clouds, ~9 TB) lives on Corpus v1 paths today. The Corpus v2 migration freeze is 2026-07-10, and our window closes June 29 - so Gustavo migrates the capture set to v2 in the first half of May, before the evaluation runs start. That way our published eval manifests are already v2-native and nothing we hand off breaks when the freeze lands eleven days after our close.

One dependency to watch: the head and hand models need a licensing-note review before any external-facing use; flagged to legal, not a blocker for internal eval.

Daniela

subject: imGHUM status: completion works, hands are the weak spot
body:
Lucia, Daniela,

Status. Integration is done and the SDF-query benchmarks look strong - differentiable signed-distance evaluation is fast enough that completion fitting runs at interactive-adjacent speeds on a single GPU. On the internal capture set, body-scan completion recovers plausible geometry on 83% of our partial-scan test cases, versus 61% for the current heuristic pipeline, and the implicit semantics give us surface labeling for free, which the cleanup tooling team immediately asked for.

Weak spot: hands. On scans where fingers are partially occluded, the hand models produce anatomically plausible but wrong finger poses in ~30% of cases - the latent prior dominates when observations are thin, exactly as you'd expect from a generative model. Efe's take is that for the scan-cleanup product this is acceptable if we flag low-confidence hand regions instead of silently completing them; confidence comes cheap from the observation coverage stats.

Decision needed by mid-June: ship v1 with flagged-hands, or hold for a hand-specific fitting pass. My recommendation is flag-and-ship.

Yara

subject: Re: imGHUM status: decision - flag-and-ship, go for scan cleanup v1
body:
All,

Decision for the June 29 memo: it's a GO for scan-cleanup v1, flag-and-ship on hands. The 83% vs 61% completion result carries the case on its own, and Efe's framing is right - a flagged low-confidence hand region keeps a human in the loop exactly where the model is guessing. Silent completion would have been the version that erodes trust.

Scope notes for the memo: hand-specific fitting is the first v1.1 item, and the surface-semantics labeling goes in as an explicit bonus deliverable since the cleanup tooling team is already building against it. External-facing anything remains gated on the licensing-note review plus Launch Review Board - internal pipeline use only until both clear.

Gustavo - thanks for the early v2 migration; handing off eval manifests that are already freeze-proof is the quiet kind of competence I appreciate.

Lucia

subject: IMP kickoff - one multimodal encoder for retrieval
body:
Team,

Kicking off the IMP track for graphs-retrieval. Our open-source MAX & IMP release (alternating gradient descent plus mixture-of-experts for integrated multimodal perception) trains a single model across image, video, and audio - IMP-MoE-B at 90M params posts 83.2 on IN1k, 68.2 on K400 and 88.7 on UCF101, which for one shared encoder is remarkable. For us the prize is multimodal retrieval: one embedding space over all modalities instead of three bolted-together towers.

Scope this window: reproduce IMP-B and IMP-MoE-B from the released experiment configs, then run an IMP-MoE-L-scale training to test whether the retrieval-relevant representations keep improving with scale. Milestones: base repros by end of May, the MoE-L run in early July, findings memo by 2026-07-20.

Csilla leads research, Tereza and Vera experiments, Jorge infra. Bruno - resourcing note please; the MoE-L run is the big compute item and needs booking early.

Anders

subject: Re: IMP kickoff - staffing + Vulcan booking for the MoE-L run
body:
Anders,

Resourcing:

- Staffing: Csilla 60%, Tereza 40%, Vera 50%, Jorge 60% through July 20.
- Base repros (IMP-B, IMP-MoE-B): 64 titan-a100 best-effort covers it. Jorge has the released config stack (imp_base.all.train / sparse_moe_imp_base.all.train) running already.
- The big one, booked as you asked: we hold the vulcan-h100 reservation - 128 accelerators for the week of 2026-07-06 - for the IMP-MoE-L-scale training run. Went through the Infra Lead reservation process and it's confirmed on my side; that placement gives us buffer after the run for the July 20 memo, and it's comfortably clear of the Vulcan maintenance window in late June.

Risk to note: MoE-L at 350M params is at the edge of what one week at 128 H100s buys us, so Csilla is preparing a reduced-token-budget variant as the fallback if throughput disappoints mid-week.

Bruno

subject: IMP status: base repros green, AGD schedule sensitivity is the risk
body:
Anders, Bruno,

Status. Both base repros are green: IMP-B lands 80.4 IN1k / 63.5 K400 (released: 80.5 / 63.6 - within noise), and IMP-MoE-B matches on the video suite including the 88.7 UCF101 headline. Audio (ESC50) reproduces as well. Retrieval probes off the shared embedding space look promising - cross-modal recall@10 beats our current two-tower baseline by 9% on the internal video-text set.

The risk for the MoE-L run: the alternating gradient descent schedule is sensitive at scale. In our B-scale ablations, reordering the modality alternation changed final IN1k by up to 0.8 pts, and we haven't validated the released schedule at L scale. If the first two days of the Vulcan week show instability, we fall back to Csilla's reduced-token-budget variant with the conservative schedule rather than burning the week debugging.

Vera has the eval configs (sparse_moe_imp_base.all.eval and friends) staged so results flow the moment training checkpoints land.

Csilla

subject: Re: IMP status: decision - retrieval prototype goes ahead on MoE-B
body:
All,

Wrapping up ahead of the July 20 memo. The Vulcan week was bumpier than hoped - we lost roughly a day and a half at the start to allocation churn on the cluster, so the MoE-L run went out with the reduced-token-budget fallback. Even so: scaling held, with the L-scale checkpoint adding +2.1 cross-modal recall@10 over MoE-B on the internal set.

Decisions:
1. The multimodal retrieval prototype for Q3 builds on IMP-MoE-B - reproducible, well-characterized, cheap to serve. The L-scale result goes in the memo as scaling evidence, not as the serving target.
2. AGD schedule sensitivity gets its own section; anyone scaling this further needs Csilla's ablation table first.
3. Jorge writes up the allocation-churn incident for Ines's team - if we book full-week reservations we need them to actually start on day one.

Good recovery under compute pressure. Memo draft to me by the 17th please.

Anders

subject: Project Sirocco kickoff - training to the metric that actually ships
body:
Team,

Kicking off what we're calling Project Sirocco internally - our trust-theory effort built on the Implicit Constrained Optimization (ICO) release. The problem it attacks: production classifiers are judged on rate metrics with a thresholded form - false negative rate at a fixed false positive rate, precision at fixed recall, AUC-PR - but trained on proxies. ICO's trick is expressing the threshold as a function of the model parameters via the implicit function theorem, so you can optimize the deployed metric directly, constraint and all.

Scope for Sirocco: reproduce the FNR-at-fixed-FPR results on the CelebA attribute tasks, then evaluate on two internal screening classifiers where the FPR budget is contractual.

Milestones: CelebA repro by mid-March, internal-classifier evaluation through April, recommendation memo by 2026-05-25.

Fumiko owns methodology, Wanjiru implementation, Nikhil experiments. Ivo - staffing and compute note please. Use the Sirocco tag on docs so things stay findable.

Ximena

subject: Re: Project Sirocco kickoff - staffing and compute
body:
Ximena,

Resourcing for Sirocco:

- Staffing: Wanjiru 60%, Fumiko 50%, Nikhil 40% through late May. No hiring ask.
- Compute: light - CelebA attribute classifiers train on single GPUs, so a 12-16 GPU slice of titan-a100 best-effort covers the repro matrix (attributes x target FPRs x sigmoid temperatures). The internal-classifier phase runs on the owning teams' existing training setups, we just bring the ICO loss.
- Data access: the two internal screening classifiers involve sensitive data, so I've filed the Privacy Review paperwork already - their 2-3 week SLA means clearance should land just as the CelebA repro finishes. Filed under the Sirocco codename per your doc-tagging note.

One planning caution: the second internal classifier's owning team is mid-reorg; if their eval infra isn't stable by early April I'd rather drop to one internal case than rush two. Flagging now so it's not a surprise in the memo.

Ivo

subject: Sirocco status: CelebA repro done, sigmoid temperature is the sharp edge
body:
Ximena, Ivo,

Sirocco status. CelebA repro is complete: on our attribute set, ICO improves FNR at the fixed FPR target versus the cross-entropy-plus-post-hoc-threshold baseline on 9 of 11 attributes, with the median improvement around 8% relative. Constraint satisfaction is the real story - post-hoc thresholding misses the FPR budget on held-out data far more often than ICO does, which is exactly the property the contractual-FPR use cases need.

The sharp edge: sigmoid_temp. The implicit-function-theorem machinery needs the thresholded rate to be smooth enough, and the results are sensitive to that temperature - too low and gradients get spiky, too high and the FPR constraint goes slack on eval. Fumiko has a tuning recipe (validate on the constraint gap, not the objective) that stabilizes it, but it needs to be in the memo as required practice, not a footnote.

Internal case one is underway. Case two: the owning team's reorg did eat their eval infra, as Ivo predicted - recommend we formally drop to one.

Wanjiru

subject: Re: Sirocco status: decisions for the May 25 memo
body:
All,

Decisions for the Sirocco close-out memo:

1. We formally drop internal case two - one deep case study beats two shallow ones, and the reorg isn't our problem to wait out. The memo says so plainly.
2. Internal case one carries the recommendation: ICO held the contractual FPR budget on held-out data across all four monthly slices while cutting FNR ~6% relative. That's the number the screening team's leadership cares about.
3. Fumiko's sigmoid_temp tuning recipe (validate on constraint gap, not objective) goes in as required practice, boxed and bolded. Anyone adopting ICO without it will produce exactly the slack-constraint failures we're trying to eliminate.
4. Recommendation: ICO becomes the trust-theory-endorsed method for thresholded rate-metric training where constraint satisfaction is contractual; general rollout gets scoped as a Q3 proposal.

Thanks all - Sirocco lands on time on May 25.

Ximena

subject: IPDF kickoff - pose uncertainty that survives symmetry
body:
Team,

Kicking off the IPDF track. Our release represents probability distributions over the rotation manifold SO(3) implicitly - the model scores (image, rotation) pairs, so a symmetric object naturally gets a multi-modal pose distribution instead of a single wrong answer with high confidence. For data-platforms this slots into the pose-labeling pipeline: calibrated pose uncertainty is what downstream auto-labeling gates on, and current regressors are confidently wrong on symmetric parts.

Scope: reproduce the SYMSOL I results from the released configs, benchmark evaluation cost (the dense rotation-grid evaluation is the known expensive bit), and prototype the labeling-pipeline integration on our internal parts set.

Milestones: SYMSOL repro by end of May, cost benchmark and the big eval sweep in June, integration recommendation by 2026-07-06.

Yara leads research, Katya experiments, Nikhil integration, Leilani infra. Santiago - resourcing note please, including the June compute booking.

Dmitri

subject: Re: IPDF kickoff - staffing + June Vulcan booking
body:
Dmitri,

Resourcing:

- Staffing: Yara 40%, Katya 60%, Nikhil 50%, Leilani 40% through July 6.
- Day-to-day: training runs are single-GPU-friendly (batch 128 per the released SYMSOL config); 16 titan-a100 best-effort covers the repro matrix.
- The June booking: we hold the vulcan-h100 reservation - 256 accelerators for the week of 2026-06-15 - for the full evaluation sweep. The driver is evaluation, not training: resolving tightly-focused densities on SO(3) needs the dense rotation grid (2M+ query points per example), and doing that across the whole SYMSOL suite plus our internal parts set is a genuinely large batch job. Placement note: Vulcan's maintenance window is June 22-24, so our week lands us right before it - if we slip the sweep we lose three more days on top, which is why Leilani is doing a dry run at 1/10 scale the week prior.

No other asks. Budget fits the existing envelope.

Santiago

subject: IPDF status: SYMSOL repro green, eval-grid memory is the risk for next week
body:
Dmitri, Santiago,

Status before the big week. SYMSOL I repro is green with the released recipe (random SO(3) sampling, 3 Fourier components, the [256,256,256,256] head, 100k iterations): distributions on the symmetric shapes come out properly multi-modal - the cube's 24-fold symmetry shows up as 24 clean modes - and average log-likelihood matches the published numbers within tolerance. The 4-Fourier-component cube config also reproduces.

The risk for the sweep: memory. At 2M+ rotation queries per example the eval batches blow past single-GPU memory unless test_batch_size stays at 1 and queries are chunked; Leilani's dry run at 1/10 scale caught a chunking bug that would have OOMed us mid-sweep on the real thing. Fixed, and the dry run now projects the full suite comfortably inside our reserved week - with about 20% headroom, which I'd like to keep as slack rather than adding configs.

Integration prototype: Nikhil has IPDF uncertainty wired into the labeling gate on a 500-part sample; early precision numbers look promising and go in the next update.

Katya

subject: Re: IPDF status: decision - labeling-gate integration recommended
body:
All,

Closing out for the July 6 memo. The June sweep completed inside the reserved week (the 20% slack got used, for the record - Katya was right to defend it), and the numbers make the case: on the internal parts set, gating auto-labels on IPDF pose uncertainty cuts wrong-pose label acceptance by 71% on symmetric parts at a 9% throughput cost, versus the regressor-confidence gate.

Decision: the memo recommends IPDF as the pose-uncertainty gate for the labeling pipeline, phased in starting with part families where symmetry is documented. The dense-grid evaluation cost stays a batch-mode reality - the memo is explicit that this gate runs offline, not in any interactive path, until someone funds a distillation effort.

Santiago - the dry-run-before-reserved-week practice goes in the memo as a recommended pattern. Cheap insurance that saved us the week, twice.

Dmitri

subject: Infinite Nature kickoff - perpetual scenes from a single photo
body:
Team,

Kicking off Infinite Nature. Our open-source release does perpetual view generation - fly into a single RGB image of a natural scene and keep generating plausible landscape forever. It's the most demo-able thing in the vision portfolio, and that's the plan: a polished interactive experience (built off the release's HTML frontend concept) as the centerpiece of our June external demo slot, pending Launch Review Board.

Scope: get the released model running in our serving environment, retrain on our licensed aerial-coastline corpus so the external demo isn't leaning on third-party data, and harden the interactive frontend. Umar owns the model work, Kaia generation quality, Farah serving integration, Oyin the frontend.

Milestones: local pipeline reproduced by early April, retraining through May, LRB submission and demo freeze by 2026-06-22.

Deshawn - resourcing note please, including the TPU ask for retraining.

Lucia

subject: Re: Infinite Nature kickoff - staffing + the June TPU week
body:
Lucia,

Resourcing:

- Staffing: Umar 50%, Kaia 40%, Oyin 50%; Farah 40% on serving integration through May (June is tight for her, so serving needs to be functionally done by end of May - noted in the plan).
- Compute: repro and iteration on 24 titan-a100 best-effort. For the final full retraining run on the licensed corpus, we hold the cirrus-tpu reservation - 128 accelerators for the week of 2026-06-08 - out of the vision portfolio's quarterly allocation. That lands the retrained checkpoint about a week before the June 22 demo freeze, with the intervening days for eval and demo integration. It's tight but deliberate: earlier weeks would mean retraining on an unfinished corpus.
- One build annoyance: the differentiable renderer (tf_mesh_renderer) needs the gcc build path rather than Bazel to work with TF 2.x, plus the release's compatibility patch. Oyin has it building reproducibly in a container now.

Budget fits the portfolio envelope; no headcount ask.

Deshawn

subject: Infinite Nature status: pipeline reproduced, long-horizon drift is the demo risk
body:
Lucia, Deshawn,

Status. The released pipeline reproduces end-to-end in our environment - renderer container included, thanks Oyin - and the interactive frontend runs the pretrained model at demo-acceptable frame rates.

The demo risk is long-horizon drift. Perpetual generation means errors compound: past roughly 60 generation steps on coastline inputs, scenes drift toward repetitive texture - plausible locally, but a spell-breaker if a demo visitor flies straight ahead for two minutes. Kaia measured quality-vs-step curves on 40 held-out images; degradation onset is consistent around step 55-70.

Two mitigations for the June freeze, not mutually exclusive: (1) demo choreography - guided flight paths that vary heading, which keeps perceived quality high essentially indefinitely; (2) Kaia's re-grounding trick, periodically re-anchoring generation, which pushes onset past step 120 in early tests but needs the retrained checkpoint to validate properly.

Recommendation: plan the demo around (1), treat (2) as an upside from the June retraining week. Decision by mid-May keeps Oyin's frontend work unblocked.

Umar

subject: Re: Infinite Nature status: decision - demo freeze scope for June 22
body:
All,

Decisions for the June 22 freeze, with the retraining week behind us:

1. The demo ships with guided flight paths as the primary experience - Oyin's three choreographed routes look genuinely great - plus a free-flight mode capped at 90 steps with a graceful 'return to path' transition. No uncapped free-flight in front of external visitors.
2. Kaia's re-grounding validated better than hoped on the retrained checkpoint (degradation onset past step 130 on the eval set), so it's enabled in free-flight mode. That's what makes the 90-step cap feel invisible.
3. The retrained-on-licensed-corpus checkpoint is the only model in the demo build. The pretrained release checkpoint stays for internal comparison only - that's a hard line for LRB.

LRB submission goes in tomorrow with the eval annex. Assuming sign-off at the next board, we're the June demo centerpiece. Genuinely proud of this one - thank you all.

Lucia

subject: InfiniteNature-Zero kickoff — perpetual view generation
body: Team, kicking off our productization of InfiniteNature-Zero, our open-source release on perpetual view generation of natural scenes from single images. The pitch for data-platforms: turn any still landscape into an unbounded flythrough for partner creative tools, with no paired video supervision needed. The method trains on single photos (LHQ) with a StyleGAN2 backbone and softmax splatting for point-cloud rendering, which is what makes the training story cheap enough to productize. Milestones I want to sanity-check with Santiago: (1) repro the pretrained LHQ checkpoint and input examples by May 15; (2) retrain on our licensed landscape corpus by end of June; (3) Shipyard-hosted demo for Launch Review Board mid-July. Gustavo owns repro, Csilla the retrain recipe, Saoirse the demo path. Flag risks early — the LRB calendar is biweekly and slots go fast. Thanks, Dmitri

subject: INZ compute plan — cirrus week + storage
body: Hi Ines, quick note on compute for InfiniteNature-Zero so nothing surprises us in Q3. Dev iterations (softmax-splatting renderer port, StyleGAN2 patch validation) stay on titan-a100 best-effort; we're averaging 24 GPUs there and that's fine. The big item is the retrain: we hold the cirrus-tpu reservation for the week of 2026-07-06 — 128 accelerators — and the full LHQ retrain is scheduled against it. Plan is about ten days of wall-clock packed into that week with checkpointing every 4 hours, so if the pod has any planned interrupts those days please flag now. Separately, can you confirm our storage quota can absorb the LHQ mirror plus checkpoints (~9 TB)? Dmitri is holding a mid-July Launch Review slot, so the retrain week is on the critical path. Thanks, Santiago

subject: Re: InfiniteNature-Zero kickoff — perpetual view generation
body: Status through June 9. Repro: done — the pretrained LHQ checkpoint runs end-to-end and our flythroughs match the project-page examples qualitatively; FID on our held-out LHQ split is 14.6 vs 14.2 reported. The pain point is the environment: the codebase pins Python 3.8 / CUDA 11.3, and the StyleGAN2 upgrade patch (stylegan2_upgrade.patch) doesn't apply cleanly against the newer rosinality revision, so Saoirse froze a known-good commit in our image. Softmax splatting also needed a rebuild for our driver stack. Risk for the retrain: our licensed corpus skews coastal; early finetunes drift toward water textures after ~200 steps of autoregressive generation. Csilla is testing a resampled mix. Nothing blocking the July plan yet. — Gustavo

subject: Re: InfiniteNature-Zero kickoff — perpetual view generation
body: Decision after yesterday's sync: we're cutting the custom-corpus retrain from Q2 scope. The coastal-drift work is promising but not demo-stable, and I'm not risking the LRB slot on it. Revised plan: ship the demo on the pretrained LHQ checkpoint with Saoirse's Shipyard deployment; keep Csilla's resampled-mix experiments running as background work and fold the retrain into Q3 planning. The July compute week stays as-is since we'll use it for ablations and longer flythrough stress tests (500+ steps) instead. Nadia has us on the 2026-07-16 Launch Review agenda; Santiago, please make sure the demo has a recorded fallback in case serving hiccups. Good work getting the repro solid — that's the part that had to land. Dmitri

subject: Kickoff: infinite-width uncertainty & calibration audit
body: Team — kicking off the infinite-width uncertainty project for the trust-theory portfolio, grounded in our open-source release on the uncertainty properties of neural networks' implicit priors in the infinite-width limit. We treat the function-space prior of an ensemble of infinitely-wide networks as a Gaussian process (the NNGP), put a softmax link on top for multi-class classification, and sample the posterior with parallelized elliptical slice sampling in JAX. What this unlocks: a calibration audit others can actually run — a direct comparison of NNGP calibration against finite-width analogues, which is exactly the evidence we keep getting asked for in model reviews. Milestones inside our window (Feb 16 – May 4): repro the ESS pipeline on the precomputed Myrtle-10 kernels by mid-March; calibration comparison report by late April; decision on productizing as an internal service at close. Deshawn will follow up on staffing. — Ximena

subject: Staffing & constraints — infinite-width uncertainty
body: Ximena — staffing and constraints for the plan above. Committed for the window: Halima 80% (ESS + JAX), Wanjiru 40% (infra for kernel loading), Bilal 30% (Colab packaging), Paloma 20% (plots and report). Carmen is wrapping another push through spring, but for the H2 extension — Gaussian process classification with ESS on the larger kernel grids — Carmen Reyes is committed at 60% to this project for July 2026; I've put that in the resourcing sheet already. Compute is modest: the sampling runs are embarrassingly parallel and titan-a100 best-effort covers it; no vulcan or cirrus ask.
