subject: Project Palisade kickoff: fact tracing for LM assertions
body:
Hi all,

Kicking off our fact-tracing effort. Internally we're calling this Project Palisade — please use the codename in subject lines and docs so search stays clean.

The basis is our open-source fact-tracing work: given a factual assertion an LM generates, identify which training examples taught it that — the "proponents". The release's benchmark compares gradient-based and embedding-based training-data-attribution methods, and notably both trail a BM25 baseline that never touches the model. Product framing: provenance for model assertions, which legal and enterprise customers keep asking for.

Milestones:
- Mar 6: benchmark reproduced end to end.
- Apr 10: TDA methods + BM25 baseline evaluated on a slice of our own pretraining corpus.
- May 8: readout with a go/no-go on productizing provenance.

Alina owns staffing; Linnea is tech lead.

Anders

subject: Re: Project Palisade kickoff: fact tracing for LM assertions
body:
Anders,

Palisade staffing and compute:

- Linnea Yamada 50% tech lead, owns the benchmark reproduction and methodology.
- Chiara Olsen 40% Feb-Apr on the corpus-slice indexing (BM25 side plus the embedding index).
- Amara Okafor 30% on gradient-computation infra — the gradient-based TDA methods need per-example gradients, which is the expensive part.

Compute: 24 A100s on titan-a100 best-effort for the gradient extraction runs in March; embedding and BM25 passes are cheap. No reservation-class ask this window.

One flag: per-example gradients on the corpus slice will dominate our budget — Amara estimates ~9k GPU-hours if we do the full slice naively. She's implementing the release's suggested last-layer approximation first, and we only go deeper if precision demands it.

Alina

subject: Re: Project Palisade — April status and a sobering number
body:
Hi Anders, Alina,

Palisade status:

- Benchmark reproduced on schedule (Mar 5). Our numbers confirm the paper's headline: both gradient-based and embedding-based TDA trail the BM25 baseline on proponent-retrieval precision.
- Our corpus slice: same ordering. BM25 hits precision@10 of 0.31, embedding-based 0.24, gradient-based 0.19 with the last-layer approximation. Amara checked whether going beyond last-layer closes the gap — gradient saturation appears to be the limiter, exactly as the release flagged, so deeper gradients buy little for 5x the cost.

The honest takeaway for the May readout: today, "provenance" is better served by lexical retrieval over the training corpus than by model-internals attribution. Thats a fine product — it's just not the sexy one. Chiara's index makes BM25-over-pretraining-corpus queryable in ~200ms, which could demo well.

Linnea

subject: Re: Project Palisade — readout decision
body:
Team,

Decision going into Friday's Palisade readout:

1. We recommend productizing the BM25-over-training-corpus provenance path — Chiara's 200ms index is the demo. Framed as "training-data provenance v1", with TDA methods positioned as the research roadmap, not vaporware.
2. Gradient-based TDA work stops at the last-layer approximation writeup. Amara's saturation analysis goes into the readout appendix; it's the clearest justification for not burning the 5x compute.
3. Follow-on proposal for next window: closing the precision gap (0.31 is a start, not a product) via hybrid lexical+embedding scoring. Linnea drafts one slide on it.

I know BM25-wins wasn't the outcome anyone dreamed of, but a true negative at this cost is a good quarter's work. See everyone Friday.

Anders

subject: Kickoff: memorization audit for our LMs
body:
Hi team,

Kicking off the memorization audit. Our open-source study established three log-linear relationships: verbatim memorization grows with (1) model capacity, (2) how many times an example is duplicated in training data, and (3) the number of tokens of context in the prompt. The release ships the prefixes and continuations used in the analysis (sourced from The Pile, uncurated).

What we're building: the same measurement, but on Meridian's own model family and pretraining corpus, packaged as a memorization audit that privacy review can require before any launch. Every LM launch currently answers "does it leak training data?" with a shrug.

Milestones: Mar 6 methodology reproduced on the released prompt set; Apr 24 duplication-counting pipeline over our corpus; mid-June full capacity sweep on our four model sizes; Jun 19 audit readout with Kofi's team.

Santiago owns staffing + the TPU ask. Nikhil is tech lead.

Priya

subject: Re: Kickoff: memorization audit for our LMs
body:
Priya,

Staffing and compute:

- Nikhil Abebe 50% tech lead; Vera Egede 40% on the duplication-counting pipeline (suffix-array based, corpus-scale); Oyin Iversen 40% on generation infra; Bilal Novak 30% on analysis tooling.
- Compute: methodology reproduction fits titan-a100 best-effort. For the capacity-sweep generation runs we hold the cirrus-tpu reservation for the week of 2026-06-08 — 256 accelerators — which is enough to prompt all four model sizes across the full duplication grid in one week. That's confirmed against the language portfolio's quarterly Cirrus allocation.

Dependency: Vera's duplication counts must be final before the sweep, since the prompt sampling is stratified by duplication count. Her Apr 24 date has ~6 weeks of slack to the reservation, which I'm comfortable with.

Santiago

subject: Re: Kickoff: memorization audit for our LMs — status + privacy process
body:
Hi Priya, Santiago,

Status:

- Methodology reproduced in early March on the released prompt set; our extraction curves show the same log-linear shape in context length (memorization roughly doubles going from 50 to 200 prompt tokens on the largest public model we tested).
- Vera's duplication pipeline finished Apr 27 — slightly late, but the counts are validated. Notable: 0.9% of our corpus appears 10+ times, and those examples are exactly where early spot-checks show verbatim continuations.

Process risk: Kofi (cc'd) points out the audit outputs will themselves contain memorized training text, so the readout artifacts need privacy review, and that SLA is 2-3 weeks. Counting back from the Jun 19 readout, the sweep outputs must be locked and submitted by May 29 — before the June reservation week produces the final numbers. Proposal: submit the report template + March sample outputs for review now, then the June numbers drop into an approved format. Kofi's tentatively ok with this, confirming this week.

Nikhil

subject: Re: Kickoff: memorization audit for our LMs — readout decisions
body:
Team,

Ahead of Friday's readout, decisions and the headline:

- The June sweep completed on the reserved week. Our models show the same three log-linear relationships as the public study — capacity, duplication, context length — and our largest model emits verbatim continuations for 38% of examples duplicated 10+ times at 200-token prompts. That number alone justifies the audit.
- Decision 1: the audit becomes a standing pre-launch requirement; Bilal's tooling gets a runbook and an owner in the platform org next quarter. Kofi's approved-template path worked, so the privacy SLA is no longer on the critical path for future runs.
- Decision 2: dedup mitigation (dropping 10+ duplicated examples from future pretraining) goes into Q3 planning as a corpus-team ask, with our duplication counts as the evidence base.

Thanks all — Friday is mostly a victory lap.

Priya

subject: Kickoff: LocoProp training-efficiency evaluation
body:
Hi all,

Kicking off the LocoProp evaluation for trust-theory. The pitch: second-order optimizers give state-of-the-art training quality but their memory footprint and compute cost keep them off our budget-constrained runs. Our LocoProp release (AISTATS'22) constructs layerwise local losses — per-neuron targets set in the backward pass, then independent parallel updates per layer — and gets close to second-order performance using only first-order optimizers.

If that holds on our workloads, it's a direct GPU-hours reduction across the portfolio's recurring training jobs.

Milestones:
- May 8: benchmark reproduction (squared loss + layerwise Bregman divergence variants).
- Jun 12: head-to-head on two internal trust-model training jobs — wall-clock, memory, final eval quality.
- Jul 10: adopt/pass recommendation.

Bruno owns staffing. Giannis is tech lead.

Ximena

subject: Re: Kickoff: LocoProp training-efficiency evaluation
body:
Ximena,

Resourcing:

- Giannis Sato 50% tech lead on the optimizer benchmarks; Emeka Pinto 30% on the training-job integration for the June head-to-head.
- Compute: 16 A100s on titan-a100 best-effort. The whole point is cheap training, so no reservation ask.

Scope addition, agreed with you Wednesday, formalizing here: quality deltas between optimizers on trust models are subtle enough that automated metrics won't settle an adopt/pass call on their own. There's no shared tool for structured human ratings, so we're scoping and building a human-rating annotation UI from scratch — Saoirse owns it at 50% with Giannis contributing the backend — to collect side-by-side preference ratings on models trained with the candidate optimizers. Rating queues, blind A/B presentation, agreement stats. Estimate is 6 engineer-weeks, reusable for the portfolio afterward.

Total ask: 1.3 FTE through mid-July.

Bruno

subject: Re: Kickoff: LocoProp training-efficiency evaluation — status
body:
Hi Ximena, Bruno,

Status:

- Reproduction landed May 7. Both the squared-loss variant and the layerwise Bregman-divergence variants behave as published: on the benchmark models LocoProp closes most of the gap to the second-order baseline at essentially first-order memory. The parallel per-layer local updates are the key win — we get several local iterations per batch without blowing up step time.
- Head-to-head: job 1 (the abuse-classifier retrain) is done — 22% wall-clock reduction vs our current second-order setup at equal final AUC, and peak memory down 41%, which lets the job fit on half the GPUs. Job 2 (the trust-ranker) starts next week after Emeka finishes integration.

Risk: job 2 uses non-standard activations, and choosing the matching transfer function for the Bregman divergence isn't obvious — wrong choice degrades convergence. I've got two candidates; may cost us a week of sweeps. Saoirse's rating UI enters pilot Friday with 4 raters.

Giannis

subject: Re: Kickoff: LocoProp training-efficiency evaluation — recommendation
body:
Team,

Decision for Friday's review — recommendation is adopt, scoped:

1. LocoProp becomes the default optimizer for the abuse-classifier retrain family now. The 22% wall-clock and 41% memory numbers held across three reruns, and the halved GPU footprint compounds monthly on a recurring job.
2. The trust-ranker stays on the current optimizer for one more quarter. Giannis's transfer-function sweeps got convergence to parity but not better, and the human-rating data (nice work Saoirse — 4 raters, 0.71 agreement) shows no perceptible quality difference to justify the migration risk yet.
3. The rating UI graduates to a portfolio tool; Saoirse writes the handover doc by Jul 10.

I'll draft the review packet; Bruno, numbers check by Thursday please.

Ximena

subject: Kickoff: LogicInference as a platform reasoning benchmark
body:
Hi all,

Kicking off the LogicInference operationalization. Our open-source release generates a dataset for evaluating logical inference — propositional logic plus a small subset of first-order logic, rendered both in semi-formal notation and in natural language. Its two long-term goals map exactly onto what model teams keep asking the platform for: (1) measure whether inference chains are real or hallucinated, and (2) test whether abstract inference skill transfers to real tasks.

Plan: make generation reproducible on the platform (it's a config-and-run of generate_dataset.py today, with a hand-edited TARGET_FOLDER — we can do better), version the outputs in Corpus, and stand up baseline fine-tunes so teams get a reference number.

Milestones: Mar 6 reproducible generation pipeline; Apr 17 v1 dataset versioned + Evalline task registered; June baseline fine-tuning grid; Jun 19 readout.

Deshawn owns staffing/compute. Yara is research lead.

Dmitri

subject: Re: Kickoff: LogicInference as a platform reasoning benchmark
body:
Dmitri,

Staffing and compute:

- Yara Jokic 40% research lead; Gustavo Moreau 50% on the generation pipeline and Corpus versioning; Paloma Castillo 30% Evalline task registration; Quentin Farkas 20% baseline configs.
- Compute in two phases. Generation is CPU-only — the README warns generation takes a while, so Gustavo will parallelize across the batch pool rather than one big machine. For the fine-tuning grid we hold the vulcan-h100 reservation for the week of 2026-06-08 — 256 GPUs — confirmed for our exclusive use that week. Grid is 4 model sizes x 3 data mixes x 2 seeds; my sizing says the week covers it with ~15% slack.

Note: Vulcan's maintenance window is Jun 22-24, safely after our week. But it means no spillover runs that week, so the grid config freezes Jun 1.

Deshawn

subject: Re: Kickoff: LogicInference as a platform reasoning benchmark — status
body:
Hi Dmitri, Deshawn,

Status:

- Generation pipeline landed Mar 4. TARGET_FOLDER is now a proper flag with a config file, runs are seeded and content-addressed, and full generation parallelized across the batch pool takes 6.5 hours vs ~2 days single-machine.
- v1 dataset is versioned in Corpus and the Evalline task registered Apr 15. Paloma's task exposes both renderings — semi-formal logical notation and natural language — as separate splits, which model teams have already started using.

Risk/trade-off for the June grid: Yara's early baselines show accuracy on the natural-language rendering trails the semi-formal one by ~9pp on the same inference patterns, and hallucinated inference chains concentrate in the first-order subset. She wants one grid axis swapped from a third data mix to an FOL-heavy mix to chase that. Cost-neutral, but it changes the frozen config, so flagging before the Jun 1 freeze rather than after.

Gustavo

subject: Re: Kickoff: LogicInference as a platform reasoning benchmark — grid results + decisions
body:
Team,

Grid week wrapped on schedule. Decisions for Friday's readout:

1. Yara's FOL-heavy mix was the right swap — it cut hallucinated inference chains on the first-order subset by roughly a third at equal propositional accuracy, and that's the headline result. The 9pp semi-formal vs natural-language gap persists across model sizes; goes in the readout as the standing research question.
2. The v1 dataset + Evalline task graduate to supported platform assets. Gustavo writes the runbook; Paloma owns the task through Q3.
3. Follow-on ask for Q3 planning: a v2 generation pass with harder FOL templates. Quentin drafts the proposal — one pager by Thursday please.

Good quarter — from research repo to platform asset with numbers teams actually cite.

Dmitri

subject: Kickoff: logit adjustment for long-tail classifiers
body:
Hi all,

Kicking off the long-tail workstream. Nearly every classifier customers train on the platform has a skewed label distribution, and rare-class accuracy is the number-one complaint in the last two feedback rounds. Our logit-adjustment release (ICLR'21) is about the cheapest possible fix — adjust the logits for label frequency, either at training or post-hoc — with strong published gains.

Plan:
- Mar 20: reproduce the release results on the CIFAR-10/100 long-tail datasets (EXP-100 profile .tfrecords, baseline vs adjusted).
- Apr 24: the adjustment available as a flag in the platform trainer.
- May 29: pilot with one partner team on their real long-tail workload, then a rollout decision.

Jelena owns staffing. Carmen leads the reproduction; Farah leads the trainer integration.

Dmitri

subject: Re: Kickoff: logit adjustment for long-tail classifiers
body:
Dmitri,

Staffing through the window:

- Carmen Reyes 40% on the reproduction and the eval methodology (per-class accuracy breakdowns, not just top-1).
- Linnea Yamada 20% supporting Evalline integration of the long-tail metrics.
- Farah Haddad 30% in March-April on the trainer flag, then Farah Haddad is committed at 60% to this project for May 2026 to drive the trainer integration and the partner-team pilot — I've locked that with her directly. The pilot month is where integration bugs surface, so I want her depth there.

Compute: tiny. The CIFAR runs are single-GPU; the pilot uses the partner's existing quota. 4 A100s on titan-a100 covers everything on our side.

Only dependency: the partner team confirms their May pilot dataset by Apr 17.

Jelena

subject: Re: Kickoff: logit adjustment for long-tail classifiers — status
body:
Hi Dmitri, Jelena,

Status:

- Reproduction done Mar 18. On cifar10-lt (EXP-100 profile) the adjusted model beats the baseline by 4.1pp overall, and the win concentrates where it should: tail-class accuracy improves by double digits while head classes hold. cifar100-lt shows the same pattern. We sanity-checked with the release's dummy-dataset test mode before every real run, which caught one bad data path early.
- Farah's trainer flag merged Apr 10, ahead of schedule. Post-hoc adjustment mode included, so teams can fix already-trained models without retraining.

Risk for the pilot: the partner's label distribution is more extreme than EXP-100 (their tail classes have <20 examples), and the adjustment's gains shrink when frequency estimates get that noisy. I'm preparing a smoothed-frequency variant as a fallback. Partner dataset confirmation slipped a week to Apr 24 — Farah's May depth just got more important.

Carmen

subject: Re: Kickoff: logit adjustment for long-tail classifiers — rollout decision
body:
Team,

Pilot wrapped Friday; decision time.

- Result: on the partner's workload the adjusted trainer improved tail-class accuracy 7.8pp with a 0.4pp overall dip — inside their tolerance. Carmen's smoothed-frequency variant was needed for the <20-example classes exactly as she predicted; without it the raw estimates were too noisy.
- Decision: rollout approved. The flag goes to generally-available in the platform trainer this month, default-off, with the smoothed variant as the documented recommendation for extreme tails. Linnea's Evalline long-tail metrics ship alongside so teams can see per-class effects instead of a single top-1 number.
- Farah — the May push made the pilot; the integration issue list (11 filed, 11 closed) tells the story. Please write the two-page rollout note by Jun 5 and we'll close this one out.

Dmitri

subject: Kickoff: loss-function guidance for transferable embeddings
body:
Hi all,

Kicking off the loss-functions-transfer study. Background: our open-source release showed that loss functions which improve a model's own accuracy often make its features *less* transferable, with checkpoints and SavedModels published for every loss variant. That tension is exactly the trap our embedding teams keep walking into — they tune the training loss for the source task and then wonder why downstream retrieval transfer degrades.

Goal: turn the released models + loss implementations into concrete guidance ("use loss X when the embedding must transfer, loss Y when it's single-task") validated on our own transfer suite.

Milestones: Apr 24 released SavedModels loaded and penultimate-layer features extracted; May 29 transfer evals across our internal task suite; Jun 26 guidance doc + readout.

Alina owns staffing. Yusuf is research lead.

Anders

subject: Re: Kickoff: loss-function guidance for transferable embeddings
body:
Anders,

Resourcing:

- Yusuf Keita 40% research lead; Ondrej Bergstrom 40% on the transfer-eval methodology; Rosa Mensah 40% on the SavedModel loading path and eval infra.
- Compute: light. Feature extraction from the released checkpoints plus linear transfer evals fits on 8 A100s, titan-a100 best-effort. No reservations.

Data logistics: the internal transfer suite datasets need to live in Corpus so the evals are reproducible by other teams. The Corpus v2 migration freeze is 2026-07-24, so landing our transfer-eval datasets in Corpus during the first half of July is safe — I've put the ingestion milestone at Jul 17 with a week of buffer. Rosa owns those tickets.

One technical heads-up from Rosa's first pass: the released models output 1001 classes (the extra background class), and it has to be dropped at eval or the numbers skew. She's baking that into the loader so nobody trips on it.

Alina

subject: Re: Kickoff: loss-function guidance for transferable embeddings — status
body:
Hi Anders, Alina,

Status:

- Loading path done Apr 21. We went the TF2 route — running the released SavedModels directly rather than the TF1-compat checkpoint loader — which gives us every block's activations plus final_avg_pool in one forward pass. Background-class drop is handled in the loader as planned.
- Transfer evals: 9 of 12 internal tasks done. The paper's pattern replicates clearly so far — the loss variants with the best source accuracy sit at the bottom of our transfer ranking on 7 of 9 tasks, with penultimate-layer (final_avg_pool) features telling the same story as the block-level probes.

Risk: the 3 remaining tasks are the graph-structured ones, and linear probes may understate transfer there — Ondrej wants to add a small non-linear probe as a check, which adds ~1 week. We can still hold May 29 if we accept linear-only on those three; otherwise Jun 5. Preference?

Rosa

subject: Re: Kickoff: loss-function guidance for transferable embeddings — readout decisions
body:
Team,

Ahead of Friday's readout (and with Q3 OKRs locking the same day), decisions:

1. We took the Jun 5 slip for Ondrej's non-linear probes — right call. On the graph-structured tasks the non-linear probe reversed one of the three rankings, which would have made our guidance wrong exactly where the portfolio cares most.
2. The guidance doc ships Friday: softmax cross-entropy variants for single-task embedding models; the transfer-friendly losses from the release when embeddings feed multiple downstream tasks; and a mandatory transfer-eval before any embedding model is declared portfolio-shared. Yusuf has the final ranking tables.
3. Rosa's loader (TF2 SavedModel path, background-class drop included) becomes a shared utility.

July ingestion milestone stands as scheduled. Nice work — this is the rare study that ends with a one-page answer.

Anders

subject: M-layer kickoff — matrix exponentiation as a drop-in layer
body:
Team,

Kicking off the M-layer effort formally. The pitch: our open-source "Intelligent Matrix Exponentiation" work gives us a single Keras layer (MLayer) that can learn periodic and multiplicative structure that stacked ReLUs handle badly. The product angle is a robustness-friendly building block we can offer inside our modeling toolkit.

Milestones I want to hold for the window ending 2026-06-22:
1) By 04-10: MLayer API hardened, unit tests, import path stable.
2) By 05-15: reproduce the CIFAR10 robustness results from M_layer_Robustness.ipynb against our internal harness (Evalline).
3) By 06-12: periodicity extrapolation demo for the launch review pre-read.

Daniela owns staffing; Umar and Fumiko own the robustness study; Farah and Oyin own the API and Evalline integration. Flag risks early — I'd rather cut scope in April than in June.

Thanks,
Anders

subject: Re: M-layer kickoff — matrix exponentiation as a drop-in layer
body:
Anders,

Staffing and compute picture for the plan you laid out.

Staffing: Farah and Oyin at 50% each through April for the API + Evalline work. Umar at 40% for the robustness study. Fumiko Rossi is committed at 60%+ to this project for June 2026 — she'll drive the adversarial sweep and the periodicity demo through the final push to 06-22. I've written that into our June allocation sheet.

Compute: this is CPU/A100-light work; 32 GPUs on titan-a100 best-effort covers the CIFAR10 robustness reruns. No vulcan-h100 reservation needed, which keeps us out of Ines's queue.

One dependency: Evalline harness onboarding — Tomas's team says 2 weeks lead time, so Farah files the intake this week.

Daniela

subject: Re: M-layer kickoff — status + robustness caveat
body:
Status ahead of Friday's sync.

Done: MLayer import path is stable (from m_layer import MLayer works against our internal package), and the trained cifar10_model.npy checkpoint reproduces in Evalline within 0.3% of the notebook's clean accuracy.

Risk: the robustness picture is more nuanced than the pitch deck. Under our PGD sweep the M-layer model degrades more gracefully than the ReLU baseline at low epsilon, but the gap inverts at higher perturbation budgets. If we sell "robust building block" we need to scope the claim to small-epsilon regimes, or the launch review will (rightly) push back.

Periodicity demo is on track — Fumiko has the extrapolation experiment running and it's genuinely striking vs an LSTM baseline.

Proposal: I write a one-pager on the epsilon caveat for the pre-read. ok?

Umar

subject: Re: M-layer kickoff — decision: scope the robustness claim
body:
All,

Decision from yesterday's review with Nadia: we ship the M-layer toolkit component with the robustness claim scoped to the small-epsilon regime, exactly per Umar's one-pager. The periodicity extrapolation demo becomes the headline instead — it demos better anyway and the matrix-exponentiation story is easy to tell.

Cut: the higher-epsilon adversarial hardening workstream moves out of this window entirely. We are not chasing it before 06-22.

Fumiko, you're the DRI for the demo through launch review on 06-19 — I know June is your heavy month on this, so shout if anything else lands on your plate. Daniela, please confirm the June allocation sheet still reflects the plan.

Adding this to the Q3 OKR draft before the 06-26 lock.

Anders

subject: M-Theory numerics — kickoff and framing
body:
Hi all,

Kicking off the M-Theory numerics project. Framing for anyone new: this is our pure-mathematics track — there is no dependency on measurement or user data at all, we're using our ML stack as a generic numerical engine to hunt for structure in supergravity potentials. The product story is credibility + tooling: the same vectorized optimization machinery generalizes to other stiff numerical searches in the portfolio.

Milestones (window closes 2026-07-06):
- 04-24: SUGRA_Colab loader flow working against our internal mirror, including the m_theory.zip upload path for modified modules.
- 05-29: reproduce the known critical-point catalogue on small scans.
- 06-26: large-scale scan results written up for the Q3 OKR lock that same day.

Bruno has staffing; Yara is tech lead. Compute ask coming separately from Bruno — the big scans are accelerator-hungry.

Anders

subject: Re: M-Theory numerics — compute + staffing
body:
Anders,

Resourcing rundown.

Staffing: Yara at 50% as TL, Giannis and Maren at 40% each on the scan infrastructure, Farah at 20% for the colab loader/mirror plumbing. That holds through June.

Compute: the small scans run fine on titan-a100 best-effort. For the large-scale critical-point scan we hold the cirrus-tpu reservation — 256 accelerators for the week of 2026-06-22, confirmed in the quarterly allocation for graphs-retrieval. That lands the scan results right before the 06-26 OKR lock, which is tight but workable if the scan code is stable by mid-June.

One wrinkle: vulcan is down for maintenance 06-22 to 06-24, so everyone will be piling onto the other pools that week. Being on cirrus keeps us insulated.

Bruno

subject: Re: M-Theory numerics — status: small scans done, precision risk
body:
Status:

- Loader flow shipped 04-22. The SUGRA_Colab notebook now loads the m_theory module from our internal mirror or from an uploaded m_theory.zip archive with the reset_package path working — Farah's demo went smoothly.
- Small scans reproduce the known critical-point catalogue: 41/41 previously published stationary points recovered, residuals below 1e-9.

Risk for the big scan: float32 on the accelerators loses us stationary points with shallow basins — on the small runs we miss ~8% of points unless we do a float64 polish pass on CPU afterwards. That polish adds roughly 1.5 days of wall-clock to the June scan. I've budgeted it into the schedule, but it means the 256-chip week has zero slack. If the scan slips past 06-26 we report partial results at the OKR lock.

Yara

subject: Re: M-Theory numerics — decision on the June scan
body:
Bruno, Yara,

Decision after this morning's check-in: we run the large scan as planned on our cirrus-tpu week starting 06-22, but we cut the scan volume 20% so the float64 polish pass fits inside the reservation with half a day of slack. Better a complete, polished catalogue of a slightly smaller region than a partial sweep of the full one.

For the 06-26 OKR lock I'll write the key result as "extended critical-point catalogue, polished residuals < 1e-9" without committing to a point count. Yara, please send me the two headline numbers you're confident in by 06-24 evening — that gives me a day of buffer.

Farah's loader work is done and she rolls off this week as planned.

Thanks all — strong quarter for the weirdest project in my portfolio.

Anders

subject: Project Saffron kickoff — MADLAD-400 serving plan
body:
Hi team,

Welcome to Project Saffron — that's the internal codename for the MADLAD-400 productization, so please use it in docs and standups. Goal: take our open-source MADLAD-400 release and stand up a long-tail translation service.

What we're working with: MT checkpoints at 3B, 7.2B (plus a backtranslation-finetuned 7b-mt-bt variant) and 10.7B parameters, an 8B parameter LM, and the shared 256k vocabulary they were all trained with.

Milestones inside our window (through 07-20):
- 04-24: 3b-mt serving on Shipyard staging, inference_example parity confirmed.
- 05-29: quality bake-off 3B vs 7.2B vs 10.7B on our long-tail eval slice.
- 07-06: Launch Review Board pre-read; external demo pending sign-off.

Bruno will follow up on compute + staffing. Carmen is research lead.

Priya

subject: Re: Project Saffron kickoff — resourcing
body:
Priya,

Saffron resourcing:

Staffing — Carmen 50% (research lead, bake-off design), Yara 30% (eval slices), Milan 50% and Paloma 40% on Shipyard serving + quantization. That mix holds through the LRB pre-read.

Compute — bake-off inference for the 10.7B MT model needs 64 A100s on titan best-effort for roughly two weeks in May; no reservation required. If we later fine-tune the 7b-mt-bt variant on internal parallel data, that becomes a vulcan-h100 ask and I'll go through Ines with at least three weeks notice.

Serving — Zeke's team confirmed Shipyard staging capacity for one model at a time; the bake-off runs offline, so that's fine.

One flag: the 256k vocab makes naive int8 quantization of the embedding table painful; Milan is scoping it this sprint before we commit to latency numbers.

Bruno

subject: Re: Project Saffron — bake-off results + a trade-off
body:
Bake-off numbers are in for Saffron.

On our long-tail slice (90 languages), 10.7b-mt beats 7b-mt by +1.8 chrF on average, but 7b-mt-bt — the backtranslation-finetuned checkpoint — closes to within 0.4 chrF of the 10.7B on the lowest-resource third while being materially cheaper to serve. The 3b-mt is fine as a fallback tier only.

Trade-off for the launch review: serve 7b-mt-bt as primary and accept the 0.4 chrF gap, or serve 10.7b-mt and eat roughly 40% higher serving cost at the latency target Milan measured post-quantization. My recommendation is 7b-mt-bt primary, 10.7B behind a quality-critical flag.

One risk: a handful of low-resource languages show audit artifacts inherited from the web crawl; Yara is compiling the exclusion list so we don't demo those at LRB.

Carmen

subject: Re: Project Saffron — LRB decision
body:
Team,

Decision for the 07-06 Launch Review Board pre-read, agreed with Nadia today:

1) Project Saffron ships with 7b-mt-bt as the primary serving model; 10.7b-mt goes behind the quality-critical flag exactly per Carmen's recommendation.
2) The 17 languages on Yara's audit-artifact exclusion list are out of the external demo and documented as a known limitation. Privacy review already signed off on the remaining set.
3) Scope cut: the 8B LM does not ship in this window. It stays research-only until we have a separate eval story — I've moved it to the Q3 backlog.

Milan, please have the staging endpoint frozen by 07-03 so LRB sees exactly what would ship.

Nice work everyone — Saffron is in good shape going into review.

Priya

subject: Marot kickoff — one eval console for human + automated MT quality
body:
Hi both,

Kicking off the Marot workstream. The goal: make our open-source Marot app the standard console every language team uses to analyze MQM human-eval data, side by side with automated metrics like BLEURT. Today teams pass around spreadsheets; the app already computes per-segment MQM scores by averaging rater scores with severity/category weights, so the win is integration, not invention.

Milestones (window through 07-20):
- 04-17: internal hosted deployment (no more downloading marot.html by hand), self-serve file upload preserved.
- 05-22: Evalline integration so BLEURT columns land automatically next to MQM.
- 07-13: adoption target — 3 language teams using it for their weekly QA reviews.

Deshawn owns staffing and the hosting plan; Freya is tech lead. Resource asks to me by end of next week please.

Lucia

subject: Re: Marot kickoff — staffing + compute asks
body:
Lucia,

Resourcing as requested.

Staffing: Freya 50% (TL), Ondrej 40% on the score-computation and sigtests code paths, Yara 30% on the Evalline/BLEURT bridge. Hosting lands on Shipyard, Zeke's team has the intake.

Compute: the app itself is client-side, but the BLEURT backfill is not — rescoring the historical MQM archive (about 2.1M segments across 14 language pairs) needs real accelerator time. We hold the vulcan-h100 reservation — 128 accelerators for the week of 2026-07-06 — to run the full backfill in one pass before the adoption push. I've confirmed the slot in the reservation sheet.

Smaller ongoing scoring fits titan-a100 best-effort.

One heads-up: rater data ingestion needs a privacy review (2-3 week SLA), filing this week so it clears well before July.

Deshawn

subject: Re: Marot kickoff — status + data-format risk
body:
Status:

- Hosted deployment shipped 04-15 (we went with the marot-lite.html approach serving JS/CSS from our own static host rather than asking users to download six files).
- Evalline bridge is in review; BLEURT columns render next to MQM scores on the pilot language pair.

Risk: the ingestion format. Marot expects tab-separated UTF-8 with ten fixed columns, one line per marked error — and two of the three pilot teams export from tooling that emits per-segment rows instead. Ondrej wrote a converter, but severity/category mappings are lossy for one team's legacy taxonomy, which shifts their MQM scores by up to 0.7 points per segment on spot checks. If we silently convert, the numbers won't match their old spreadsheets and we lose trust on day one.

Proposal: publish the mapping table in the app's Settings menu and flag converted rows visibly. Yara agrees. ok to proceed?

Freya

subject: Re: Marot kickoff — decisions going into the July backfill
body:
All,

Decisions from today's review:

1) Converter: approved as Freya proposed — visible flags on converted rows, mapping table published in Settings. We do NOT silently rewrite anyone's severity weights.
2) The legacy-taxonomy team moves to the second adoption wave; we hit the 07-13 target with the two clean-format teams plus the speech-audio raters who volunteered.
3) Backfill: locked to our vulcan-h100 week of 2026-07-06 with all 128 accelerators — Deshawn confirmed the reservation again on Friday, so the full 2.1M-segment BLEURT rescore lands before the adoption push. No schedule changes.

Privacy review cleared on 06-18, so nothing is blocking.

Thanks — this one is quietly becoming the most-used thing in the portfolio.

Lucia

subject: Project Sirocco kickoff — MathWriting as a first-class benchmark
body:
Team,

Starting Project Sirocco — our internal codename for the MathWriting effort, please tag docs and dashboards with it.

Goal: make the MathWriting dataset (digital inks of handwritten mathematical expressions from the prompted collection) a first-class benchmark in our platform, with loader code, a reference recognizer, and a leaderboard slice in Evalline.

Milestones inside the 04-06 to 06-29 window:
- 04-24: ingestion of the full 2.9 GB mathwriting-2024 archive plus the excerpt archive for CI smoke tests.

Alina owns staffing; Efe is tech lead. One open legal question on the data license — I'll raise it with Kofi separately.

subject: Re: Project Sirocco kickoff — staffing + compute
body:
Dmitri,

Sirocco resourcing:

Staffing — Efe 50% as TL, Halima 40% on the ink-parsing/loader code, Tereza 50% on the reference recognizer, Yara 25% on the Evalline metric integration. Stable through end of June.

subject: Re: Project Sirocco — status + license risk
body:

subject: Mechanic kickoff — kill manual LR tuning
body:
Team,

Kicking off the Mechanic rollout. The pitch is simple: our open-source Mechanic tuner learns the learning-rate scale factor of any base optimizer automatically — in the paper's evaluations across large-scale deep learning tasks it comes close to, matches, or beats manual tuning. Internally, teams burn real GPU-weeks on LR sweeps. The integration is genuinely two lines: keep your schedule at base LR 1.0 and wrap the optimizer with mechanic.mechanize(adamw).

Milestones (window closes 2026-05-04):
- 02-27: exact jax/optax implementation vendored into the training stack behind a flag.
- 03-27: A/B across 3 internal workloads with different batch sizes and schedules.

subject: Re: Mechanic kickoff — A/B results, one workload is stubborn
body:
A/B status across the three workloads:

- Retrieval encoder (batch 4096, cosine schedule): mechanized adamw matches the hand-tuned baseline within 0.1% eval loss, zero sweep cost. Clear win.
- Ranking model (batch 512, linear warmup): Mechanic beats the production LR by 0.8% — turns out prod was under-tuned for a year. Slightly awkward, very persuasive.
- Small-batch fine-tune (batch 64): the scale factor oscillates early and we land 1.2% worse unless we extend warmup. Quentin traced it to the schedule interaction — remember Mechanic tunes the scale, so a base_learning_rate left at 1e-4 instead of 1.0 silently double-scales; one team hit exactly that misconfiguration in dogfood.

Risk: rollout doc must make the "set base LR to 1.0" contract impossible to miss, ideally with a startup assertion. Wanjiru is adding one.

Recommendation stays: default-on for large-batch, opt-in for batch < 128.

Rafael

Great half, team.

subject: Memento kickoff — interference diagnostics for our RL stack
body:
Hi all,

Kicking off Memento. Background: our open-source catastrophic-interference work showed that training a second "Memento" agent from the position where the original agent's checkpoint plateaus reliably pushes past the plateau — evidence the wall is interference, not exploration. Two internal agents teams are hitting suspiciously similar plateaus, and I want this as a standard diagnostic.

Plan for the window (through 06-29):
- 04-17: reproduce the baseline — train the original Rainbow agent (rainbow.gin config) and the Memento agent from its checkpoint on 3 Atari games; confirm the published effect. dqn.gin variant as a stretch.
- 05-22: package the two-stage train_original_agent / train_memento_agent flow as a diagnostic recipe.
- 06-19: run the diagnostic on one internal team's plateaued agent and report.

Alina owns staffing/compute; Carmen is TL. Heads-up that the baseline training is multi-day per game, so compute planning matters here.

Ulla

subject: Re: Memento kickoff — compute plan

Compute: the April baseline reproduction fits titan-a100 best-effort — Rainbow on 3 games plus Memento agents is about 20 GPUs for three weeks given the several-days-per-game training cost. The June diagnostic on the internal team's agent is the heavy piece: their agent is much larger than an Atari Rainbow, so for that we hold the vulcan-h100 reservation — 256 accelerators for the week of 2026-06-15 — enough to run original + Memento retrains side by side and land the report by 06-19.

subject: Re: Memento kickoff — status: effect reproduced, one caveat
body:

Effect reproduces clearly on two of three: +31% and +18% score past the plateau. Breakout shows a much smaller +4%, consistent with the paper's framing that the gains concentrate where interference (not exploration) is the binding constraint.
- Rosa's recipe packaging is ahead of schedule; the dqn.gin stretch variant also runs.

Caveat for the June diagnostic: the internal team's agent uses a recurrent core, and the checkpoint-handoff assumes a feedforward value net. Efe has a workaround (freeze + re-init the recurrent state pathway) but it adds ~2 days of engineering and slightly muddies attribution. We still fit the June compute week, but the report should carry the caveat explicitly.

subject: Menger-RL kickoff — one distributed RL stack to rule them all
body:
Team,

Kicking off Menger-RL. The case: our open-source Menger work was the first distributed RL framework of its kind — scaling to a few thousand workers for data collection and inference on CPU, with pod-level accelerator training for the learner — and it was proven on real macro-placement workloads. Meanwhile our internal agents teams each maintain bespoke actor/learner plumbing. We consolidate on Menger.

Milestones (window through 07-20):
- 05-01: Menger actor fleet running on our CPU batch pool at 1,000 workers, toy environment.
- 06-05: learner integrated with our training stack; replay throughput benchmarked.
- 06-26: full-scale soak on a placement-style workload — the demo result I want for Q3 OKR planning.
- 07-17: adoption guide + first team migrated.

Bao owns staffing/compute; Leilani is TL. This one has real infra teeth — flag capacity issues early.

subject: Re: Menger-RL kickoff — capacity plan
body:

Capacity plan for the milestones:

Accelerators — the learner soak is the big ask. We hold the vulcan-h100 reservation with 512 accelerators for the week of 2026-06-22. subject: Re: Menger-RL kickoff — status: replay throughput is the bottleneck
body:
Status before the soak:

- Actor fleet: 1,000 workers stable since 04-28; we've burst-tested to 2,400. Milan's autoscaler recovers from batch-pool preemptions cleanly.
- Learner bridge: Vera has the learner training on our stack; end-to-end on the toy env converges to reference in 6.5h.

Bottleneck: replay ingest. At 3,000 simulated actors, the learner-side replay buffer saturates at ~78% of the sample throughput we need to keep 512 chips fed — the actors produce fast enough on CPU (as the framework promised), but our storage-layer hop adds latency the original in-memory design didn't have. Vera's fix is sharding the replay across 8 ingest nodes; prototype shows 1.35x, which clears the bar with margin.

Risk: the sharded ingest lands ~06-15, two days before soak-readiness. If it slips, options are (a) soak at 384 chips, or (b) accept learner idle time. Will flag by 06-12.

subject: Re: Menger-RL kickoff — soak decision
body:

Go get it.

subject: MentorMix kickoff — noise-robust training for Corpus users
body:
Team,

Kicking off the MentorMix integration. Why it matters: methods that look great on synthetic label noise often fall over on real-world noise; our MentorMix work — combining MentorNet-style curriculum weighting with Mixup, in the four-step weight/sample/mixup loop — holds up on both, and we also have the first controlled benchmark of real-world web label noise to prove it. Corpus ingestion produces exactly this kind of noisy data, so a blessed noise-robust trainer is a natural platform feature.

Milestones (window through 06-15):
- 04-03: MentorMix reference implementation reproducing published numbers on the controlled-noise benchmark.
- 05-08: trainer integrated behind a Corpus platform API with noise-level presets.
- 06-05: pilot with one internal team on genuinely noisy ingested data.

Bruno owns staffing; Ondrej is TL. Note we should sequence carefully around the Corpus v2 migration — Bruno, please align with Jun's team on timing.

Dmitri

subject: Re: MentorMix kickoff — staffing + Corpus v2 alignment
body:
Dmitri,

Resourcing:

Staffing — Ondrej 50% (TL), Quentin 50% on benchmark reproduction, Wanjiru 40% on the platform API, Oyin 40% on the pilot-team integration. Stable through 06-15.

Compute — reproduction sweeps need 32 A100s on titan best-effort through April; the pilot training runs are smaller. No vulcan ask.

Corpus v2 alignment, per Jun: the team plans around a Corpus v2 freeze date of 2026-07-10, which is comfortably after our window closes on 06-15 — so all our pilot ingestion runs on v1 paths, and Wanjiru writes the API against the v1 interface with a documented v2 shim to hand over post-freeze. Jun's team signed off on that sequencing yesterday.

Only real dependency risk is pilot-team availability in early June; Oyin is lining up a backup team just in case.

subject: Re: MentorMix kickoff — status + preset trade-off
body:
Status:

- Reproduction done (a week late, 04-10 — my miss on the schedule, the mixup-weighting interaction took debugging). Quentin matched the published accuracy on the controlled web-noise benchmark within 0.5% at both the 20% and 40% noise levels, and confirmed the paper's headline: methods tuned on synthetic noise degrade much faster than MentorMix as real-world noise increases.
- Wanjiru's platform API is in review with the presets question open.

Trade-off needing a call: preset granularity. MentorMix's key hyperparameter tracks the (unknown) noise level; too few presets and users with 60%+ noise get bad defaults, too many and nobody knows what to pick. Proposal: three presets (low/med/high) plus an "estimate for me" mode that burns ~15% extra compute running a quick noise-estimation pass. Pilot team says they'd use the estimator.

Rec: ship all four. Cost is bounded and it kills the worst failure mode (confidently wrong preset).

Ondrej

subject: Re: MentorMix kickoff — decisions + handoff
body:

Closing decisions for the window:

1) Presets: approved as proposed — low/med/high plus the noise-estimator mode. The 15% estimator overhead is a fair price for not silently mistraining people.

3) Handoff: the v2 shim work stays parked until after the Corpus v2 freeze on 2026-07-10; Wanjiru's handoff doc names Jun's team as owner from there. Nothing for us to do in July.

subject: MERF kickoff — real-time radiance fields in the browser
body:

Kicking off MERF productization. The core asset: our open-source MERF work renders large-scale unbounded scenes in real time in a browser by cutting radiance-field memory with a sparse feature grid plus high-resolution 2D feature planes, and a contraction function that keeps ray-box intersection efficient for unbounded scenes. The product target is an embeddable scene viewer for partner demos.

Milestones (window through 07-20):
- 05-15: JAX training pipeline reproduced on the mipnerf360 dataset, quality parity with the paper.

subject: Mesh Diffusion kickoff — textures on the surface, not in UV space

Kicking off the mesh-diffusion texture tool. body:
Priya,

Resourcing:

subject: Re: Mesh Diffusion kickoff — status + preprocessing bottleneck
body:
Status:

- End-to-end sampling worked on 04-08: FLVAE + FLDM checkpoint dirs wired per the released config (trainer_checkpoint_dir / model_checkpoint_dir), labels read from the ply file, textures land in the output dir. Linnea's samples on the demo meshes look genuinely production-quality.
- The catch: preprocessing. Artist meshes are messier than the curated ones — non-manifold edges and degenerate triangles break the field-latent preprocessing step on 2 of the first 6 meshes we tried. Maren has a repair pass (remeshing + label reprojection) that fixes one; the other needs manual cleanup, which artists won't tolerate at scale.

Risk for the 06-08 pilot: we can hit it if we pre-screen meshes and are upfront that ~1 in 5 needs manual prep. Longer-term fix is a robust remesher, which is real engineering — proposing it as the Q3 follow-on rather than cramming it in.

Also: single-mesh training means each new mesh family wants its own FLDM — worth setting artist expectations now.

Hyun

subject: Re: Mesh Diffusion kickoff — pilot results + decisions
body:
Team,

Pilot wrapped 06-08. Results and decisions:

1) Artist ratings: 4 of 5 production meshes rated "usable with minor touch-up" or better; average time-to-variation dropped from ~2 days to 40 minutes. That's the win we pitched.
2) Decision: the robust remesher is officially the Q3 follow-on, funded — Maren scopes it with the asset team. Until then, the tool ships internally with the pre-screening checklist and the documented ~1-in-5 manual-prep caveat.
3) Decision: per-mesh-family FLDM training is accepted as the model for now; Oyin's tooling queues family training jobs overnight so artists don't feel it.
4) Scope cut: text-conditioned texture prompts — much requested — explicitly out until the research side matures.

This closes our window as a success. Writing it up for portfolio review Thursday.

Priya

subject: Meta-reg kickoff — few-shot learning without the task-design tax
body:
Hi team,

Kicking off the meta-regularization project. The problem it solves: most meta-learning algorithms implicitly require meta-training tasks to be mutually exclusive — think per-task random shuffling of class-to-label assignments — or the learner memorizes a single zero-shot solution and never adapts. Our published meta-regularization objective, built on information theory, puts precedence on data-driven adaptation instead, so users stop hand-designing task tricks. Two vision teams currently maintain exactly those brittle label-shuffling pipelines.

Milestones (short window, closes 04-20):
- 02-27: reference implementation reproducing the paper's non-mutually-exclusive benchmark results.
- 03-20: meta-reg objective packaged as a drop-in for our few-shot training library.
- 04-13: A/B on one vision team's pipeline; go/no-go for wider rollout in the next window.

Bao owns staffing; Freya is TL.

Lucia

subject: Re: Meta-reg kickoff — staffing + data timing
body:
Lucia,

Resourcing:

Staffing — Freya 50% (TL), Amara 50% on the library packaging, Oyin 30% on benchmark plumbing, Wanjiru 30% on the A/B harness with the vision team. Fits the short window.

Compute — modest: 24 A100s on titan best-effort at peak for the reproduction sweeps in February. No reservations needed.

Data timing — the A/B pipeline reads episodic task data from Corpus, and the team plans around a Corpus v2 freeze date of 2026-06-26. Our window closes 04-20, so we're two months clear, but I'm noting it because the vision team wants a follow-up A/B in late June after wider rollout — that one would need to complete before the 06-26 freeze or wait for v2. I've put a placeholder in their calendar for the week of 06-15 accordingly.

No privacy involvement needed — benchmark data only.

Bao

subject: Re: Meta-reg kickoff — status + the beta-tuning wrinkle
body:
Status:

- Reproduction landed 02-25, two days early. On the non-mutually-exclusive few-shot setup, the unregularized meta-learner does exactly what the paper warns: it collapses to a zero-shot solution that ignores task training data. With the meta-regularization objective on, adaptation is restored and we match the published accuracy within 0.7%.
- Amara's drop-in packaging is in review; API is one extra loss term plus a strength coefficient.

Wrinkle for the A/B: the regularization strength matters more than we'd like. Too low and memorization creeps back on the vision team's task distribution; too high and we underfit the amortized component. We're shipping a default tuned on their held-out task split, but the honest position is teams with very different task structure will need a short sweep — Wanjiru is adding a 3-point auto-sweep option (~2x meta-training cost when enabled) to the harness.

Still on track for the 04-13 A/B.

Freya

subject: Re: Meta-reg kickoff — A/B verdict: GO
body:
Team,

A/B results from the vision team's pipeline, and the decision:

- With meta-reg + the tuned default, they deleted their label-shuffling task construction entirely and still gained +1.9% on 5-shot accuracy versus their production setup. Pipeline code shrank by about 400 lines. That's a clean GO for wider rollout next window.
- Decision: the 3-point auto-sweep ships default-off with a loud docs recommendation, per Freya's read. The 2x meta-training cost is opt-in, not a surprise.
- Scope confirmation: the RNN-based variants from the paper stay out of scope for the library; nobody asked and the maintenance cost is real.

Bao — the late-June follow-up A/B with their production refresh stays penciled per your data-timing note; let's confirm it at Q3 planning.

Great, tight execution on a 2.5-month window. Thank you all.

Lucia

subject: MPL kickoff — squeezing accuracy out of 10% of the labels
body:
Team,

Kicking off the Meta Pseudo Labels integration. Why: several vision customers have huge unlabeled pools and tiny labeled sets, and our open-source MPL work is the strongest teacher-student recipe we own for that regime — the released implementation covers the two low-resource benchmarks, CIFAR-10-4000 and ImageNet-10%.

Milestones (window closes 05-04):
- 03-06: CIFAR-10-4000 reproduction with the wrn-28-2 config on our accelerator quota, matching published accuracy.
- 04-03: ImageNet-10% reproduction with resnet-50; training-cost profile documented.
- 04-27: proposal for the Q3 scaled run on the internal low-label datasets, with a real budget attached — this thing is compute-hungry and I don't want a surprise in July.

Note the released code is TPU-only, so we run on our cirrus quota — Santiago will confirm feasibility. Umar is TL.

Lucia

subject: Re: MPL kickoff — compute feasibility + budget
body:
Lucia,

Feasibility + resourcing:

Staffing — Umar 40% (TL), Ondrej 40% on reproduction runs, Paloma 30% on the training-stack port, Chiara 40% on data pipelines and eval plumbing.

Compute — confirmed the TPU-only constraint is fine: CIFAR-10-4000 with wrn-28-2 fits our standing cirrus-tpu portfolio quota easily; ImageNet-10% with resnet-50 takes roughly a third of our March quota for ~9 days. Tight but no extra reservation needed.

Budget for the Q3 scaled run — good news: Idris has verbally earmarked $120k from Q3 discretionary compute budget line B-88 for this project, which covers the internal low-label runs at the scale Umar sketched. I'll get it written into the Q3 plan when the cycle opens; treating it as committed for planning purposes.

So: no blockers on any milestone. Watch item is March cirrus contention if another team bursts.

Santiago

subject: Re: MPL kickoff — status: both benchmarks in, one cost flag
body:
Status:

- CIFAR-10-4000: reproduced 03-04 with the wrn-28-2 config; we landed within 0.3% of the published accuracy. The UDA settings matter — Ondrej confirmed sensitivity to uda_threshold=0.6 and uda_weight=8; drifting those cost us a point in early runs.
- ImageNet-10%: resnet-50 run finished 04-05, accuracy within 0.5% of published. But the cost profile is the story: the teacher-student loop means every step trains two models plus the UDA batch, and our measured cost came in ~1.4x my original estimate for the full 300k-step schedule (the mpl_student_lr_wait_steps warmup interacts badly with our preemption rate — Chiara has a checkpoint-cadence fix that recovers most of it).

Flag: at measured cost, the Q3 scaled-run proposal lands right at the top of the budget envelope we discussed, with no room for reruns. Options in the 04-27 proposal: trim to 2 datasets, or seek headroom.

Umar

subject: Re: MPL kickoff — Q3 proposal decision
body:
Team,

Decision on the 04-27 proposal, made with Santiago this morning:

1) Q3 scaled run is scoped to two internal low-label datasets, not three. At Umar's measured 1.4x cost profile, two datasets fit the $120k earmarked for us on line B-88 with ~15% rerun headroom; three would leave zero margin, and this quarter taught us that margin is not optional with a teacher-student loop.
2) Chiara's checkpoint-cadence fix is mandatory for all Q3 runs — it's worth roughly $9k of recovered preemption waste on its own.
3) The third dataset (the long-tail retail one) becomes first in line if headroom materializes late in Q3.

Idris — proposal doc with these numbers is in your inbox for the planning cycle; grateful for a confirm-in-writing when the Q3 books open.

Strong quarter, everyone. Both benchmarks reproduced and an honest cost model — exactly what the scaled run needed.

Lucia

subject: MetaPose kickoff — multi-camera 3D pose without calibration
body:
Hi all,

Kicking off MetaPose productization. The differentiator: our published MetaPose model estimates 3D human pose from multiple cameras with unknown calibration, trains on 2D keypoint data only, and beats both classical bundle adjustment and weakly-supervised monocular baselines on Human3.6M and the harder in-the-wild Ski-Pose PTZ set. Two prospective internal customers: the sports-analysis demo team and the robotics lab's motion-capture-free evaluation rig — both have multi-camera setups nobody ever calibrates properly.

Milestones (window through 06-15):
- 04-10: released checkpoints + data reproducing paper metrics in our eval harness.
- 05-15: latency-optimized inference path; the "minimal latency overhead" claim quantified on our hardware.
- 06-08: pilot on the robotics lab's 4-camera rig with occlusion-heavy scenes.

Daniela owns staffing; Linnea is TL. Q3 continuation planning will come up mid-window — this one won't finish at the pilot.

subject: Re: MetaPose kickoff — staffing + compute
body:
Lucia,

Daniela

subject: Re: MetaPose kickoff — status + occlusion risk for the pilot
body:
Status:

- Reproduction: done 04-08 from the released metapose.tar data + checkpoints; Human3.6M and Ski-Pose PTZ numbers match the paper in our harness (PMPJPE within 1mm on H36M).
- Latency: Rosa's optimized path runs the full multi-view model in 31ms on a single A100 — comfortably real-time for the sports use case, and consistent with the minimal-latency-overhead claim.

Risk for the 06-08 pilot: the model's uncertainty handling for occluded joints is a strength on Ski-Pose, but the robotics rig is worse than anything in the papers — two of four cameras are frequently blocked by the robot arm itself, simultaneously. In our synthetic-occlusion stress test, PMPJPE degrades ~2.2x when two views drop together. Maren is adding a per-frame confidence gate so downstream consumers can filter; I'd rather ship honest confidence than smoothed garbage.

We're on track, but the pilot report will need an occlusion-regime section.

Linnea

subject: Re: MetaPose kickoff — pilot outcome + Q3 staffing decision
body:
Lucia,

Closing the window:

Pilot outcome — the robotics lab accepted the results 06-09. With Maren's confidence gate, their eval rig filters the double-occlusion frames (about 11% of footage) and the remaining coverage beats their old manually-calibrated setup on accuracy while requiring zero calibration. They want the double-occlusion problem solved properly in Q3.

Q3 staffing, for the allocation sheet ahead of the 06-26 OKR lock: Linnea Yamada is committed at 60%+ to this project for July 2026 — she anchors the occlusion-robustness work and the sports-team onboarding, with Rosa continuing at 40%. I've entered both in the July allocation sheet today.

A genuinely good pilot. Details in the report attached to the OKR draft.

Daniela

subject: Kickoff: mFACE factuality scoring for multilingual summaries
body:
Hi Santiago,

Kicking off the mFACE track for H1. The pitch: our open-source release ships human judgements over XLSum summaries — per-example min/avg/max scores for comprehensibility (q1), full attributability to the article (q2), and overall quality (q3) — plus ROUGE and an NLI entailment score (e2e_nli_score). We want to turn that into an internal factuality gate for the multilingual summarization products.

Rough milestones inside our Feb 9 – May 11 window:
- End of Feb: judgement data loaded into Evalline, schema agreed with Tomas.
- Early April: NLI scorer reproduced and calibrated against the q2 human labels.
- Early May: launch-review packet for using the scorer as a pre-ship gate.

Product framing for OKRs: "no summary ships in a language where the factuality scorer is uncalibrated." Can you send staffing plus compute asks by end of next week?

Thanks,
Priya

subject: Re: Kickoff: mFACE factuality scoring for multilingual summaries
body:
Hi Priya,

Staffing plan: Maren Zhou 50% on the Evalline ingestion and schema work, Amara Okafor 40% on reproducing the NLI scorer, Farah Haddad 30% on the per-language calibration dashboards. Milan Zapata is committed at 60% to this project for June 2026 to build the scorer-serving path and the batch API — I've already blocked his June on our side, so please don't let anyone else grab him.

Compute is light: the NLI scorer fine-tunes fit on 16 titan-a100 GPUs best-effort, no reservation needed. Main platform dependency is Evalline; Tomas's team owns the harness and I'd like the schema review on their calendar before March 6.

One flag: the judgement data has three raters per example (hence min/avg/max), and inter-rater spread on q2 is wide for the lower-resource languages. Calibration there will take longer than the roadmap implies.

subject: Re: Kickoff: mFACE factuality scoring for multilingual summaries — status + a risk
body:
Hi both,

Status: judgement data is fully loaded in Evalline (Maren landed the schema 3/20). The NLI scorer reproduction is done and I'm mid-calibration. Good news first: correlation between e2e_nli_score and the human q2 (attributability) average is strong on the high-resource languages — Spearman 0.61 on the test split.

The risk: ROUGE is actively misleading as a factuality proxy. We see summaries with rouge2 above 0.30 that raters scored near the bottom on q2. If any product team keeps ROUGE as their ship gate they will pass hallucinated summaries. I'd like the launch-review packet to explicitly deprecate ROUGE-only gating.

Also, for 9 of the lower-resource languages the entailment probabilities are badly mis-calibrated (systematically over-confident). I need ~2 more weeks and a per-language temperature fit before I'd trust a threshold there.

Amara

subject: Re: Kickoff: mFACE factuality scoring for multilingual summaries — decision + scope cut
body:
Team,

Decisions from yesterday's review, so we land inside the May 11 window:

1) The scorer ships as an internal eval gate only. Kofi confirmed the underlying judgement data inherits XLSum's CC BY-NC-SA license, so nothing derived from the annotations goes into a commercial-facing artifact. The NLI scorer itself is fine; the human labels stay eval-side.
2) Scope cut: we gate the 12 languages where Amara's calibration passed. The 9 over-confident lower-resource languages move to an H2 stretch goal rather than blocking launch review.
3) ROUGE-only gating is formally deprecated in the packet, with Amara's rouge2-vs-q2 examples as the evidence.

Nadia has us on the May 8 Launch Review Board agenda. Santiago — please confirm the June serving work is still staffed as planned.

Thanks all, genuinely nice work.
Priya

subject: Kickoff: microscope focus-quality QC for imaging partners
body:
Hi Daniela,

Kicking off the microscope image-quality track (window: Apr 20 – Jul 27). The asset is our open-source deep-learning focus-quality classifier (the BMC Bioinformatics method) plus the Focus_check script, which renders whole-plate montages per channel so a lab tech can eyeball data quality in one screen instead of clicking through thousands of sites.

subject: Re: Kickoff: microscope focus-quality QC for imaging partners

subject: Kickoff: MIR / wtd-Assign for aggregate-label learning
body:
Hi Santiago,

Kicking off the multiple-instance-regression project (Feb 16 – May 11). The research asset is our UAI 2024 open-source release: the wtd-Assign approach for training an MLP when you only have bag-level labels rather than per-instance ones. Product angle for data-platforms: several partner datasets only arrive as aggregates for privacy reasons, and MIR lets us train instance-level predictors on them anyway.

Milestones:
- Early March: reproduce the paper's synthetic-bag results across bag sizes with the released prep scripts.
- Early April: 1940 US Census benchmark reproduced (the paper config: batch_size 100, 1024 hidden units) and wired into Evalline.
- Early May: a design note on running wtd-Assign against Corpus-hosted aggregate datasets, for Q3 OKR planning.

Send me staffing and the Corpus dependency picture when you can.

Thanks,
Dmitri

subject: Re: Kickoff: MIR / wtd-Assign — staffing + Corpus dependency
body:
Hi Dmitri,

Staffing: Gustavo Moreau 50% leads reproduction and owns the wtd-Assign training runs; Bilal Novak 40% on dataset prep (synthetic bags across bag sizes, plus the census ingestion); Emeka Pinto 30% on the Evalline wiring; Maren Zhou 20% consulting on schema, since she's mostly on a language project this half.

Compute: modest — the MLP configs run fine on 8 titan-a100 GPUs best-effort, no reservation.

On the Corpus dependency: the v2 migration freeze is 2026-08-07, so our bag-generation jobs on the v1 pipelines can run through the whole project window and well past it — no migration work needs to land before we close in May. I'll still have Emeka write the v2 port plan as part of the design note, but nothing blocks.

One heads-up: the census CSV is 14 GB and the prep script is single-threaded; Bilal may parallelize it rather than wait 9 hours per bag-size sweep.

subject: Re: Kickoff: MIR / wtd-Assign — April status + bag-size risk
body:
Hi both,

Status: synthetic-bag results reproduced across all released bag sizes; the census benchmark matches the paper within noise using the reference config (batch_size 100, embedding_dim 0, 1024 hidden units). Emeka has both benchmarks reporting into Evalline nightly.

The risk for the design note: wtd-Assign degrades faster than I expected as bags get large. On synthetic data, instance-level MSE at bag size 32 is roughly 2.4x the bag-size-8 number, and the partner aggregates Dmitri has in mind are mostly 50-to-200-person bags. The paper's learnability guarantees are honest about this regime being hard — it's not a bug, it's the problem.

Proposal: the May design note recommends MIR for partners with bag sizes <=32 and flags larger bags as needing either auxiliary features or a different formulation. Better to scope it now then over-promise for Q3.

Gustavo

subject: Re: Kickoff: MIR / wtd-Assign — closing decisions
body:
Team,

Wrapping the window (May 11). Decisions:

1) We adopt Gustavo's scoping: the design note ships with a hard recommendation of bag size <=32 for wtd-Assign, with the 2.4x MSE degradation curve as the headline chart. The two partners with 50+ person bags get an explicit "not yet" rather than a maybe.
2) The Evalline nightly benchmarks stay on as a regression suite — Emeka, please hand pager duty for those jobs to the platform rotation before you roll off.
3) For Q3 OKR planning (locked 2026-06-26): I'm proposing one OKR around onboarding the first small-bag partner dataset, not the big ones. That matches what we can actually deliver.

Emeka's v2 port plan is appended to the design note as-is. Nice clean close, everyone — this one did what it said on the tin.

Dmitri

subject: Kickoff: cross-dataset label harmonization (missing_link)
body:
Hi Deshawn,

Kicking off label harmonization for the vision corpora (window Mar 9 – Jul 6). The asset is our open-source ECCV release: manually verified label relations across three dataset pairs — ade_coco_mapping.csv, ade_bdd_mapping.csv, bdd_coco_mapping.csv — built automatically over MSEG annotations and then hand-corrected. Each row is a simple (label_a, relation, label_b) triple.

Why this matters as a product: Corpus hosts segmentation sets with incompatible label vocabularies, and every team re-derives their own crosswalk. A blessed relation service means joint training and joint eval come for free.

Milestones: April — relation files ingested into Corpus with a query API stub; late May — harmonized ADE20k+COCO training run validating the mappings; late June — full joint-training validation sweep across all three pairs; sign-off by Jul 6.

Staffing and compute asks to me by end of March, please.

Dmitri

subject: Re: Kickoff: cross-dataset label harmonization — staffing + compute
body:
Hi Dmitri,

Plan:

- Kaia Wolde 50% owns the relation semantics and the hand-verification of any new pairs we add; Efe Lindqvist 40% on the joint-training experiments; Linnea Yamada 40% on the Corpus ingestion and query API.
- Good news on compute: we hold the cirrus-tpu reservation — 256 accelerators for the week of 2026-06-22 — which is exactly when the joint-training validation sweep needs to run, so the schedule works backward from that week. subject: Re: Kickoff: cross-dataset label harmonization — May status + relation-direction risk
body:
Hi both,

Status: Linnea's ingestion is done — all three mapping files are queryable in Corpus, and the API stub returns relation triples in under 10 ms. My ADE20k+COCO harmonized training run finished Friday: +1.8 mIoU over training on either dataset alone, which is the validation signal we wanted.

Risk: direction handling. The mappings encode asymmetric relations (a BDD label can be a strict parent of a COCO label), and I found 14 cases where naive symmetric merging silently collapses parent/child into equivalence — "rider" vs "person" being the ugly one. Kaia is re-auditing those rows against the original MSEG-derived annotations; her call is that maybe 5 need manual correction, consistent with how the release itself was built (auto-derive, then hand-fix).

This doesn't move the June sweep, but the query API needs a direction-aware mode before anyone builds on it. Linnea estimates 1 week.

Efe

subject: Re: Kickoff: cross-dataset label harmonization — sweep week + closing decisions
body:
Team,

Quick decisions as the validation sweep spins up this week on our cirrus allocation:

1) Kaia's 5 corrected rows are in; the sweep runs against the corrected mappings only. We are not maintaining a "paper-faithful" variant — the corrected CSVs become the canonical Corpus copy, with a changelog note.
2) Direction-aware query mode ships with the sweep results. Symmetric mode stays available but logs a deprecation warning, per Linnea's suggestion.
3) Scope cut: the fourth dataset pair we floated in April (adding the drive-scene set) is out of this window. It goes to the Q3 list — OKRs are locking Friday and I'd rather commit to what's running now.

If the sweep confirms the +1.8 mIoU pattern holds across all three pairs, we present at the Jul 2 review and close on schedule.

Dmitri

subject: Kickoff: black-box debiasing service (ml_debiaser)
body:
Hi Santiago,

Kicking off the debiasing-service project (Feb 16 – May 11). The research assets are our two NeurIPS releases: a near-optimal post-processing method (randomized_threshold) that debiases binary classifiers treated purely as black boxes, and a reduce-to-binary pre-processing method for multiclass datasets. The multiclass one is the product hook — it needs no sensitive attribute at inference time, which is exactly the constraint our internal model teams keep hitting.

Milestones:
- Mid-March: both methods wrapped behind one internal API, walk-through example ported.
- Mid-April: pilot with two model teams, bias metrics before/after in Evalline.
- Early May: rollout recommendation plus a Corpus integration plan for debiased dataset generation.

Can you send staffing, compute, and the Corpus dependency read by early March?

Thanks,
Dmitri

subject: Re: Kickoff: black-box debiasing service — staffing + Corpus timeline
body:
Hi Dmitri,

Staffing: Nikhil Abebe 50% owns the service API and the randomized_threshold wrapper; Csilla Nassar 40% on the reduce-to-binary multiclass path and the pilot-team evaluations; Quentin Farkas 40% on Corpus integration; Linnea Yamada 20% shared with the label-harmonization work, advising on schema.

Compute: negligible — post-processing is CPU-bound; the pilot retrains fit in 8 titan-a100 GPUs best-effort.

On Corpus: we're planning around the Corpus v2 migration freeze on 2026-07-10, per Jun's timeline: the debiased-dataset write-back path lands on v1 during our window, and Quentin ports it to v2 in the first week of July, comfortably before the freeze.

One early technical note from Csilla: the papers' test-time guarantees hold with high probability only given sufficient sample size per group. The pilot teams need a per-group sample-size check up front or we'll be promising guarantees we can't keep.

Santiago

subject: Re: Kickoff: black-box debiasing service — pilot status + small-group risk
body:
Hi both,

Pilot status: both teams are live behind Nikhil's API. Team A (binary risk classifier) is the clean win — randomized_threshold cut their demographic-parity gap from 11.2% to 2.1% with a 0.4-point AUC cost, training-set bias requirement fully satisfied. Team B is the multiclass case, 7 classes, and reduce-to-binary works, but here's the risk I flagged in March showing up in the data: two of their groups have under 400 samples, and on held-out data the bias constraint is violated for exactly those two groups. The papers are explicit that generalization needs sufficient per-group sample size, so this is expected behaviour, not an implementation bug.

Proposal: the service refuses to certify any group below a sample-size floor (I'm fitting the threshold empirically, likely 800–1,000) and reports "insufficient data" instead. Less flattering, more honest.

Csilla

subject: Re: Kickoff: black-box debiasing service — rollout decision
body:
Team,

Closing decisions ahead of the May 11 window end:

1) The service goes to general availability for binary classifiers now; Team A's 11.2% -> 2.1% parity-gap result headlines the rollout note.
2) Csilla's certification floor is adopted: groups below the empirical sample-size threshold get "insufficient data," never a certified badge. Kofi is comfortable with that language from a review standpoint — a false certification is the worst outcome for everyone.
3) Multiclass stays in pilot through Q3 until we've seen one more team with healthier group sizes.
4) Quentin's Corpus write-back plan is approved as scoped in March; no changes to the July port timing.

Thanks all — this is the rare fairness project that ends with a number we can defend.

Dmitri

subject: Kickoff: MMMT-IF as the multimodal instruction-following gate
body:
Hi Daniela,

Kicking off MMMT-IF (Mar 16 – Jun 22). The benchmark from our open-source release is a genuinely hard one: image-based multi-turn Q&A where global instructions are added between questions and constrain the answer format. Models have to retrieve multiple instructions spread across a long chat history and reason over all of them at once — and every instruction is program-verifiable, so scoring is objective, no rater budget needed.

Why product cares: the assistant team keeps shipping models that pass single-turn evals and then drop formatting constraints by turn 12 in real sessions. This becomes the pre-release gate for that failure mode.

Milestones: mid-April, harness running in Evalline with the verifier programs ported; late May, baseline sweep across our three candidate checkpoints; mid-June, gate thresholds proposed for launch review.

Staffing and platform asks when you get a chance?

Thanks,
Priya

subject: Re: Kickoff: MMMT-IF — staffing + platform dependencies
body:
Hi Priya,

Plan:

- Tereza Aliyev 50% owns the Evalline harness and porting the instruction-verifier programs; Paloma Castillo 40% on the inference plumbing for the checkpoint sweep; Yusuf Keita 30% on analysis and the gate-threshold proposal.
- Compute: the baseline sweep needs 64 titan-a100 GPUs best-effort for about two weeks in May. No reservation-class ask.
- Corpus: we're building the plan around the Corpus v2 migration freeze on 2026-07-10: the benchmark's image assets and chat transcripts get ingested on v2 directly, and since our window closes June 22 we're done well before the freeze either way.

One scoping note from Tereza — the verifiers are objective but they're per-instruction programs, and chaining them across turns means the harness has to replay full chat history per example. That's a 6x token cost versus single-turn evals; Paloma is batching accordingly.

Daniela

subject: Re: Kickoff: MMMT-IF — baseline results + a gating trade-off
body:
Hi both,

Baseline sweep is done. Headline: all three candidate checkpoints degrade sharply with instruction count. With 1–2 active instructions, verifier pass rates sit at 88–91%. By turn 15, with 6+ instructions accumulated in history, the best checkpoint passes 54% and the worst 41%. The failure is retrieval, not reasoning — when we re-inject all active instructions into the final prompt as an oracle, pass rates recover to 85%+. That matches what the paper found; the instructions spread through history are what kills them.

The trade-off for the gate: if we set the threshold at 80% pass over full 20-turn sessions, nothing ships this quarter. My proposal is a two-tier gate — 85% at up-to-4 instructions (hard block) and a published-but-non-blocking score on the full benchmark, tightening each quarter.

tbh the honest read is the models need an instruction-tracking scratchpad, but that's a model-team roadmap item, not an eval item.

Yusuf

subject: Kickoff: MobileBERT on-device NLU
body:
Hi Bruno,

Kicking off the MobileBERT productization (Mar 9 – Jul 20). The asset: our open-source thin BERT_LARGE with bottleneck structures and a carefully balanced split between self-attention and feed-forward capacity. The released artifacts give us a big head start — the uncased_L-24_H-128_B-512_A-4_F-4_OPT checkpoint plus float32 and quantized int8 SavedModels for SQuAD at sequence length 384, ready for tf.lite conversion.

Product story: the on-device assistant needs question-answering that runs on mid-tier phones without a server round trip. This is the launch-review candidate for the Q3 device release.

Milestones: April — SQuAD V1.1 fine-tune reproduced in-house; May — int8 path validated on our device farm; early July — final quality sweep; Jul 20 — launch-review packet.

Send staffing and the compute reservation plan when ready — the July sweep is the long pole.

Thanks,
Priya

subject: Re: Kickoff: MobileBERT on-device NLU — staffing + compute
body:
Hi Priya,

Staffing: Vera Egede 40% leads the fine-tuning and distillation work; Efe Lindqvist 30% on eval quality; Amara Okafor 40% on the tf.lite conversion and device-farm automation; Milan Zapata 30% on the serving-side fallback path for devices below the memory floor.
