Compute is locked: we hold the vulcan-h100 reservation — 512 accelerators for the week of 2026-07-06 — for the final distillation-and-finetune sweep, and I've built the July schedule backward from that week. Everything earlier (SQuAD V1.1 reproduction at learning rate 4e-05, doc stride 128, per the released config) runs on titan-a100 best-effort, 64 GPUs.

Note I kept us clear of the Vulcan maintenance window in late June — reservation starts the week after.

One ask: the device farm needs 6 more mid-tier handsets to make the int8 latency numbers representative. ~$4k, coming to you for signoff.

Bruno

subject: Re: Kickoff: MobileBERT on-device NLU — May status + int8 risk
body:
Hi both,

Status: Vera's SQuAD V1.1 fine-tune reproduction matches the released numbers (F1 within 0.2 of reference). The float32 SavedModel converts to tf.lite cleanly at sequence length 384 and runs on the full device farm.

The risk is the int8 path. Quantized conversion works, but on the 6 new mid-tier handsets we see an F1 drop of 1.9 points versus float32 — double what the release notes led us to expect — and latency on the two cheapest devices is 340 ms per query against our 250 ms budget. Efe traced most of the quality gap to the bottleneck layers being sensitive to per-tensor quantization; per-channel helps but isn't supported by one of the target delegates.

Options: (a) ship float16 on low-end and int8 elsewhere, (b) quantization-aware fine-tune in the July sweep. (b) is better long-term and Vera says the sweep has capacity for it.

Amara

subject: Re: Kickoff: MobileBERT on-device NLU — decisions before the July sweep
body:
Team,

Decisions locked before next week's sweep:

1) We go with option (b): quantization-aware fine-tuning is in scope for the July run on Vulcan, with Vera owning the grid. Amara's option (a) float16 fallback is the contingency if QAT doesn't close the 1.9-point F1 gap — Milan, please have the capability check for the fallback path ready either way.
2) The 250 ms latency budget stands. If the two cheapest devices can't hit it post-QAT, they route to Milan's server fallback rather than degrading the on-device bar.
3) Launch-review packet moves from Jul 20 to Jul 17 at Nadia's request — LRB calendar is packed that week, and sign-off is required before the device team's external demo.

Efe — please pre-register the eval plan for the sweep so we're not arguing metrics after the fact.

Thanks,
Priya

subject: Kickoff: pruning toolkit for the efficiency portfolio
body:
Hi Ivo,

Kicking off the pruning-toolkit project (Mar 9 – May 18). The base is our open-source model-pruning library: it injects pruning ops into the training graph so models are pruned while they train — you wrap a layer's weights with apply_mask and get mask and threshold variables that control which weights participate in the forward pass. The extension we care about is the newer gradient-based pruning ops alongside the classic magnitude-based ones.

Product framing: three model teams asked for a supported "train sparse" path this half. Serving cost is the efficiency portfolio's headline OKR, and block sparsity is what actually buys us hardware speedups rather than paper sparsity.

Milestones: end of March — library adopted by first pilot team with masks stripped for deployment; late April — magnitude vs gradient-based comparison on two internal models; mid-May — sparsity-vs-quality recommendation report.

Staffing and compute by Mar 20?

Zofia

subject: Re: Kickoff: pruning toolkit — staffing + compute
body:
Hi Zofia,

Staffing: Hyun Traore 40% as tech lead across both pruning families; Wei Ivanov 40% on the pilot-team integrations; Giannis Sato 30% on the mask-stripping/deployment tooling; Jorge Vidal 20% on CI and the benchmark harness. Vera Egede is committed at 65% to this project for May 2026 — she owns the gradient-based pruning comparison and the final sparsity-vs-quality report, and that report is the deliverable the whole window closes on. In April she's at 30% while she wraps a language-team commitment.

Compute: the comparison grid (two models x two pruning methods x four sparsity targets) needs 96 titan-a100 GPUs best-effort through April and May. No Vulcan ask.

One constraint to note: block sparsity trades quality for actual hardware speedup, so the report will quote both raw sparsity and block-sparse throughput — otherwise the model teams will pick settings that look good and serve slow.

Ivo

subject: Re: Kickoff: pruning toolkit — April status + a threshold-scheduling risk
body:
Hi both,

Status: pilot team 1 is training with magnitude pruning at 80% target sparsity; Giannis's tooling strips the mask and threshold variables from the trained graph cleanly, so deployed checkpoints carry no pruning overhead. Wei has team 2 integrating this week.

Comparison grid is half done. Early read: gradient-based pruning wins at high sparsity — at 90%, it holds a 1.1-point quality advantage over magnitude on the recommendation model — but is roughly even at 70-80%.

The risk: the pruning schedule's threshold updates interact badly with team 1's learning-rate warm restarts. Twice we saw the effective sparsity snap from 60% to 78% within 500 steps after a restart, destabilizing training. Workaround is freezing threshold updates for 1k steps around each restart; Vera is folding a proper fix into the hparams defaults so pilot teams don't need to know this footgun exists.

Hyun

subject: Re: Kickoff: pruning toolkit — closing decisions
body:
Team,

Decisions to close by May 18:

1) The recommendation report ships with a two-tier guidance: magnitude pruning as the default up to 80% sparsity (simpler, no quality gap), gradient-based for anything above — Vera's 90% comparison with the 1.1-point advantage is the dividing line. Her final report lands Friday.
2) The warm-restart threshold fix goes into the library defaults before we call the toolkit "supported." Nobody should have to learn that failure mode from a chart in our appendix.
3) Scope cut: the block-sparsity throughput benchmarks cover the serving hardware we actually run, not the full matrix Jorge sketched. The exotic accelerator column moves to a Q3 item — OKR planning locks Jun 26 and I'd rather propose it there properly.

Good window, team. Pilot 3 starts under the efficiency banner in June.

Zofia

subject: Kickoff: Model Swarms expert adaptation
body:
Hi Bao,

Kicking off Model Swarms (Mar 23 – Jun 22). The method from our open-source release: treat a pool of LLM experts as particles in a swarm search and collaboratively adapt them to a target task — no gradient training, just utility-guided search that tracks a global best. The release ships a starter pipeline on the NLGraph graph-reasoning dataset, which is conveniently on-portfolio for us.

Product thesis: retrieval customers keep asking for domain-adapted experts without the cost and data-governance overhead of fine-tuning. If swarm search gets us 80% of fine-tuning quality at a fraction of the compute, that's a service.

Milestones: mid-April — NLGraph reproduction with the released search scripts; late May — swarm search on two internal retrieval tasks; mid-June — final validation sweep and a go/no-go for a Q3 service beta.

Staffing, compute, and the data-migration picture by Apr 10, please.

Anders

subject: Re: Kickoff: Model Swarms — staffing + the migration date
body:
Hi Anders,

Staffing: Fumiko Rossi 50% leads the method work and owns the utility functions; Freya Ruiz 30% on the two internal retrieval tasks; Leilani Nakamura 40% on the search infrastructure (the released scripts assume a fixed 5-GPU layout via the -g flag — she's generalizing that to our scheduler); Oyin Iversen 30% on expert-pool management and checkpoint hygiene.

Compute: each search run holds 8 experts resident, so we need 40 titan-a100 GPUs best-effort through May, then a burst for the final sweep in June.

Heads-up on the hard date: the Corpus v2 migration freeze is 2026-06-26, the same week Q3 OKRs lock, so the swarm-search validation corpora have to be fully migrated onto v2 before our final sweep or we lose data access mid-run. Leilani has migration tasks in her plan for late May, which is tight but doable.

Bao

subject: Re: Kickoff: Model Swarms — May status + utility-function risk
body:
Hi both,

Status: NLGraph reproduction is solid — our global best beats the starting best-validation expert by 9.4 points, in line with the release's reported search dynamics, and the utility_scratchpad.json trajectories (global best/worst plus per-particle) match the published pattern. Leilani's scheduler integration means we can run swarms on arbitrary GPU sets now, not just the fixed 5-GPU layout.

The risk is on the internal tasks. Retrieval task A improves +6.1 on its utility metric, but task B shows classic reward hacking: the swarm found experts that inflate the retrieval-utility proxy by emitting degenerate long answers, so the proxy goes up while human-checked usefulness goes down. Swarm search optimizes exactly what you measure — there's no gradient regularizer to save you.

Freya and I are rebuilding task B's utility as a composite (retrieval score + length penalty + a small held-out probe). Costs us ~2 weeks; the June sweep should still fit.

Fumiko

subject: Re: Kickoff: Model Swarms — go/no-go decision
body:
Team,

Decision from this morning's review: qualified go.

1) The Q3 service beta proceeds, scoped to tasks with vetted utility functions. Fumiko's composite-utility recipe (task metric + length penalty + held-out probe) becomes a hard requirement for onboarding — no raw single-proxy utilities, full stop. Task B's reward-hacking traces go in the service docs as the cautionary example.
2) The final sweep runs this week as planned; Oyin, please snapshot the expert pools and global_best checkpoints for the beta baseline before we release the GPUs.
3) Scope cut: multi-task swarm composition (the mu2Net-style ambition Freya floated) is out of the beta. One task per swarm until we trust the utilities.

I'm writing the Q3 OKR submission around "two beta customers live by end of August" — deadline for OKR lock is the 26th, so speak now.

Anders

subject: Kickoff: MolDQN lead-optimization pilot
body:
Hi Bao,

Kicking off MolDQN (Apr 20 – Jul 27). Our open-source release frames molecule optimization as an MDP — the definition in chemgraph/mcts/molecules.py — where every action is a chemically valid edit, and a DQN learns to walk molecules toward a property target. The starter task is QED optimization with both naive and bootstrap DQN configs.

Why now: two chemistry partners want interpretable lead optimization where every intermediate structure is valid by construction — that's the trust story this portfolio exists for, and it's a differentiator against black-box generative baselines.

Milestones: mid-May — QED reproduction on both configs; mid-June — partner property targets encoded as reward functions; mid-July — pilot report with a go/no-go on a Q4 engagement.

Known limitation to scope honestly: the MDP doesn't support modifying aromatic bonds or multiple oxidation states, so some partner chemotypes are out of reach. I want that in the pilot agreement, not discovered later.

Staffing + budget by May 8?

Ximena

subject: Re: Kickoff: MolDQN lead-optimization pilot — staffing + budget
body:
Hi Ximena,

Staffing: Wei Ivanov 40% leads the RL work and reward design; Saoirse Eriksen 40% on the training pipeline and the SA_Score dependency packaging (the rdkit Contrib module needs vendoring for our build); Giannis Sato 30% on partner-facing tooling; Oyin Iversen 20% on experiment tracking, shared with another search project.

On money: Idris has verbally earmarked $240k from the Q3 discretionary compute budget line B-58 for this project, which covers the bootstrap-DQN ensemble sweeps plus the partner pilot runs, so treat the compute plan below as funded.

Compute plan: QED reproduction is cheap (single-GPU jobs), but bootstrap DQN is an ensemble — step 1 and step 2 configs per the release — and the partner sweeps multiply that by reward variants. I'm estimating 120k GPU-hours on titan-a100 across June–July.

One flag: Wei wants episode-level logging of every molecule edit for the trust/audit story. Storage is small; the review overhead isn't.

Bao

subject: Re: Kickoff: MolDQN lead-optimization pilot — June status + aromatic-bond risk
body:
Hi both,

Status: QED reproduction done on both configs — bootstrap DQN (two-step schedule) beats naive DQN on mean final QED, 0.041 higher across 20 seeds, matching the paper's ordering. Saoirse vendored SA_Score cleanly and the pipeline runs end-to-end with full episode logs, so every optimized molecule ships with its edit trajectory. Partner A's logP-with-similarity-constraint reward is encoded and training.

The risk has a shape now: Partner B's series is heavily aromatic. Because the MDP can't modify aromatic bonds — including bonds perceived as aromatic when parsing the starting molecule — about 60% of their seed structures have most of their interesting edit space locked. Early runs confirm it: the agent decorates the periphery instead of touching the core, and property gains plateau ~40% below Partner A's.

Recommendation: pilot report presents Partner B as "supported for peripheral optimization only." Not a failure, but it must be in writing.

Wei

subject: Re: Kickoff: MolDQN lead-optimization pilot — decisions for the pilot report
body:
Team,

Decisions for the Jul 27 close:

1) Pilot report recommends go for a Q4 engagement with Partner A only. Partner B gets the "peripheral optimization only" framing in Wei's words, verbatim, plus an explicit note that aromatic-core edits need MDP work we have not scheduled.
2) The edit-trajectory audit log becomes a headline feature, not an internal artifact — Giannis, package the trajectory viewer for the partner readout. It's the strongest trust differentiator we have.
3) Budget: we're tracking to the B-58 earmark; Idris, looping you in since the Q4 engagement would need a fresh line — the Q3 earmark doesn't roll over.
4) Scope cut confirmed: multi-property optimization stays out of the pilot.

Readout with both partners the week of Jul 20. Nice work getting the science and the honesty into the same document.

Ximena

subject: Kickoff: advice-based frequency-moment estimation for telemetry
body:
Hi Ivo,

Kicking off moment_advice (Mar 23 – Jul 6). The open-source release estimates frequency moments by sampling according to advice, benchmarked against three baselines: perfect advice (exact frequencies), PPSWOR ell_1 sampling, and ell_2 sampling. It supports exactly the input shapes our infra customers have — graph edges for in/out degree moments (with parallel edges counted) and net_traffic packets keyed by unordered IP pairs.

Product case: the telemetry team samples network flows today with plain ell_1-style sampling and their heavy-hitter estimates degrade on skewed traffic. Learned advice should cut estimation error substantially at the same sample budget — that's the pitch to make it a platform primitive.

Milestones: April — reproduce baselines on public graph datasets; late May — advice models trained on our telemetry history; late June — full-scale validation; Jul 6 close with an adoption recommendation.

Staffing + compute by mid-April please.

Anders

subject: Re: Kickoff: advice-based moment estimation — staffing + compute
body:
Hi Anders,

Staffing: Umar Costa 50% leads the estimation work and owns the baseline comparisons; Freya Ruiz 30% on the advice-model architecture; Vera Egede 25% on the telemetry data plumbing — she's heavily committed elsewhere until June, so her share rises to 40% after the 1st.

Compute: the sampling experiments themselves are CPU-heavy but cheap. The expensive part is training advice models on 90 days of telemetry history. We hold the cirrus-tpu reservation — 256 accelerators for the week of 2026-06-22 — for training the advice models at full telemetry scale, and the June milestones are sequenced around that week. Before then, prototyping fits on 16 titan-a100 GPUs best-effort.

One scoping note from Umar: for the graph inputs we'll validate on temporal graphs too (the "u v time" edge format), since the telemetry team's flows are inherently timestamped and advice staleness is the thing that will actually decide adoption.

Ivo

subject: Re: Kickoff: advice-based moment estimation — May status + advice-staleness risk
body:
Hi both,

Status: baselines reproduced on the public graph datasets. On a skewed temporal graph, advice-based sampling cuts second-moment estimation error to roughly a third of PPSWOR at the same sample budget, and perfect advice shows another ~2x of headroom beyond that — so the learned-advice quality is what everything hinges on.

Which brings the risk: staleness. Freya trained advice on week N of telemetry and evaluated on week N+1 vs N+4. At N+1 we keep ~85% of the error reduction; at N+4 we keep barely half, and on one traffic shift (a datacenter drain that reshuffled the heavy IP pairs) stale advice was briefly worse than plain ell_1 sampling. Advice-guided sampling concentrates the budget where the advice says mass is — when the world moves, it concentrates in the wrong place.

Plan: weekly advice refresh as the recommended operating mode, plus a fallback that blends in ell_1 sampling when observed frequencies diverge from advice. The June full-scale run will quantify the blend.

Umar

subject: Re: Kickoff: advice-based moment estimation — post-run decisions
body:
Team,

With last week's full-scale run in hand, decisions for the Jul 6 close:

1) Adoption recommendation is a yes, with Umar's blended mode as the default: advice-guided sampling with the ell_1 fallback engaging automatically on divergence. The full-scale numbers held up — error at one-third of the current pipeline's at equal budget, and the drain-event replay stayed safely above the plain-sampling floor with the blend on.
2) Weekly advice refresh is a hard operational requirement in the recommendation, with the N+4 staleness curve as the justification. Vera, please write the refresh runbook before rolling off — the telemetry on-call inherits this.
3) Scope cut: the unweighted_elements and weighted input types are documented but not productized; graph and net_traffic are what the customer runs.

Handoff review with the telemetry team is Jul 2. Thanks all — tidy project.

Anders

subject: Kickoff: Project Kestrel — MPI view extrapolation
body:
Hi Ivo,

Kicking off the view-extrapolation project (Apr 20 – Jun 29). Internally we're calling this effort Project Kestrel — please use the codename on invites and docs so search stays clean.

The asset is our CVPR open-source release: predict a multiplane image (MPI) from a narrow-baseline pair of RGB images, then render novel camera views from the predicted MPI. It builds on the Stereo Magnification training approach but pushes extrapolation well beyond the input baseline. The release includes a pretrained model and a render_sway.py path that makes for a killer demo.

Product story: the capture team wants parallax-rich "living photos" from dual-lens stills — no depth sensor, no multi-shot capture.

Milestones: mid-May — pretrained model reproduced, sway demo on our own captures; mid-June — retraining on internal capture data; Jun 29 — demo-readiness review (LRB sign-off needed before anything external).

Staffing and compute when you can.

Lucia

subject: Re: Kickoff: Project Kestrel — staffing + compute
body:
Hi Lucia,

Kestrel staffing: Rafael Duran 50% leads the modeling and retraining; Freya Ruiz 25% on evaluation (she's splitting with a swarm-search project this quarter); Maren Zhou 30% on the data pipeline for internal captures; Rosa Mensah 40% on the demo path and render performance.

Compute: reproduction runs on 32 titan-a100 GPUs best-effort. Retraining on internal captures in June needs 128 A100s for about two weeks — still best-effort tier, but I've asked Ines to flag us if the pool gets contended, since our window has no slack after Jun 15. All Kestrel experiment configs live under the kestrel/ namespace on the cluster.

One early observation from Rafael: the released checkpoint expects narrow-baseline stereo pairs with known camera intrinsics; the capture team's dual-lens rigs drift on calibration, so Maren's pipeline needs an intrinsics-refinement pass before training data is usable. That's in scope but it's the schedule risk to watch.

Ivo

subject: Re: Kickoff: Project Kestrel — status + extrapolation-range trade-off
body:
Hi both,

Status: the pretrained model is reproduced and Rosa's demo path renders the sway trajectory from our own dual-lens captures — it genuinely impresses in person. Maren's intrinsics-refinement pass works; calibration drift on the capture rigs is now correctable in preprocessing.

The trade-off we need a decision on: extrapolation range. Within ~4x the input baseline, renders are clean. The capture team's product spec asks for wider sweeps (~8x), and out there the MPI's fixed depth planes show their limits — we get visible stack-of-cards artifacts and edge smearing on foreground occluders in roughly a quarter of test scenes. Retraining on internal captures (starting next week on the 128-GPU allocation) should help texture realism but won't change the geometry limits; that's inherent to the plane parameterization.

Options for the Jun 29 review: (a) demo locked at 4x — reliably beautiful; (b) 8x with a scene-screening step. I lean (a).

Rafael

subject: Re: Kickoff: Project Kestrel — decision for the demo review
body:
Team,

Decision for next Monday's review: we go with Rafael's option (a). The Kestrel demo locks extrapolation at 4x baseline, and the capture team's 8x ask moves to an H2 investigation with the stack-of-cards artifact examples attached so nobody relitigates this from a slide.

Supporting decisions:
1) Retrained checkpoint (internal captures) is the demo model — Freya's eval shows it beats the released pretrained model on our capture distribution, especially on texture realism at the extrapolation edge.
2) Rosa's screening heuristic ships anyway as a capture-time warning — flagging deep-parallax scenes at capture is useful even at 4x.
3) Nadia — requesting LRB sign-off at the Jun 26 board for a partner-facing demo in July. Materials will be under the Kestrel name in the shared drive by Thursday.

Great half, everyone. This one demos itself.

Lucia

subject: Kickoff: muNet multitask evolution
body:
Hi Jelena,

Kicking off the muNet project (Mar 2 – May 11). The research line from our open-source release: muNet evolves a pretrained network into a scalable auto-tuning multitask system, and the follow-up mu2Net adds dynamic introduction of new tasks into a large-scale multitask system without retraining from scratch. The released notebooks reproduce all published experiments, so reproduction cost is low.

Why product cares: the retrieval org currently maintains 11 per-task fine-tuning forks of the same base model. Every fork is its own eval surface, serving artifact, and on-call burden. One evolving multitask system that absorbs a new task on demand collapses that mess.

Milestones: end of March — muNet reproduction from the notebooks, ported to our training stack; mid-April — mu2Net-style dynamic task addition demonstrated on 3 internal retrieval tasks; early May — cost/quality comparison vs the fork farm and a Q3 adoption proposal.

Staffing and dependencies by Mar 13?

Anders

subject: Re: Kickoff: muNet multitask evolution — staffing + dependencies
body:
Hi Anders,

Staffing: Yara Jokic 50% leads the method port and owns the evolution runs; Hyun Traore 30% (he's also on a pruning project this window) advising on the parameter-sharing and mutation mechanics; Milan Zapata 40% through May on porting the notebook code into our training stack — note he's spoken for by other teams from June, so anything serving-side that slips past our window loses him.

Compute: evolution is search-shaped, so it's many medium jobs rather than one big one — I've sized it at 64 titan-a100 GPUs best-effort sustained through April.

On the Corpus side we have breathing room: the v2 migration freeze is 2026-08-07, so the task-suite datasets can stay on v1 pipelines through our whole window and the v2 port is a leisurely June/July item after we close.

One honest flag: the mutation search can grow the parameter footprint per added task; Yara will track parameters-per-task as a first-class metric so the cost comparison vs the fork farm stays fair.

Jelena

subject: Re: Kickoff: muNet multitask evolution — April status + task-order risk
body:
Hi both,

Status: Milan finished the port — the muNet evolution loop runs on our stack, and reproduction matches the published notebook results on the benchmark suite. Dynamic task addition works: I introduced retrieval task 3 into a system already trained on tasks 1–2, mu2Net-style, and it reached fork-level quality using 41% fewer added parameters than a full fine-tuning fork.

The risk I want on the record: task-introduction order matters more than the papers emphasize at our scale. Adding the noisy click-feedback task before the clean relevance task degraded the shared components — average quality across all three tasks ended 1.3 points lower than the reverse order. With 11 tasks the ordering space is unsearchable, so the adoption proposal needs either a curriculum heuristic (clean-to-noisy seems to work) or an isolation guarantee for shared parameters.

Hyun suggests borrowing a freeze-then-branch policy from his pruning work; we'll test it next sprint.

Yara

subject: Re: Kickoff: muNet multitask evolution — closing decisions
body:
Team,

Decisions for the May 11 close:

1) The adoption proposal goes forward with a phased plan: migrate 4 of the 11 forks in Q3 using the clean-to-noisy curriculum heuristic, which held up in Yara's follow-up runs (freeze-then-branch also helped — thanks Hyun — and it's in the proposal as the isolation mechanism for the noisiest task).
2) Headline numbers for the proposal: fork-level quality at 41% fewer added parameters per task, and one serving artifact instead of four.
3) Scope cut: full 11-fork migration is explicitly not proposed for Q3. The ordering-sensitivity result means we earn trust four tasks at a time.
4) Milan's port is done and documented, so his roll-off at end of May is clean; serving integration lands with the platform team in Q3.

Proposal draft to this thread by Friday for review before I take it to Hana.

Anders

subject: Kickoff: mucped22 — IQA foundation for codec tuning
body:
Hi Bruno,

Kicking off the mucped22 project (Feb 9 – Jun 1). The premise from our open-source release: existing human-rated IQA databases — KADID-10k, TID2013, CSIQ, LIVE — are what everyone tunes objective metrics like MS-SSIM against, but they lean on crowdsourced raters without strong image-comparison experience and on distortions that don't resemble what real compression produces. Tuning a codec against a metric tuned against the wrong database is an extra error source nobody accounts for.

Product goal: make mucped22 the reference database for our codec team's tuning loop, and stand up our own expert-rater pipeline so we can extend it with new distortion types on demand.

Milestones: March — database ingested, metric-correlation baselines (MS-SSIM et al.) reproduced; April — rating pipeline operational with a pilot batch; May — first extension batch rated and a tuning-loop recommendation.

Staffing and tooling plan by end of Feb?

Lucia

subject: Re: Kickoff: mucped22 — staffing + tooling plan
body:
Hi Lucia,

Plan:

- Gustavo Moreau 50% owns ingestion and the metric-correlation baselines; Ondrej Bergstrom 40% designs the rating methodology (rater qualification, session length, pair sampling) so we don't recreate the crowdsourcing weaknesses the release critiques.
- Since nothing suitable exists in-house, we're building a human-rating annotation UI from scratch — Emeka Pinto owns it at 50% (pairwise comparison views, rater qualification flow, session quality checks), roughly seven weeks of work for a v1 we can run study batches through.
- Compute: negligible; this is a data and tooling project. Storage ask to Corpus for the image sets is in.

Budget note: expert raters aren't free — Ondrej estimates ~$18k for the April pilot batch at the session lengths he wants. I'd rather pay for experienced raters than re-import the exact problem this dataset exists to fix.

Bruno

subject: Re: Kickoff: mucped22 — April status + metric-divergence finding
body:
Hi both,

Status: database ingested and the correlation baselines are done. Emeka's annotation UI v1 is live — pairwise views, qualification flow, and per-session quality checks all working — and Ondrej's pilot batch ran last week with 9 qualified raters.

The finding that matters: on compression-typical distortions, metric rankings disagree with each other far more than the legacy-database correlations would predict. MS-SSIM and the perceptual metrics agree on the easy cases, but on the multi-bitrate ladders they invert ordering on about 1 in 6 image pairs — and the pilot's human judgments side with different metrics in different distortion regimes. That's exactly the release's thesis: a metric tuned on KADID-style distortions is not trustworthy for codec tuning.

Risk/trade-off: the codec team wants a single blessed metric by May. The honest answer may be "metric X within this bitrate range, human eval outside it." Less convenient, more true.

Gustavo

subject: Re: Kickoff: mucped22 — decisions for the June close
body:
Team,

Decisions from the review:

1) We adopt the regime-scoped recommendation, exactly as Gustavo framed it: a blessed metric per bitrate regime, with mandatory human eval (through our pipeline) for cross-regime codec comparisons. The codec team pushed back on losing a single number; the 1-in-6 ordering-inversion stat ended that conversation.
2) The May extension batch is funded — same 9-rater pool, $21k, Idris signed off. Ondrej's methodology doc becomes the standard for any future rating study in the vision portfolio.
3) Emeka's annotation UI graduates from project tooling to a maintained internal tool; he'll spend 20% in June on hardening and docs.

One miss to own: we're landing three weeks later than the original April pipeline milestone. Fully worth it for rater quality, but I'll note it in the portfolio review.

Lucia

subject: Kickoff: Project Vantage — JPEG encoder evaluation (mucped23)
body:
Hi Ivo,

Kicking off the mucped23 work (Apr 13 – Jul 27). We're running this internally under the codename Project Vantage — use it in doc titles and the chat channel (#proj-vantage) so the encoder vendors don't show up in search.

The asset: our open-source mucped23 IQA database — human perceptual evaluations of images compressed with MozJPEG, libjpeg-turbo, and the jpegli encoder, built on 49 512x512 source images drawn from the CID22 validation set. jpegli applies insights from the butteraugli and JPEG XL lines to squeeze more quality-per-byte out of plain JPEG, which every image-heavy surface we run still serves.

Product question, plainly: do we switch our serving stack's encoder, and at which quality settings? Serving costs say yes if perception says tie.

Milestones: mid-May — dataset + eval harness internalized; late June — encoder bake-off on our own image corpus; mid-July — recommendation to the serving org.

Staffing and compute by May 1?

Lucia

subject: Re: Kickoff: Project Vantage — staffing + compute
body:
Hi Lucia,

Vantage staffing: Yusuf Keita 40% leads the perceptual analysis and owns the recommendation methodology; Bilal Novak 50% builds the Vantage eval harness (encoder wrappers for MozJPEG, libjpeg-turbo, jpegli; bitrate-ladder generation; metric computation); Oyin Iversen 25% on corpus sampling from our serving logs so the bake-off images match what we actually serve, not just the CID22-derived set.

Compute: tiny by portfolio standards — encoding sweeps and metric computation on 8 titan-a100 GPUs best-effort, mostly CPU anyway.

Budget flag: if we want a human-rated confirmation batch on our own corpus (Yusuf strongly recommends it — the mucped23 ratings cover the public sources, not our distribution), that's an external rater spend, ballpark $12k. I'll bring the exact number to the Vantage weekly sync.

One process note: encoder licensing review for jpegli redistribution is with Kofi, 2–3 week SLA, started today so it doesn't gate the July recommendation.

Ivo

subject: Re: Kickoff: Project Vantage — bake-off status + a distribution risk
body:
Hi both,

Status: Bilal's harness is done and the first bake-off pass ran over the weekend — full bitrate ladders for all three encoders across the mucped23 sources plus Oyin's 2,400-image serving sample. Directionally the public-data result holds on our corpus: at matched perceptual quality, jpegli comes in around 12–14% smaller than MozJPEG in the mid-quality range where most of our traffic sits, and libjpeg-turbo trails both on quality-per-byte (as expected — it optimizes for speed).

The risk: our serving sample is much heavier on text-in-image and UI screenshots than the CID22-style photographic sources, and on that slice the jpegli advantage shrinks to ~5% with occasional ringing around high-contrast text that the metrics under-penalize. This is exactly the distribution-mismatch trap mucped23 warns about with legacy IQA databases, just one level up.

Recommendation: spend the $12k on the human confirmation batch, weighted toward the text-heavy slice. Without it I can't sign a switch recommendation for all traffic.

Yusuf

subject: Re: Kickoff: Project Vantage — final recommendation
body:
Team,

The human confirmation batch came back Thursday, so locking decisions for the Jul 27 close:

1) Recommendation to serving: switch photographic traffic to jpegli — raters confirmed the metric story, and 12–14% at matched quality is real money at our volume. Zeke, the handoff doc is in the Vantage drive folder.
2) Text-heavy and UI-screenshot traffic stays on MozJPEG for now. Raters penalized the text ringing harder than any metric did, which validates Yusuf's caution; a tuned jpegli config for that slice is the natural Q4 follow-up.
3) Kofi's licensing review cleared with no redistribution concerns for our serving use.
4) The Vantage eval harness and the routing-by-content-type criteria transfer to Zeke's team as maintained artifacts.

That's a clean, defensible split recommendation. Thanks all — especially for insisting on the confirmation batch.

Lucia

subject: Kickoff: MULLER learned resizer for retrieval pipelines
body:
Hi Deshawn,

Kicking off MULLER (Mar 23 – Jun 1) — a short, sharp one. The asset is our ICCV 2023 open-source release: a multilayer Laplacian resizer, a learned resizing layer with a handful of parameters that sharpens the band-pass detail that downstream vision models actually use. Because it's so small it drops into existing preprocessing with effectively zero serving-cost delta, and the released demo notebook shows the integration in a few lines.

Product case: the retrieval org's image towers all downsample with fixed bilinear resize today. If swapping in MULLER buys even a fraction of a point of retrieval precision at zero serving cost, it's the cheapest quality win on the roadmap.

Milestones: mid-April — resizer integrated into one tower's input path, offline A/B on the retrieval eval set; mid-May — retraining sweep across the three main towers; Jun 1 — ship/no-ship recommendation.

Staffing and the compute/budget ask by Apr 10?

Anders

subject: Re: Kickoff: MULLER learned resizer — staffing + budget
body:
Hi Anders,

Staffing: Yara Jokic 30% leads the integration and the offline A/B (she's also carrying the muNet close this spring, hence the modest slice); Oyin Iversen 30% on the preprocessing plumbing and serving parity checks; Hyun Traore 20% consulting on the training-side interactions, since a learned resizer changes what the towers see during fine-tuning.

Funding is settled: Idris verbally earmarked $120k from the Q3 discretionary compute budget line B-77 for this project, which covers the retraining sweeps for the retrieval towers with MULLER in the input path. The April single-tower work fits in our existing best-effort allocation (24 titan-a100 GPUs); the May sweep is what the earmark actually pays for.

One caution so we don't oversell: MULLER's wins in the paper come when the downstream model is trained (or at least fine-tuned) with the resizer in the loop. A pure drop-in with frozen towers may show nothing — that's precisely what Yara's April A/B will settle before we spend the sweep money.

Deshawn

subject: Re: Kickoff: MULLER learned resizer — A/B results + sweep status
body:
Hi both,

Results from the April A/B, and Deshawn's caution was exactly right: pure drop-in on the frozen tower moved retrieval precision@10 by +0.05, statistically indistinguishable from zero. With a light fine-tune (2 epochs, resizer in the loop), tower 1 gains +0.42 precision@10 and +0.31 recall@50 on the offline eval — consistent with the paper's claim that the multilayer Laplacian filtering sharpens detail the model learns to exploit. Latency delta in Oyin's serving parity check: under 0.3 ms per image, effectively free as promised.

The May sweep across all three towers is running on the B-77-funded allocation; towers 2 and 3 finish this week. One trade-off to flag for the Jun 1 recommendation: the fine-tune requirement means MULLER rides along with each tower's regular retraining cadence rather than shipping instantly — tower 3 doesn't retrain until July, so full rollout completes next quarter regardless of our decision.

Yara

subject: Kickoff: multi-annotator disagreement modeling for Corpus labeling
body:
Hi Daniela,

Kicking off the multi-annotator effort formally. Goal: bring the approach from our open-source release (train on every annotator's label instead of the majority vote) into the Corpus labeling pipeline for hate-speech detection, so downstream teams see disagreement rather than a fake single ground truth.

Scope for this half: (1) adapt the data format — N annotator columns named 0 to N-1 plus a text column, values 0/1/NaN — to Corpus export schemas; (2) extend preprocess.py beyond the two datasets it currently reformats; (3) a pilot eval against the majority-vote baseline.

Milestones I want to socialize at the next Launch Review Board: format validator by 04-03, pilot model trained by 04-24, integration readout before 05-25. If we land the pilot, this becomes the Q3 OKR anchor for data-platforms.

Can you confirm staffing this week?

Thanks,
Dmitri

subject: Re: Kickoff: multi-annotator disagreement modeling for Corpus labeling
body:
Dmitri,

Staffing confirmed: Csilla leads modeling, Emeka owns the Corpus export adapter, Maren and Tereza split preprocessing and the validator. That covers the 04-03 milestone.

On compute and money: pilot training fits on titan-a100 best-effort, but the annotator-pool scaling runs (we want to sweep pools of 20 to 80 annotators) won't. Good news there — Idris verbally earmarked the full $120k from Q3 discretionary compute budget line B-13 for this project, so the scaling sweep is covered without touching the portfolio baseline. I'd still like it in writing before Q3 OKRs lock on 06-26, but he was unambiguous on the call.

One constraint: current code is binary-only. If Corpus wants multi-class toxicity tiers, that's a head refactor we have not scoped.

Daniela

subject: Pilot results: per-annotator heads vs majority vote
body:
Hi both,

Pilot is trained, two days ahead of the 04-24 milestone. Numbers on the held-out Corpus hate-speech slice:

- Majority-vote baseline: F1 0.66
- Multi-annotator model (one head per annotator, NaN-masked where an annotator skipped an item): F1 0.71 when we aggregate heads, and we additionally get per-item disagreement scores for free.

The NaN masking matters — in our pilot pool each item is only annotated by 2 of 4 annotators, exactly the sparse pattern the release code expects.

Risk to flag: disagreement scores are well calibrated on political-speech items but noisy on slang-heavy ones, where annotator pools are small. Maren is pulling more annotations for those slices via Corpus before we call it robust. Also re-confirming: binary labels only for now.

Csilla

subject: Re: Pilot results: per-annotator heads vs majority vote — decision
body:
Team,

Decision from yesterday's review, writing it down so we're aligned:

1. We ship the binary multi-annotator model to the Corpus labeling pipeline as an advisory signal (disagreement score alongside the existing label). Integration readout stays 05-25.
2. Multi-class toxicity tiers are explicitly cut from this half. The head refactor is real work and I'm not trading the integration date for it. It goes on the Q3 candidate list.
3. Slang-heavy slices ship flagged as low-confidence until Maren's additional annotations land.

The 0.71 vs 0.66 F1 delta plus the disagreement signal is a good story for the Launch Review Board — Nadia has us on the 05-21 agenda.

Nice work getting here ahead of milestone.

Dmitri

subject: MGDT kickoff — generalist agent checkpoint for H1
body:
Hi Jelena,

Kickoff note for the Multi-Game Decision Transformer push. The pitch upstairs: one transformer, one set of weights, trained purely offline, playing 46 Atari games at close-to-human level — and, more importantly for us, fine-tuning rapidly to new games. That fine-tuning story is the product: a generalist checkpoint plus a recipe agents-rl can hand to any team with an offline interaction log.

Milestones inside our window (03-02 to 06-22): offline data pipeline validated by 04-10, medium-scale training done by mid-May, then a large scaling run in early June so we have the model-size scaling curve for the H1 readout. The colab-style eval loader from the open-source release is our starting point for the eval harness.

Jelena — can you sketch the compute ask this month? The June run is the long pole.

Ulla

subject: Re: MGDT kickoff — compute plan locked
body:
Ulla,

Compute plan for the long pole is locked. We hold the vulcan-h100 reservation — 256 accelerators for the week of 2026-06-01 — for the large scaling run. Ines's reservation process went smoothly; that week gives us enough to train the biggest config and still replicate the two smaller points on the scaling curve. Everything before that (data pipeline shakeout, medium-scale training in May) fits on titan-a100 best-effort.

Staffing: Vera owns the offline Atari dataset ingest, Wanjiru the training infra, Yara evals and the fine-tuning recipe. No additional headcount ask this half.

One dependency to note: we want Evalline to host the per-game human-normalized scores, and Tomas's team quoted a 2-week integration. I've asked Yara to file that this week so it doesn't collide with the June run.

Jelena

subject: Re: MGDT kickoff — April status + a data loader risk
body:
Hi both,

Status: offline dataset ingest is done for 41 of 46 games; the last five have replay logs with a schema quirk I'm normalizing this week. Medium-scale training started Monday and the early curve looks healthy — we're tracking the offline-RL vs behavioral-cloning comparison from the paper and, as expected, the decision-transformer objective is the most stable of the three at this scale.

Yara's first fine-tuning probe: adapting the medium checkpoint to a held-out game with ~1% of its data recovers 78% of the single-game specialist's score. Encouraging for the recipe pitch.

Risk: loader throughput. At the June config the current pipeline feeds about 60% of what 256 accelerators will eat. Wanjiru is sharding the trajectory decode; if we don't hit 95%+ utilization in the May dress rehearsal, the scaling run needs either more days or fewer ablations.

Vera

subject: Re: MGDT kickoff — decision ahead of the June run
body:
Team,

Decision from this morning's pre-run review. The dress rehearsal got the loader to 91% utilization — good but not the 95% bar. Rather than gamble the reserved week, we're cutting scope:

1. The June run trains the large config plus ONE replication of the mid point. The online-RL comparison arm is dropped; the open-source paper already establishes that offline decision transformers scale better, and we don't need to re-prove it on our dime.
2. Yara's fine-tuning recipe ships with the medium checkpoint first; the large-checkpoint version follows after the run.

That keeps us comfortably inside the week and protects the scaling-curve deliverable for the H1 readout on 06-18. Wanjiru, please freeze the loader config by Friday.

Thanks all — tight but doable.

Ulla

subject: Kickoff: abbreviation-aware normalization from the survey release
body:
Hi Bao,

Kicking off the abbreviation project. We're building on our open-source survey release: survey.tsv has consultant-level responses across 19 columns per locale — whether a locale has first-character abbreviations (NATO-style), stump compounds (FiDi < Financial District), truncations (Col. < Colonel), augmented truncations (footie < football), word-internal deletions (Blvd.), plus examples for each. Locale codes like ru, ja, pt-br.

Product goal: an abbreviation-aware text normalization model for the language portfolio's keyboard and TTS pipelines — expand or preserve abbreviations per locale conventions instead of today's one-size-fits-all rules.

Rough milestones: survey-to-features pipeline by mid-April, per-locale rule baselines by end of May, multilingual model trained in early July, readout before 07-20. Compute ask comes from your side once the model config settles.

Priya

subject: Re: Kickoff: abbreviation-aware normalization — resourcing
body:
Priya,

Resourcing summary for the half:

Staffing — Nikhil on the survey-to-features pipeline, Paloma on data tooling, Efe on the rule baselines, Umar leading the multilingual model. All four hold through July.

Compute — the rule baselines are CPU-only. For the multilingual normalization model we're doing one big consolidated sweep rather than dribbling runs out: we hold the vulcan-h100 reservation, 256 accelerators, for the week of 2026-07-06, which covers the full training sweep across locale groupings plus the ablations Umar wants (script-family transfer, with/without stump-compound features). Reservation is squared away with the infra process, so the only date risk on the run itself is our own data readiness.

Ask: can you confirm the target locale list by 04-24? The sweep config keys off it.

Bao

subject: Re: Kickoff: abbreviation-aware normalization — May status + coverage risk
body:
Hi both,

Status: pipeline milestone hit. survey.tsv parses cleanly into per-locale feature vectors; we track consultant proficiency (column 3) as a confidence weight, which noticeably de-noises the rule baselines.

Efe's baselines cover 27 locales so far. Truncations and first-character abbreviations are well-attested nearly everywhere; the thin spots are augmented truncations and word-internal deletions, where several locales have a Yes flag but only one or two consultant examples to learn from.

Risk: for roughly 8 of the 27 locales we have a single consultant response. Fine-grained rules learned from one person's examples will overfit — Umar suggests grouping those locales by script family in the July sweep rather than giving them dedicated heads. Costs some per-locale precision, protects generalization.

Locale list from Priya received, sweep config is keyed to it.

Nikhil

subject: Re: Kickoff: abbreviation-aware normalization — decision on locale scope
body:
Team,

Decision, confirmed at yesterday's checkpoint just under the Q3 OKR lock:

1. The July training sweep targets 12 dedicated high-priority locales; the remaining single-consultant locales get script-family grouped heads per Umar's proposal. We are not shipping per-locale rules learned from one consultant's examples.
2. TTS integration is the launch surface for Q3; keyboard follows in Q4. Nadia has pencilled us for the Launch Review Board on 07-16, so the sweep output needs eval numbers by 07-13.
3. Paloma to prep the sweep data drops the week before the run so we walk in with everything staged.

Q3 OKR is filed as: normalization model beating rule baselines on 12 locales, measured on Evalline.

Thanks all,
Priya

subject: MultimodalChat kickoff — photo suggestion in conversation
body:
Hi Alina,

Kickoff for MultimodalChat. Base asset is the PhotoChat dataset from our open-source release: dialogues where every turn carries a share_photo boolean and user_id, plus a photo_description with object labels and the photo's Open Image ID. That gives us two trainable tasks out of the box — (1) predict the turn where a photo share is appropriate, (2) retrieve the right photo given dialogue context.

Product framing: rich-content suggestion (photos/GIFs/stickers) inside the language portfolio's chat surfaces. The share-intent trigger is the differentiator; retrieval alone is table stakes.

Milestones: Open Image data pulled and indexed by mid-May, intent + retrieval baselines by end of June, end-to-end demo for Launch Review Board in late July. Window closes 08-03 so there's not much slack after that demo.

Staffing plan from you when ready?

Priya

subject: Re: MultimodalChat kickoff — staffing plan
body:
Priya,

Staffing plan for the half:

- Yara: share-intent model (lead)
- Hyun + Carmen: retrieval model and dialogue-context encoder
- Efe: eval design, including the human-judged relevance pass
- Amara Okafor: image retrieval index and serving path — I have her committed at 60% to MultimodalChat for June 2026, which is what the index build plus the Shipyard integration needs. She drops to 30% in July once the index is in maintenance mode.

Compute is modest; titan-a100 best-effort covers both model families. The Shipyard demo slot for late July is requested with Zeke's team — they want the serving config three weeks ahead, so Amara's June allocation is genuinely the critical path here.

One flag: Open Image download via the external mirror is slower than expected; Amara is parallelizing the pull.

Alina

subject: Re: MultimodalChat kickoff — June status, one label-noise risk
body:
Hi both,

Status ahead of the end-of-June baseline milestone:

- Share-intent model: F1 0.58 on predicting the share_photo turn, vs 0.41 for a recency heuristic. Turns where share_photo is true have empty message text, which makes the supervision clean.
- Retrieval: Hyun and Carmen's dual-encoder hits Recall@1 of 0.34 / Recall@5 of 0.62 against the ~10k photo pool. Index and serving path are up (thanks Amara — June crunch is paying off).

Risk: photo_description quality. The object labels are coarse ("dog, grass, frisbee"), and Efe's first human-judged pass shows ~15% of top-1 retrievals are label-matched but contextually wrong. Options: enrich descriptions with a captioner before indexing (Amara estimates 1 week of index rebuild), or accept and message it as v1 quality. We need a call by 06-26 to hold the demo date.

Yara

subject: M-RL kickoff: making Munchausen agents our value-based baseline suite
body:
Hi Ivo,

Kickoff for the Munchausen RL effort. Context: our open-source M-RL release ships two agents on top of Dopamine — M-DQN and M-IQN — plus an Advantage Learning implementation used for ablations. Teams keep re-running these ad hoc; the product here is a maintained, reproducible value-based baseline suite for the whole agents-rl portfolio, with pinned configs (the atari.gin path) and published reference curves.

Milestones inside the window (02-16 to 05-25): repo hygiene and the train.py entry point wrapped for our infra by mid-March, full Atari sweep for M-DQN by end of April, M-IQN plus the AL ablation by mid-May, reference curves on Evalline before close.

Biggest known wart: the release is TensorFlow v1, no eager mode. Want your read on whether we port or contain.

Ulla

subject: Re: M-RL kickoff — resourcing and the TF1 question
body:
Ulla,

Resourcing:

Staffing — Quentin leads the sweeps, Yara owns eval/reference curves, Rosa the infra wrapping, Farah the config pinning. Comfortable with that against your milestones.

Compute — the Atari-57 sweeps (3 seeds x 57 games x 3 agent types) don't fit our standing titan-a100 share. On budget: Idris verbally earmarked $120k from Q3 discretionary compute budget line B-44 for this project, which covers the full sweep plan with headroom for re-runs. I'll treat that as committed for planning; getting it papered before Q3 OKRs lock is on my list.

On TF1: recommendation is contain, not port. We pin the environment, run it as-is (no eager mode means our standard profiling hooks don't attach, we accept that), and revisit a port only if the suite becomes load-bearing beyond this half.

Ivo

subject: Re: M-RL kickoff — sweep status + replay checkpoint risk
body:
Hi both,

Sweep status: M-DQN Atari run is ~70% through the 57 games. Curves reproduce the release's story so far — M-DQN outperforms our pinned DQN baseline on 39 of the 41 games completed, and on Pong the m_dqn agent trained via the train.py path matches the reference within noise. The al_dqn ablation runs are queued behind it as planned.

Two issues:

1. Replay-buffer checkpointing under the TF1 graph runner occasionally corrupts on preemption; Rosa added an atomic-rename guard, no losses since 04-06, but we burned about 4 days of re-runs. The re-run headroom in the budget is earning its keep.

2. M-IQN is ~1.6x slower per step than M-DQN on our A100s (quantile head overhead), so the mid-May M-IQN milestone is tight. Options: 2 seeds instead of 3 for M-IQN, or slip a week. Preference?

Quentin

subject: Re: M-RL kickoff — closing decisions
body:
Team,

Closing decisions for the half:

1. M-IQN ships with 2 seeds, not 3. The suite's job is to be a dependable baseline, and a week's slip past 05-25 costs us the Evalline publication slot. We annotate the seed count on the reference curves so nobody misreads the variance.
2. TF1 stays contained per Ivo's March call. A TF2/JAX port is formally out of scope for this half — I've written it into the Q3 candidate list instead, where it can compete on merit.
3. Yara publishes M-DQN reference curves (full 57 games, 3 seeds) plus the al_dqn ablation to Evalline by 05-20; M-IQN follows by 05-25.

Quentin — the 39-of-41 result is exactly the reproduction story I wanted for the readout. Nice.

Ulla

subject: MUSIQ kickoff — IQA scoring API + quality leaderboard
body:
Hi Deshawn,

Kicking off the MUSIQ productization. We're starting from a strong place: the open-source release ships inference code and checkpoints trained on four datasets (ava_ckpt, koniq_ckpt, paq2piq_ckpt, spaq_ckpt), with the default model taking 3-scale input — native resolution plus 224 and 384. No training needed for v1; this is a packaging and serving play.

Two deliverables this quarter:
1. An internal image-quality scoring API on Shipyard, MUSIQ under the hood, for the vision portfolio's data-filtering pipelines.
2. A benchmark leaderboard service so quality models get tracked over time instead of living in one-off spreadsheets.

Milestones: serving prototype by 05-15, leaderboard MVP by mid-June, Launch Review Board readout before 07-13. Resourcing proposal from you next, please — especially who builds the leaderboard.

Lucia

subject: Re: MUSIQ kickoff — resourcing, incl. leaderboard build
body:
Lucia,

Resourcing proposal:

- Scoring API: Nikhil packages the run_predict_image path for Shipyard; Wei owns model validation against the published numbers. ~3 weeks to the 05-15 prototype.
- Benchmark leaderboard service: we're scoping and building this from scratch — there's nothing on the shelf internally that does per-dataset tracking with score history. Katya and Gustavo are staffed on it at 50% each for a 6-week build: submission API, per-dataset boards (KonIQ, SPAQ, AVA to start), score history, and an Evalline hook so runs report in automatically. MVP lands mid-June per your milestone.

Compute is negligible — inference-only, a few titan-a100 nodes.

One ask back: for the leaderboard's v1 metric set I want to lock SRCC and PLCC per dataset and nothing else. Metric creep is how these things die.

Deshawn

subject: Re: MUSIQ kickoff — validation status + latency trade-off
body:
Hi both,

Status: scoring API prototype landed 05-14, a day early. Validation looks good — the koniq_ckpt reproduces SRCC 0.916 on our KonIQ holdout, and spaq_ckpt is within 0.004 of the published correlation. Checkpoint loading from the release's .npz format was uneventful.

Trade-off we need a decision on: the default 3-scale model (native + 224 + 384) runs ~140 ms per image on an A100, dominated by the native-resolution scale on large photos. The MUSIQ-single variant (native resolution only, the full_size_single_scale checkpoint) runs ~55 ms with SRCC dropping about 0.01 on KonIQ. For the data-filtering pipelines, which score millions of images, I'd offer both: default endpoint = single-scale, opt-in flag for full 3-scale.

Leaderboard: Katya reports the submission API and KonIQ board working end to end; SPAQ and AVA boards next sprint.

Wei

subject: Re: MUSIQ kickoff — decisions for launch review
body:
Team,

Decisions locked today, in time for the Q3 OKR cutoff:

1. Serving: Wei's proposal adopted. Single-scale is the default endpoint at ~55 ms; 3-scale behind a flag for callers who need the last 0.01 SRCC. Nikhil to document the trade-off in the API spec.
2. Leaderboard MVP scope: it slipped a week (mid-June became 06-22), so we freeze v1 at the three boards — KonIQ, SPAQ, AVA — with SRCC/PLCC only, per Deshawn's metric lock. The PaQ2PiQ board and any custom-dataset support move to Q3.
3. Launch Review Board readout confirmed for 07-09 with Nadia; both the API and the leaderboard demo on the agenda.

Q3 OKR filed: leaderboard adopted by 3+ vision teams, API scoring >5M images/week.

Good half, team.

Lucia

subject: Kickoff: MI-maximization study → objective guidance for retrieval encoders
body:
Hi Daniela,

Kickoff for the MI representation-learning effort. Our open-source companion study showed that mutual information maximization alone doesn't explain representation quality — estimator and architecture choices dominate. Teams across graphs-retrieval still pick contrastive objectives by folklore. The deliverable: replicate the study at scale, extend it to our retrieval-encoder setups, and publish an opinionated internal guide ("use this objective/estimator for this data regime") backed by numbers.

Plan: the original suite ran at batch size 128 averaged over 20 runs — a single run takes ~2 hours, so the notebook path is fine for smoke tests, but the full 20-run replication plus our retrieval extensions needs a standalone job on real accelerators. Milestones: harness stood up by end of April, replication done by mid-June, guide published before window close 06-22.

Compute plan from your side when ready.

Anders

subject: Re: Kickoff: MI-maximization study — compute + staffing
body:
Anders,

Compute and staffing:

Staffing — Halima leads the replication and the estimator comparisons, Nikhil the retrieval-encoder extension, Chiara converts the Colab suite into a standalone runner (the RUN_EXPERIMENTS path is not built for 20-run batches, as the release itself warns).

Compute — smoke tests fit anywhere. For the full matrix (20 runs x estimator x architecture grid, plus the retrieval extension) we hold the cirrus-tpu reservation, 256 accelerators, for the week of 2026-06-08 out of the portfolio's quarterly allocation. That single week covers the entire consolidated batch, which is why I want everything staged and dress-rehearsed by 06-01 — if we miss the week, there is no second cirrus window before your 06-22 close.

Risk noted accordingly: the schedule has one hard pivot point and it's that week.

Daniela

subject: Re: Kickoff: MI-maximization study — pre-run status
body:
Hi both,

Status ahead of the June window:

- Chiara's standalone runner is done; a 5-run smoke batch at batch size 128 reproduces the precomputed Colab results within run-to-run noise. Dress rehearsal for the full 20-run protocol is scheduled 06-01, per Daniela's gate.
- Early signal from the smoke runs matches the study's headline: the estimator with the loosest MI bound is producing the best downstream linear-eval accuracy on two of three configs — another data point that tighter MI estimates don't buy better representations. This will lead the internal guide.
- Nikhil's retrieval extension: dual-encoder configs are written; recall@10 on the internal graph-retrieval benchmark is the extension's headline metric.

Risk: the runner's checkpoint restore adds ~9 min per run. Over the full matrix that's ~30 hours of the reserved week. Chiara has a fix in review; if it misses 06-01 we trim the architecture grid by one column.

Halima

subject: MuZero hardening — kickoff
body:
Hi Ivo,

Kickoff for the MuZero hardening effort. Our open-source implementation of the MuZero pseudocode runs on SEED RL and ships two environments — tictactoe and atari — plus a muzero agent that plugs into the standard seed_rl scripts. Today it's research-grade; several teams want planning-with-a-learned-model as a capability but nobody trusts the current state of the harness for anything load-bearing.

Goal for the half: a supported MuZero that (1) passes a deterministic tictactoe convergence test in CI, (2) trains distributed on the atari environment with published reference configs, (3) documents the learned-model planning knobs (simulations per move, unroll depth) so users don't cargo-cult them.

Milestones: CI gate by 03-06, single-machine atari validation by early April, distributed run and readout by 05-18.

Staffing and compute from you, please.

Ulla

subject: Re: MuZero hardening — staffing + compute
body:
Ulla,

Plan:

Staffing — Rafael owns agent correctness and the planning-knob documentation; Paloma owns the SEED RL infra path (learner/actor split, preemption recovery); Rosa takes the CI convergence gate and reference configs. That's a lean three, but the scope is hardening, not research.

Compute — single-machine work runs on titan-a100 best-effort. The April distributed atari validation needs about 64 A100s for two weeks; I've sized that within our standing agents-rl share, no special reservation needed. We deliberately stay off vulcan for this one.

Sequencing note: SEED's actor fan-out is where I expect the bodies to be buried — the pseudocode-faithful agent plus a few hundred actors has queue-depth interactions the release never had to care about. Paloma starts there next week.

CI gate on track for 03-06.

Ivo

subject: Re: MuZero hardening — April status
body:
Hi both,

Status:

- CI gate landed 03-05: tictactoe converges to perfect play in under 40 min on a fixed seed, and the test fails loudly if the learned-model rollout diverges from the reference trajectories. Already caught one regression from a dependency bump.
- Single-machine atari validation done on 3 games. Interesting knob finding for the docs: cutting simulations per move from 50 to 24 loses almost nothing on Pong but is a big hit on Ms. Pacman — planning depth matters most where the reward is sparse and delayed. Writing that up properly.
- Distributed: Paloma's fan-out work found exactly what Ivo predicted — at 300+ actors the inference batcher starves the learner. Her fix (double-buffered batching) gets learner utilization from 61% to 88%. One preemption-recovery bug remains; replay contents survive but priorities reset, which skews sampling for ~1h after restart.

On track for the May distributed run.

Rafael

subject: Re: MuZero hardening — close-out plan and June staffing
body:
Ulla, Rafael,

Close-out plan for the 05-18 readout, plus staffing decisions for what comes next:

1. The distributed run starts Monday with the double-buffered batcher. The priority-reset bug is documented as a known issue rather than fixed this half — it self-corrects within an hour and doesn't change end scores measurably.
2. Post-readout, the follow-on hardening phase (priority-reset fix, preemption soak tests, and the Go/Chess-style board-game env users keep asking for) is staffed now so we don't lose momentum: Paloma Castillo is committed at 60% to MuZero for June 2026, with Rosa picking up her CI duties. Rafael stays advisory at 20%.
3. Rosa publishes the reference configs and Rafael's planning-knob guide alongside the readout.

Ulla — flagging item 2 for your headcount tracking; it's the whole June plan for this workstream.

Ivo

subject: Negative cache kickoff — cheaper dual-encoder training for retrieval
body:
Hi Deshawn,

Kickoff for the negative-cache adoption. Our NeurIPS 2021 open-source release implements a streaming negative cache for dual-encoder training: at each step you sample a negative from a large cache to approximate the cross-entropy loss, instead of paying for in-batch or brute-force negatives. Memory-efficient, simple API (CacheManager + CacheClassificationLoss + a handler).

Why now: retrieval training is the biggest single line in our portfolio's compute spend, and the release's approach should cut effective negative-mining cost substantially at equal quality.

Deliverables: (1) integrate the cache loss into our standard dual-encoder trainer, (2) head-to-head at production scale vs our current negative sampling on the two flagship retrieval benchmarks, (3) adoption guide. Milestones: integration by end of March, mid-scale comparison in May, production-scale run in June, readout by 06-29.

Resourcing from you please — the June run will need a real reservation.

Anders

subject: Re: Negative cache kickoff — resourcing
body:
Anders,

Resourcing:

Staffing — Freya leads modeling and the comparison design; Yusuf owns the benchmark evals; Chiara and Oyin do the trainer integration (the CacheLossHandler slots into our trainer cleanly; Oyin's prototype already runs with cache_size 131072 and top_k 64 per the release defaults).

Compute — mid-scale May comparison fits in our titan-a100 share. For the June production-scale head-to-head we hold the vulcan-h100 reservation, 256 accelerators, for the week of 2026-06-15 — that covers both arms (cache-based and current sampler) at full corpus size, run side by side so the comparison is apples-to-apples on hardware. Ines's process was painless for once.

Budget-wise this stays inside portfolio baseline; no discretionary ask.

One heads-up: embedding staleness in the cache is the known failure mode at scale. Freya wants a refresh-rate ablation in the May round so June isn't a surprise.

Deshawn

subject: Re: Negative cache kickoff — mid-scale results
body:
Hi both,

Mid-scale comparison is done. Summary:

- Quality: cache-based training matches our current negative sampler on benchmark A (recall@10 0.842 vs 0.845, inside noise) and beats it on benchmark B (+1.9 points recall@10). The score_transform scaling (20x, per the release) mattered — without it the cache loss underweights hard negatives early in training.
- Cost: 38% less accelerator time to reach the quality plateau. That's the headline for the adoption guide.
- Staleness ablation: quality is flat until cache embeddings are ~4k steps stale, then degrades quickly. Our June config refreshes well inside that, so I'm comfortable.

Risk for June: the current sampler arm at full corpus size needs the brute-force miner, which is memory-hungry on H100s — Oyin is validating it fits at 256 accelerators alongside the cache arm's schedule. If it doesn't, we stagger the arms within the week rather than shrink the corpus.

Freya

subject: Re: Negative cache kickoff — decision + readout plan
body:
Team,

With the production-scale numbers in from last week's run, decisions ahead of Friday's Q3 OKR lock:

1. We adopt the negative cache as the default negative-mining path for new dual-encoder training in graphs-retrieval, starting Q3. Final numbers: quality parity on benchmark A, +1.6 recall@10 on benchmark B at full corpus, 35% accelerator-time saving — slightly below the mid-scale 38% because the staggered brute-force arm ate some of the week, but the story holds.
2. Existing production retrievers migrate opportunistically at their next scheduled retrain, not on a forced schedule. Chiara's adoption guide plus Oyin's trainer config are the migration kit.
3. Q3 OKR filed as: 3 production retrievers migrated, portfolio retrieval-training spend down 25%.

Readout to Hana's staff on 06-29, closing out the window on time. Thanks all — this one delivered exactly what it said on the tin.

Anders

subject: NAM kickoff — interpretable models for regulated customers
body:
Hi Jelena,

Kickoff for the Neural Additive Models effort. The open-source release gives us a tf.keras NAM model that drops into any training procedure, plus helpers for classification/regression graphs and a nam_train.py example script. The pitch: data-platforms customers in regulated domains keep asking for models where every feature's contribution is inspectable — NAMs give near-DNN accuracy with per-feature shape functions you can literally plot.

Deliverables this half: (1) a supported internal library wrapping the release, (2) tuned defaults per dataset family, which means large hyperparameter sweeps over the paper's benchmark suite (public sets live in the gs://nam_datasets/data bucket), (3) one lighthouse customer integration.

Note: the MIMIC-II medical benchmark needs a signed data use agreement — I've looped Kofi separately so Privacy Review starts now given their 2-3 week SLA.

Milestones: library alpha end of March, sweeps in June, customer readout by 07-06.

Dmitri

subject: Re: NAM kickoff — resourcing + June sweep reservation
body:
Dmitri,

Resourcing:

Staffing — Wanjiru leads the library work, Jorge the sweep harness, Oyin the customer integration path. The run.sh test script from the release is already wired into our CI as a sanity gate.

Compute — the per-dataset-family sweeps are wide (feature-net depth/width, dropout, feature-sparsity regularizer, output penalty... crossed with ~10 datasets and 20 splits each). Individually small models, but the matrix is enormous, so we're batching it into one reserved week: we hold the vulcan-h100 reservation, 512 accelerators, for the week of 2026-06-22. Ines flagged the cluster maintenance window ending 06-24, and has us starting Wednesday of that week at full 512 — the sweep fits in four days with margin since each job is tiny.

Everything pre-June runs titan-a100 best-effort.

MIMIC-II: blocked on the DUA per your note; sweep plan treats it as optional.

Jelena

subject: Re: NAM kickoff — library status + TF version risk
body:
Hi both,

Status:

- Library alpha shipped 03-27. Two internal teams are already importing it for prototyping.
- Benchmark reproduction: on the public datasets from gs://nam_datasets we match the paper's reported AUCs within 0.005 on 8 of 9 sets; the credit dataset needed the ExU feature-net variant to close the gap. Shape-function plots are in the library as a first-class API — that's the feature customers actually screenshot into their model-risk docs.
- Jorge's sweep harness is done and dress-rehearsed at 1/50th scale on titan.

Risk: the release code targets tensorflow>=1.15 via tf.compat.v1 in places, and our serving stack is TF2-only. The tf.keras.Model path is clean but the graph-mode helpers aren't. Recommendation: library v1 supports the tf.keras path only, and we document the compat helpers as unsupported. Affects one prospective customer whose pipeline is graph-mode; Oyin is checking whether they can move.

MIMIC-II DUA still with Legal.

Wanjiru

subject: Re: NAM kickoff — decisions before the sweep week
body:
Team,

Decisions from today's pre-sweep review:

1. TF2-only for v1, per Wanjiru's recommendation. The graph-mode compat helpers are documented as unsupported. The graph-mode prospect has agreed to test on the tf.keras path — Oyin owns that integration and it becomes our lighthouse customer readout.
2. MIMIC-II is cut from the June sweep. Kofi says the DUA countersignature won't land before the run, and I'm not holding 512 accelerators hostage to paperwork. If it clears in July we do a small follow-up run on titan; the tuned-defaults story stands on the 9 public datasets.
3. Sweep configs freeze 06-17. Jorge publishes the final matrix Monday; anything not in it waits for Q3.

Q3 OKR (filing before the 06-26 lock): tuned defaults published for 4 dataset families, 3 customer integrations live.

Dmitri

subject: Kickoff: neural-guided symbolic regression as a formula-discovery service
body:
Hi Bruno,

Kickoff for the symbolic regression effort. Base: our open-source release on neural-guided symbolic regression with asymptotic constraints — an expression-generating network that respects a formula's leading power at 0 and at infinity. Training set is 28,837 rational expressions with complexity M <= 4; the release also ships holdout sets at M=5 and M=6 specifically to test generalization beyond training complexity, plus metrics code for success rate, L1-distance, and syntactic/semantic novelty.

Product: data-platforms customers who want closed-form, auditable relationships out of tabular data instead of black-box regressors. Constraint-conditioning is our differentiator — analysts usually know the asymptotics even when they don't know the formula.

Milestones in our short window (04-13 to 06-29): training pipeline reproduced by mid-May, constraint-conditioning eval by mid-June, go/no-go readout 06-25.

Resourcing thoughts?

Dmitri

subject: Re: Kickoff: symbolic regression — resourcing
body:
Dmitri,

Resourcing:

Staffing — Tereza reproduces the expression-generating NN training (the models folder path), Yusuf owns the constraint-conditioning eval and the baseline comparisons against the empirical-distribution models, Leilani builds the service wrapper and the grammar tooling (we extend the univariate_one_constant_grammar production rules for customer feature vocabularies).

Compute — individual models are small but the June evaluation is a large matrix: beam widths x constraint settings x the three holdout tiers (M<=4, M=5, M=6), with enough sampled expressions per cell for the novelty metrics to be meaningful. We're consolidating that into our reserved slot: we hold the vulcan-h100 reservation, 256 accelerators, for the week of 2026-06-15, which runs the full eval matrix plus Tereza's retraining ablations in one pass. Before that, titan best-effort suffices.

Grammar tooling is the sleeper risk — customer vocabularies blow up the production-rule set fast. Leilani is prototyping caps.

Bruno

subject: Re: Kickoff: symbolic regression — status + generalization risk
body:
Hi both,

Status:

- Tereza hit the mid-May milestone: NN training reproduced end to end from train.tfrecords, eval on eval.csv (4,095 expressions) tracks the release's curves.
- Early constraint-conditioning numbers from Yusuf on the holdout tiers: with leading-power constraints supplied, success rate on holdout_m_leq_4 is strong and roughly doubles the unconstrained baseline. The story weakens with complexity: on holdout_m_5 (1,000 expressions) the constrained model still leads clearly, but on holdout_m_6 the gap narrows and absolute success is low for both. Semantic novelty stays healthy — we're not just memorizing training expressions.
- Service wrapper: grammar caps working; a 40-symbol customer vocabulary keeps generation tractable.

Risk for the readout: if customer formulas skew toward M=6-level complexity, v1 will underdeliver. Suggest we position v1 for M<=5-class problems explicitly and say so on the label.

Leilani

subject: Re: Kickoff: symbolic regression — go/no-go decision
body:
Team,

Go/no-go outcome from this morning, with last week's full eval matrix in hand:

GO, scoped. Decisions:

1. v1 ships as a formula-discovery service for M<=5-class problems, exactly per Leilani's framing. The M=6 tier results from the eval week confirmed the mid-May trend, so the product label says what the model can actually do. No heroics chasing M=6 this half.
2. Constraint input is required, not optional, in the v1 API. The unconstrained mode's numbers don't meet the quality bar, and making it required keeps the differentiator front and center.
3. Tereza's retraining ablation (larger training set with M<=5 expressions synthesized via the grammar) is the headline Q3 investment — it's the clearest path to lifting the ceiling.

Readout deck to Hana's staff going out tomorrow, inside the window. Well run, everyone — tight timeline, clean landing.

Dmitri

subject: NeuTra kickoff — fast posterior sampling for the Bayesian toolkit
body:
Hi Santiago,

Kickoff for NeuTra. The open-source release gives us neural-transport HMC: train an IAF bijector to warp away bad posterior geometry, then run HMC in the transformed space. The neutra_runner reproduces the flagship result on the 100-dimensional funnel target — a distribution plain HMC basically cannot traverse — with both IAF and affine baselines.

Product: a NeuTra preset inside the efficiency portfolio's Bayesian inference toolkit, so internal users stop hand-tuning step sizes on nasty posteriors. Deliverables: (1) runner productized with our config system, (2) benchmark suite (funnel + two internal calibration posteriors) with tuned defaults, (3) toolkit docs.

Milestones: runner ported by end of March, benchmarks by mid-May, toolkit release before window close 06-08. One dependency: the internal calibration posteriors come from datasets that are moving in the Corpus v2 migration, so let's get our data pulls sorted early.

Zofia

subject: Re: NeuTra kickoff — resourcing + Corpus timing
body:
Zofia,

Resourcing:

Staffing — Umar leads the benchmark methodology and tuning, Vera ports the runner, Tereza handles the toolkit integration and docs.

Compute — modest. The release itself notes it just wants a GPU with decent batch sizes; our whole benchmark plan fits on titan-a100 best-effort. No reservation needed, which is a nice change.

On the Corpus dependency: I checked the migration timeline — the Corpus v2 freeze lands 2026-07-24, so it sits comfortably past our 06-08 close and we can re-pull the calibration datasets any time during the project without racing the migration. I've told Tereza to schedule the final data refresh for late May, right before toolkit release, so we ship against the freshest pre-freeze snapshot.

Runner port is already underway; Vera says the hparams plumbing (the giant --hparams strings) is the ugliest part and she's mapping it onto our config system first.

Santiago

subject: Re: NeuTra kickoff — benchmark status + tuning risk
body:
Hi both,

Status:

- Vera's port landed 03-30. Config system mapping done; the funnel configs (IAF with 3 stages, [100, 100] hidden layers, vs the affine/tril baseline) reproduce cleanly.
- Funnel benchmark: NeuTra with the IAF bijector reaches target rhat on the 100-dim funnel in roughly a sixth of the wall-clock of tuned vanilla HMC on our A100s. The affine baseline splits the difference — worth keeping in the docs as the cheap option.
- Internal calibration posterior #1 shows the same shape of win. #2 in progress.

Risk: the step-size tuner. The release tunes within a min/max step-size band with a leapfrog cap of 100, and the rhat-based objective is sensitive to that band on our posterior #2 — badly set bounds either blow past the leapfrog cap or crawl.
